# The 2026-09-06 use-report round — 17o · 18c · 18d · 18e · 18f (EXECUTION PLAN, v2)

**STATUS: READY TO KICK OFF (v2, 2026-09-07 — solidified at her follow-up; v1 was the read-only draft
of the same night).** Runs NEXT, before 13u (her sequencing). **Run shape, her ruling:** a classic
`/architect-phase` — a **Fable orchestrator** that stays LEAN (briefs by pointer, repo-first records,

## 0. What this round is (one paragraph)

She spent an evening writing with takes and the app fought her three times in ten minutes: Return
stopped making blocks in the middle of a note (the chip said on; one block swallowed two paragraphs),
so she reached for divide; divide dragged every take onto both halves (the 13j default she ruled and
now reverses); and the ceremony she opened to keep the take on the first block could not park the
scissors at the end, arrived with the take unchecked, and looked "so ugly" that using it was work.
Around that core sit ~twenty smaller annoyances she listed as a punchlist, plus five design asks she
added the next night (the tray, the sidebar's note box, the ceremonies' names and presets, the bulk
"make every newline a block", the snippets editor). This round takes all of it, **grouped by kind and
by seam** into five letters run as one round: **18c** Return makes blocks (the typing model — her
biggest pain, first) · **18f** Divide choosing takes / Merge choosing takes (the ceremonies rebuilt to
the mockup) · **17o** the defects · **18d** the sidebar's note box, the tray, the outline's room · **18e**
markdown marks faded. Her line to keep in view: *"overall I have to emphasize that the app is looking
and feeling great after the various rounds of changes."*

## 1. Her rulings (2026-09-06 + 2026-09-07 — verbatim-faithful; SETTLED unless marked PROVISIONAL)

- **U-1 — NEWLINES MAKE BLOCKS, ANYWHERE IN WRITE.** *"newlines to make new blocks is NOT working
  properly at all"* … *"I was writing in Write, but in the middle of Write, so I had paragraphs above
  and below. I want it to work on newlines even when you're in the middle of write."* → Return makes a
  block wherever the caret is: at a block's end, a new block below; inside a block's text, a divide at
  the caret. Today's model only crystallizes at the note's END (§4.1). This is a typing-model change,
  built as **18c**.
- **U-2 — DIVIDE KEEPS THE TAKES ON THE TOP BLOCK.** *"I know I said that should be the default, but I
  honestly believe now that if you divide, the takes should automatically stay on the top block that
  you divided."* Supersedes the 13j J4 duplicate default on the Mac — and, her follow-up: **the phone
  flips too** (*"the phone divide should update to match this default divide behavior"*).
- **U-3 — THE CEREMONY OPENS WITH EVERY TAKE CHECKED AND THE ✂ AT THE END.** *"Takes should
  automatically be selected in the divide ceremony to come along with and should automatically have the
  scissors at the end."*
- **U-4 — THE NAMES.** *"'divide choosing takes' should replace 'divide ceremony', since it's clearer.
  same with merge - should be a button, not just a shortcut, and should say 'merge choosing takes'."*
- **U-5 — THREE PRESETS EASY, THE CUSTOM SELECTOR DELIBERATE.** *"the phone should offer three options
  (somehow, not sure how to not make it crowded): 1. all takes stay with the top block 2. all takes stay
  with the bottom block 3. all takes go on both. I think those options should feel easily available in
  the divide ceremony for ease and the custom selector should be something you really have to choose to
  do."* → The Mac's sheet gets the same first row (the mockup's figure A); the phone's face is its
  parity row.
- **U-6 — A "MAKE ALL NEWLINES BLOCKS" BUTTON.** *"that automatically just leaves any take at the top
  paragraph of its block (aka, if you had a multi paragraph block now the top paragraph is a block with
  all the takes)."* Her reason: fixing a note written with the chip off meant *"a lot of divides to run"*
  and, under the duplicate default, deleting an extra take between each.
- **U-7 — THE RING FOLLOWS THE PREFERENCE.** *"the take mode always shows a ring around what piece
  you're editing - it doesn't follow the preference on cursor being enough, wanting background wash, or
  ring."*
- **U-8 — THE TITLE LEADS.** *"it should be aligned to the left again so it starts where 'in no book' is,
  and it should be able to extend at least as far as the middle centered title can extend right now to
  support longer titles."* Supersedes Act 10 rows 4/19.
- **U-9 — THE TRAY: LEAVING vs ARCHIVED TOP-LEVEL, BLOCKS vs TAKES UNDER EACH.** *"you should be able to
  select if you want to see leaving, if you want to see blocks or takes under leaving, and separetly if
  you want to see archived (archived v. leaving should be top level, with block or takes as a filter
  under each one."* (Mockup figure D.)
- **U-10 — THE SIDEBAR'S NOTE BOX.** *"The block menu should move to being where the 'this note, write,
  lenses, compare, etc.' menu is, measured to take up the same amount of room, and should show 'no note
  selected' when you haven't clicked into anything or you've clicked out of something."* … *"I want the
  note box with the block menu and other information to be well designed and useful and it's more of a
  new area."* (Mockup figure C; the design §5.4.)
- **U-11 — MARKDOWN MARKS OUT OF SIGHT, FADE FIRST.** *"I want markdown items to disappear unless you're
  at the edge editing them or turn seeing them back on"* … *"I think fading them is a good start I
  suppose."* → FADE is the first form (18e); collapse is the recorded follow-on (§5.5 explains both).
- **U-12 — REMEMBERED NOTE LENGTHS.** *"I see no reason why we wouldn't add in remembering the length of
  notes so it can be perfect after the first time."*
- **U-13 — THE OUTLINE'S ROOM.** *"the chapters feel too tightly clustered and the panel with the chapter
  names should also be draggable to be a bit bigger"* · *"table of contents in read mode for a note is
  horizontally limited and not changable, should be adjustable."*
- **U-14 — THE RUN SHAPE.** *"I will be letting a Fable orchestrator run this and I want Opus to fix the
  defects and handle the coding"* · *"I want to use a classic /architect-phase style of running this, I
  don't want the orchestrator's context window to become bloated and I don't need the orchestrator to
  verify everything"* · on the snippets editor: *"only opus to fix this item."*
- **U-16 — MERGING SEVERAL BLOCKS: TWO CHOICES, NO CEREMONY (2026-09-07, at the mockup approval).** *"if
  you're merging several notes together you should be given the choice of bringing every take or only the
  currently shown ones, but i don't want a super complex ceremony for merging multiple blocks together."*
  → A merge over a run of THREE OR MORE blocks offers exactly two options — Bring every take · Only the
  shown ones — and never the pairing surface (§5.2). The mockups (figures A–D) are APPROVED with this one
  amendment: *"I like your mockups, I approve of them."*
- **U-17 — THE BOOK'S RIGHT GUTTER RETIRES ENTIRELY** once the bar moves into the sidebar box (her answer to
  the open question; the unfocused rows' facts line goes with it — state 2 of the box carries the facts).
- **U-18 — FADED MARKS ARE FAINT, NEVER PAPER-COLORED.** *"i think the fade will look weird if they're 100%
  the color of the paper because the spacing will look odd, so maybe just render them faintly, at a grey or
  lower opacity or something."* → outside the caret's span the markers render in the marker color at a low
  opacity (a faint grey), inside it at full; never invisible.
- **U-19 — THE LAST FIVE, ANSWERED (2026-09-07, the third message; EVERYTHING IS NOW SETTLED):** (1) versions
  on a blockless note — *"a is good"* → mint the empty first block and link at once; (2) Return's empty block —
  *"a, the eager deleting of whitespace has already been an annoyance and we won't reintroduce it with
  paragraphs disappearing"* → an abandoned empty block STAYS as an empty paragraph, never auto-removed;
  (3) *"shift return is good for a blank line within a paragraph, and users can also turn off newlines make
  blocks if they want, right?"* → yes: the chip OFF (`one_block` for that note) makes Return content again,
  as today; the k−1 typed-blank-line rule narrows to ⇧⏎; (4) lists stay whole under "make every newline a
  block" — *"confirmed"*; (5) the ring preference governs every live pane — *"confirmed"*.
- **U-20 — EVERY DOOR INTO WRITE LANDS AT THE CARET, NOT THE BLOCK'S START (2026-09-07, the third message).**
  *"when you are within a block and then click go to write, you also end up with your caret at the start of
  the block rather than where you were within it, which is annoying on long blocks."* → Row 42; the same
  mechanism as row 7 (the current-block memory carries no offset), the same additive fix, in 17o batch b.
  Her condition — tell her if it is hard or disturbs scrolling/layout — is answered in that row: it is not.
- **U-15 — THE PUNCHLIST** (rows 6–33 of the ledger, her words there) and the follow-up's small ones:
  the tag field collapses after use (*"if there's a tag already applied this new tag template shouldn't
  just sit here by default, it should collapse after you click out of it"*); the divider's white top
  (*"the line that separates the left pane from the main editor is white for just a tiny bit at the
  top"*); the header/highlight crowding (*"the highlight on the mode you're in and the words 'this note'
  or 'open' is very close to touching and the items in that pane should all be aligned"*); the snippets
  editor (*"it just opens a whole note with several different snippets but not even the snippet that i
  right clicked on"* … *"you can't tag snippets but there's a tag on there"*).

## 2. Where this sits — numbering, sequencing, the 13u fence

> **Read §2 with this correction (added at the round's close):** the round ran as **FOUR** letters — **18e was HELD at her word on 2026-09-08** (§5.5 carries her ruling verbatim and her markdown-mode contemplation). Everything else below stands as written and as run.

- **Five letters, why.** CLAUDE.md's rule splits fixes (17) from product (18) — her R-cor-13. The
  typing model (18c), the ceremonies (18f), the sidebar box + tray + room (18d) and the markdown setting
  (18e) change what the app IS; the rest are defects (17o). Letters are allocation order. **Running order:
  18c → 18f → 17o → 18d → 18e** — her two named pains first; 18e is the most separable (she may hold it).
- **Sizing (`notes/PhaseSizingGuidance.md`), stated:** 18c is one phase-sized unit (the typing model)
  plus a composition and a bulk op; 18f one (the sheet rebuilt) plus naming; 17o ~24 defect rows in
  four one-surface batches; 18d two phase-sized units under one theme (the box; the room + memory) plus
  the tray — AT the line; 18e one. One implementer session per batch; a session that finds a second unit
  hands off with a record.
- **Precedents:** the Act 10 correction round (her report answered row by row; one surface per session)
  and the 13j fanned-defaults batch (a default changed by COMPOSING an existing op — 18c repeats it).
- **THE 13u FENCE — what this round deliberately does NOT take** (read the master plan's `### 13u`
  section and `notes/plans/phase-13u-feel-and-polish.md`'s fold + addenda before touching the seam):
  - **Cross-block delete (image 8)** — 13u1 item 5, ruled and fenced; she said so herself. Nothing here
    touches `CrossBlockEditPlanner`, the refusal grammar, or the fanned matrix.
  - **The O(N²) family, the churn pair, the arm-then-hand-off residual** — 13u1's. 18c's Return road is
    an INTERCEPT at the key (like ⇧⏎'s), deliberately NOT a rewrite of `BlockRangeIndex`'s tiling (§5.1
    says why); if a session finds it must change the index's regions, it stops and records.
  - **Pane stability (13u2 item 1)** — the general trace stays 13u2's; two named members are built here
    (rows 16 · 25).
  - **The title cut-off (13u2 item 13 + row 93)** — row 11's fix very likely satisfies it; the 13u2 kickoff
    decides; this round records what it changed.
  - **P39b** (`WriteTakesPanel` constructing `TakesViewModel`) — 13u2's; 18d's composition adds no sibling
    violation (§5.4 says how).

## 4. The traces (the architect's read — by reading, never by running; the pin decides)

### 4.1 Row 1 — why Return stopped making blocks, and why the fix is a model change

**The designed gesture.** Type-time crystallization only ever plans over the OPEN TAIL — text after the
LAST block (`CrystallizationPlanner.swift`; `SegmentationRules.crystallizedBoundary`). The tail opens by
one gesture: a single newline typed at the exact UTF-16 document end while no tail exists
(`BlockRangeIndex.verdict` → `.openTail`, `BlockRangeIndex.swift:144–152`; the ratified Phase 7 gesture,
re-pinned at 13d A15, `ReturnKeyTraceTests` (b)). **Every other newline — including Return at the end of
block 2 of 3, or inside any block — is I4 content of the block it lands in.** So in the middle of a note
the chip's promise ("each finished paragraph becomes its own block as you type past it") was never true:
the machinery has no position but the end. That is her scenario exactly (*"paragraphs above and
below"*), and it is not a bug in the tail road — it is the tail road's scope.

**At the very end, a second trap (kept for the record; moot once 18c lands, the fallback fix if 18c is
ever deferred):** an EMPTY open tail lingers after one Return and a pause (the idle mint plans nothing
over ""; nothing closes an empty tail but deleting its separator, `:154–158`), or the last block ends with
a content newline (the k−1 rule, `attachLeadingTailRunIfNeeded`, `EditorViewModel.swift:1306–1338`). Either
way the last visible line is blank, a click at the end of the text lands the caret BEFORE that last
character, and Return there is content — image 4's "several new lines". The narrow fix (F1): recognize
the EFFECTIVE end (`lastEnd` with an empty tail open → move the caret into the tail, no bytes change; inside
a trailing newline run → the run's last newline becomes the separator, bytes unchanged). Pins for it are
written in v1's record (this file's git history, `a45ee0cc`).

**The model change (U-1), in one sentence:** with the chip ON, **Return makes a block wherever the caret
is** — at a block's end, a new block below (the shipped New Block Below, ⌘⇧⏎, `insertBlockBelowCaret`,
`EditorSurfaceController.swift:667–683`, on the plain key); inside a block's text, a divide at the caret
(the shipped `divideAtCursor`; single-take in place, fanned → the keep-on-top default); Shift-Return stays
the content newline (13d A15, `SoftNewlineTests`); with the chip OFF (`one_block`) Return stays content.
Built as an INTERCEPT at the key in `EditorTextView` (the `isSoftNewlineKey` precedent: decide before the
gate, route to the structural door or fall through), so `BlockRangeIndex`'s tiling is untouched — the 13u1
fence holds. Consequences and options are §5.1.

### 4.2 Rows 7 · 8 · 20 — the landing family (one memory, three doors, no offset, no scroll)

`CommandRouter.focusedBlock` is the ONE current block across modes (Act 10 batch C, row 39); its memory
is `CurrentBlockMemory` (`"blockID|variantID"`, `:44`). Three roads read it and each stops one step short:
Takes → Write lands at the block's START (`bareArrivalLanding`, `EditorViewModel.swift:1729–1734`) because
the fact has no caret offset; Blocks → Write (`applyWriteIntent`, `:1743+`) computes the offset, sets the
selection and (verify) does not scroll — and the arrival road's `scrollRangeToVisible` (`:1705`) lands short
on TK2 before layout (TEXTKIT2 §2; `JumpPrimitive.jump(toOffset:textView:scrollView:)`,
`JumpPrimitive.swift:94–140`, is the Phase 6 hybrid jump built for exactly this); the fan panel → Takes
landing blooms and focuses (`TakesChoreographer.swift:159–176`) and the article column has no scroll-to at
all. **One fix:** `FocusedBlock` gains `utf16Offset: Int?` (reported by Write's caret context,
`EditorViewModel.swift:2544`, and by the live pane's selection, `TakesViewModel.swift:521`; persisted as a
third field — old memories read as nil → the block start); every landing consumes it: Write lands at
`range.location + min(offset, length)` and reveals through `JumpPrimitive` (with the arrival's next-turn
retry); the board's article gains a `ScrollViewReader`/`scrollPosition(id:)` over its slots and scrolls
the landed slot to the top band once per landing (the typewriter room already exists, `:582`).
`LandingTarget.utf16Offset` is the same idea one door over — reuse the name.

### 4.3 Rows 18 · 19 — chrome titles are one-shot reads

`PostTitleLabel` reads once per note (`.task(id: postID)`, `PostDetailView.swift:646–657`);
`WorkspaceModel.resolveTitles` once per change of the SUBJECT SET (`titleSubjectsKey`,
`WorkspaceModel.swift:382`; the trigger `SidebarView.swift:259`). Neither watches the rows, so a rename or a
date change shows only where the write happened. **One fix:** a bounded `ValueObservation` over the
`container` rows in question (title · entry_date · created_at — `DisplayTitle.note`'s three inputs): the
open set for the strip, the one note for the masthead — a sync pull's rename lands too. Cost ∝ open notes.

### 4.4 Row 3 — the scissors and the end slot

By design the end is placeable (`legalCutPositions` = `BoundarySnapping.boundaries(.word)` "ends
included", `DivideWCeremony.swift:226–234`; `flowItems` ends `.slot(end)`; `wordStep(forward:)` stays at
`boundaries.last`). Pin, in order: (i) `legalCutPositions(of: "Alpha beta.")` contains 11; (ii)
`CutFlowGeometry.make` lays the end slot INSIDE `geometry.size` — `size.width = min(widest, width)`
(`CutFlowGeometry.swift:105`) can clip a slot when the LAST line is the widest, and the flow is framed to
`geometry.size` (`DivideWSheet.swift:329`); her screenshot shows the ✂ one slot short — (ii)'s picture;
(iii) `nearestSlot(to:)` resolves a point right of the last token to the end. If all pass, the fault is
`WCutFlow`'s gesture wiring (`:347–356`). 18f's rebuilt face lands the ✂ by character hit-testing, but the
pure brains keep their pins.

### 4.5 Row 38 — the snippets editor opens the wrong pool

`BlocksAreaView.cardMenu` (`:508–510`): `Button(SnippetsCopy.openRow) { if let pool = area.activePool {
openPool(pool.id) } }` — the ACTIVE group, not the card's `item.poolID`; and `openHere(.pool(id))`
(`RootView.swift:671`) lands nowhere in particular. Browsing "all groups", the active pool is the default
"Snippets" pool; her snippet lives in the tutorial's own pool ("tutorial scraps", `TutorialSeeder.swift:41`).
**Fix:** `openPool(item.poolID)` + a landing on `item.block.blockID` (a `WriteIntent`/`LandingTarget`
into the pool editor — the Blocks → Write road, which row 20 fixes to scroll). The header's "open as
editor" keeps the active group. Pin: opening from a card in group B while group A is active opens B with
the caret in the clicked block.

## 5. The five letters

### 5.1 — 18c · Return makes blocks (the typing model; U-1 · U-2 · U-6)

**Goal.** With the chip on, every Return makes a block, wherever the caret is; the fanned-divide default
keeps the takes on top on both platforms; a note written with the chip off is repaired by one command.

**Batch 1 — the keep-on-top composition (zero core change) + the phone's flip.**
- `KeepOnTopDivide.compose(displayedID:cut:fan:) -> [String: Int]?` in `App/Variorum/Shared/` beside
  `CarryAllMerge` (`FannedDefaults.swift:38` — the pattern): the displayed take's cut = the gesture's
  snapped position (`BoundarySnapping`, S4-22 unchanged); **every other live ACTIVE take's cut = its
  text's UTF-16 length — parked at the END**, which by S4-22 ruling 2 rides that take whole into the FIRST
  block. Handed to `Operations.divideW(blockID, cuts:)` (`Operations+Structural.swift:320`). Result: B's fan
  = the displayed take's first half (chosen — the per-side rendered rule, `:~403`) + every other take
  whole; C's fan = the displayed take's second half (chosen); A released to lineage preserved whole
  (reversible, ⌥⌘Z). **Edges the composition speaks:** an EMPTY other take cannot park (`legalCutPositions`
  = []; `divideW` refuses `invalidCut`) → left unmarked, it stays on A in lineage, counted in the receipt;
  the displayed take's cut at its own start/end refuses as today; the F-3 guard → `takesChangedDivide`. A
  sibling `compose(keepBelow:)` (every other take parked at its START — U-5's second preset) lands with
  it; the third preset IS `divideDuplicating`.
- The Mac's fanned-divide sites (`EditorSurfaceController.swift:419–500`, `TakesStructureController.swift:437`)
  call the composition instead of `divideDuplicating`; the receipt (`FannedDefaultsCopy.divided`, the J8
  copy-truth pin): *"Block divided — the take you were in split across both blocks; N other takes stayed
  on the first. ⌥⌘Z undoes."*
- **The phone flips in the same batch (U-2, her follow-up):** `MobileEditorViewModel`'s fanned-divide door
  (the parity-chain Stage A site; `grep -n divideDuplicating App/Variorum/VariorumMobile`) calls the shared
  composition; its pin and the iOS suite green. The phone's three-preset FACE is 18f's parity row.
- **Canon delta drafted for the closeout:** AppSpec §9's `divideDuplicating` paragraph gains the 2026-09-06
  supersession — the default on BOTH platforms is keep-on-top; `divideDuplicating` stays in core as the
  "copy takes to both" preset; `FannedDefaults.swift`'s header updated. Pins: the composition's matrix
  (2/3/5 takes, an empty other take, a locked other take); instant default == ceremony-unchanged on a
  three-take block (18f's pin, shared).

**Batch 2 — Return makes a block, anywhere (the intercept).**
- **The rule (chip ON — `header.effectiveSegmentation != .oneBlock`):** Return with the caret **at the END
  of a block's text** (trailing whitespace ignored; any block, last included) → `insertBlockBelowCaret`'s
  shape (an empty block after it, the caret in it — the shipped ⌘⇧⏎ road, `EditorSurfaceController.swift:667–683`,
  through `runStructural`: one flight, flush first, store-led rewrite, caret by identity). Return **INSIDE
  a block's text** → `divideAtCursor` at the caret through the one snapping rule (single-take: in place, A
  keeps identity; fanned: the keep-on-top composition; the caret lands at the START of the second block —
  "the paragraph I just started"). Return **at the START of a block** (before any text) → an empty block
  ABOVE it, caret staying in the text block (the everyday "push this paragraph down") — or refuse; the
  implementer picks the first unless the seam argues. Return **in an EMPTY block** → nothing happens (never
  a second empty block; recorded, not spoken). Return **inside an open tail** (a tail exists only after a
  paste/drop now) → the tail's own road, unchanged. **⇧⏎ → content, always** (A15). **Chip OFF → content**
  (today). A sealed note → the structural door's own refusal, spoken.
- **Where:** an intercept in `EditorTextView` on the Return key BEFORE `insertNewline:` reaches the gate
  (the `isSoftNewlineKey` precedent — `EditorTextView.swift`, the soft-newline flag), deciding from the
  caret's block and offset (`model.caretBlockID` / the index's entry range) and dispatching to the
  structural doors; `BlockRangeIndex.verdict`'s `.openTail` arm stays for pasted tails and is otherwise
  unreachable from typing. **Do not rewrite the index's regions** (the 13u1 fence). The MarkdownActs Return
  intercept (`.continueList`, `MarkdownActs.swift:388` — list continuation) runs FIRST and keeps its
  behavior: inside a list, Return continues the list; a second Return on an empty item ends the list AND
  makes the block (the two intercepts compose in that order; pin it).
- **The empty block — RULED (U-19 (2)):** a Return she then abandons leaves an empty block, and **it
  STAYS** — an empty paragraph, as in every editor; seam-backspace removes it (the A7 carve,
  `deleteBlock(requiring: .emptyWithNothingUnshown)`); Blocks/Index show it as "(empty block)". **Never
  auto-removed** — her words: *"the eager deleting of whitespace has already been an annoyance and we
  won't reintroduce it with paragraphs disappearing."* No quiet-removal follow-on; never a positional open
  gap in the index (seam surgery, 13u1's).
- **The k−1 spacing rule (QUESTIONS #12, 2026-07-12) narrows — RATIFIED (U-19 (3)):** typed newline runs no
  longer reach the tail, so a blank line INSIDE a paragraph is ⇧⏎ (⇧⏎ twice for a blank line); pasted runs
  keep the rule unchanged; the chip OFF returns the whole note to Return-as-content. The closeout records
  the supersession in AppSpec §7's segmentation-trigger paragraph and beside #12.
- **Pins that must go RED on old and green after** (`ReturnKeyTraceTests`' real-key harness): (1) seed
  `["alpha","beta","gamma"]`, caret at the end of "beta", ⏎, type "new" → `["alpha","beta","new","gamma"]`
  (the middle case — her scenario); (2) caret inside "beta" after "be", ⏎ → `["alpha","be","ta","gamma"]`
  with the caret at "ta"'s start; (3) a fanned middle block, ⏎ inside its displayed take → keep-on-top
  (B carries the others whole); (4) ⏎ at the end of the LAST block → a new block, no open tail
  (`!hasOpenTail`); (5) ⏎ in an empty block → no change; (6) ⇧⏎ mid-block → content (A15's pin stays
  green); (7) `one_block` → content; (8) a list item's ⏎ → continues the list; (9) her S1 scenario (⏎,
  pause 2 s, click at the end of the last line, ⏎, type) → a new block every time. **Pins that the ruling
  RETIRES, named and cited, never silently:** `ReturnKeyTraceTests` (b) "⏎ opens the tail at the document
  end" and B2's tail-from-typing setup (rebuilt over a pasted tail); any `EditorSessionTests` /
  `CrystallizationTests` case whose premise is a TYPED tail (the planner's pure tests over bulk/idle stay).
  The implementer lists every retired pin in the batch record with the ruling beside it.
- **Evidence:** her scenario walked on the dev store by the implementer (write, ⏎ in the middle, type;
  ⏎ at the end; ⇧⏎; a list), captured to `…-screens/18c-2/`; the bar reading "block k/N" honestly (row 28).
- **Review: Fable** (the editor seam). **Implementer: Opus**, per her cast — the brief RESTATES the seam
  rules (the identity oracle runs per keystroke in DEBUG and kills the process on identity corruption; the
  macOS-26 widening rule for any attribute stamp; `runStructural` is the ONE structural door; the
  intercept never touches `BlockRangeIndex`).

**Batch 3 — "Make every newline a block" (U-6).**
- **Core op `splitBlockAtNewlines(blockID)`** in `Operations+Structural.swift`, ONE transaction per block
  (atomic; a pin per shape): find the break points in the block's DISPLAYED take (the chosen; `Queries`
  gives it); **breaks = newline runs**, with ONE exception — a run of exactly one newline between two
  LIST-LEAD lines (`MarkdownSyntax.isListLead`) is not a break, so lists stay whole (PROVISIONAL; her
  ratify list); each piece edge-trimmed by `SegmentationRules.trimmedPiece` (the K8 law: a list lead keeps
  its indent). **Single-take block:** successive in-place `divide`s at each break (A keeps identity as the
  first paragraph). **Fanned block:** the first break is a keep-on-top `divideW` (the displayed take cut
  there, every other take parked at the end) → B = paragraph 1 + every other take whole (*"the top
  paragraph is a block with all the takes"* — her words exactly), C = the rest as one take; then C splits in
  place at the remaining breaks. Blank lines vanish into separators (they were content; the separator
  renders the paragraph break). A block with no break is a no-op (no touch, no churn). Sealed → refuses.
  Registers ONE structural undo entry per block with the exact-row redo (the 13c rule: `register(redo:)`
  is required, never defaulted).
- **Doors:** the note ▾ menu — **"Make every newline a block"** (all blocks, one `withCompound` — one ⌥⌘Z,
  `UndoStack.swift:190`); the block ▾ menu — **"Split this block at its newlines"**; the Blocks workbench's
  bulk bar gets the same verb for a selection (the 13e multi-select). Receipt: *"12 blocks from 3 — every
  take stayed with its top paragraph. ⌥⌘Z undoes."* (counts from the op's own result — the 13e rule).
- **Pins:** the break rule (runs; the list exception; trailing/leading whitespace); single-take 3-paragraph
  → 3 blocks in order, A's identity kept; fanned (3 takes, 3 paragraphs) → B holds [p1, t2, t3] with p1
  chosen, then p2, p3 single; the compound's one undo restores every row; sealed refuses; sync: ordinary
  ops (no `Sync/` change).
- **Review: Fable** (core structural op). Implementer Opus.

### 5.2 — 18f · Divide choosing takes · Merge choosing takes (U-3 · U-4 · U-5; mockup figures A/B)

**Her verdict on today's sheet, verbatim:** *"so ugly with the spacing between the words, the way that
you have to scroll to get the different takes, just overall"* … *"I want there to be a pretty good plan for
how it can look better because I was just displeased with it."* The mockup IS the plan for how it looks;
this section is what it does.

**Batch 1 — the mechanics: names, doors, defaults, presets, the end slot.**
- **Names (U-4):** the verbs become **"Divide choosing takes…"** (`CapabilityRegistry.swift:186`) and
  **"Merge choosing takes…"** (`:214`); the sheet titles follow (`DivideWSheet.swift:66`,
  `MergeCeremonySheet.swift:48`); the tutorial lesson and the helper (`TutorialSeeder.swift:688`,
  `HelperView.swift:300`) and `FannedDefaultsCopy`'s sentences re-word; the word "ceremony" leaves every
  UI string (the code's type names may keep it). The field guide's changed lesson is her one restore act
  at the end (the standing handoff item).
- **Doors:** "Merge choosing takes…" becomes a BUTTON beside Merge — the block ▾ menu (`CommitBar.swift:492–507`),
  the Takes board's ⌘-click selection bar, the Blocks workbench's bulk bar; ⌥⌘⇧M stays. The same for
  "Divide choosing takes…" beside Divide.
- **The arrangement row (U-5) — the sheet's FIRST control, four options in this order:** **Keep takes on
  the top block** (selected on open — the default the instant divide uses) · **Keep takes on the bottom
  block** · **Copy takes to both** · **Choose per take…**. Choosing a preset places every ✂ (top: seed at
  the gesture, others at the END; bottom: others at the START; both: the duplicate shape — the sheet
  confirms through `divideDuplicating`, not `divideW`); the one sentence under the row says what will
  happen in counts (*"The take you were in splits at the ✂. 2 other takes stay whole on the top block; the
  bottom block starts with one take."*). **Confirming the sheet unchanged reproduces the instant default
  byte-for-byte** (pin). "Choose per take…" reveals the checklist — every take CHECKED, non-seed ✂ at the
  end (U-3) — with today's whole vocabulary (parking at both ends, ⇥ between takes, ←/→ and ⌥←/→,
  the confirm blocker) on the new surface; `CutPropagation`'s proposal survives as the ⌥←/→ strong step,
  never the default position. `DivideWCeremony.State` (`:177–215`) gains the preset + seeds all marked.
- **The merge sheet's row:** **Bring every take** (selected — the carry-all default) · **Only the two
  shown** (plain pair; the others stay in lineage) · **Pair by hand…** (the shipped S4-23 pairing UI).
  **Over a run of THREE OR MORE blocks (U-16):** the same door shows TWO options only — **Bring every
  take** (the shipped carry-all chain, `CarryAllMerge` link by link) · **Only the shown ones** (the plain
  `merge` chain, every other take left with its released block in lineage) — and no "Pair by hand"; the
  standing `mergeCeremonyIsPairwise` refusal (`FannedDefaultsCopy`) retires in favor of this two-option
  sheet. The sentence under the row counts what comes along. Pins: the run's two roads produce the
  carry-all chain's rows and the plain chain's rows respectively; the pairing surface never mounts for
  a run.
- **The end slot (row 3):** §4.4's pins in order; fix the link that reds.
- **The phone's parity row (write it into `notes/MobileSoul.md` at the close):** the phone's fanned divide
  offers the three presets as a bottom sheet of three plain rows in the same words, with "Choose per
  take…" as a fourth, quieter row — her note *"not sure how to not make it crowded"* answered by ONE
  sheet, no inline controls; the phone never gets the hand-placement surface (her 2026-08-03 mobile-gate
  rule: the ceremonies need no mobile replication). Built at the mobile catch-up, not here.
- **Review: Fable.** Implementer Opus.

**Batch 2 — the FACE, built to mockup figure A (and B's header).**
- **Real prose, natural spacing.** Each take renders as prose in the voice's body face (`tokens.body`), no
  inter-word slots; the ✂ is an overlay glyph on the inter-word gap at the cut — the layout never moves
  when it does (the L1 lesson kept by overlaying instead of occupying). Pointer placement by character
  hit-testing on the rendered take (a read-cheap TK2 surface's `characterIndex(for:)`, or the flow geometry

**Batch 1 — THE SIDEBAR'S NOTE BOX (her "new area"; mockup figure C — the binding shape).**

### 5.5 — 18e · markdown marks faded (U-11)

> **HELD OUT OF THE ROUND — her ruling 2026-09-08 (verbatim, in chat to the successor orchestrator):** *"honestly, I know that I said earlier to do 18e this phase, but honestly I don't want it done now. there's other items that are at a higher priority and I'll reconsider the markdown marks issue later - you can record in the 18e phase that I'm contemplating if even *markdown mode* should be on or off, and if it's off yoou don't use markdown to format but you can use the native formatting tools like bolding and such. i like the clean look that google docs and apple notes have, for example, but i did like the idea of markdown formatting. you can record the ideas in 18e but it's not high enough priority to happen for a while."* **What a future 18e kickoff reads first:** the open question is now upstream of fade vs collapse — whether a MARKDOWN MODE exists as a switch at all; OFF would mean no markdown formatting, with native formatting tools (bold and the like) in its place; her references are the clean look of Google Docs and Apple Notes; she still likes the idea of markdown formatting. If markdown stays, the fade (U-11/U-18, below) remains the recorded first form. Nothing here was built; R-14 (the pre-drafted brief) was not appended — it is KEPT, not deleted with the round's scaffolding, at `notes/plans/held-18e-markdown-marks-brief.md` (the successor's J47, 2026-09-09: a future 18e kickoff starts from her contemplation above and that brief's pointers, which will have drifted).


**Her lean, verbatim:** *"I think fading them is a good start I suppose."* **Ruled first form: FADE — and
FAINT, never paper-colored (U-18):** outside the caret's span the markers render in the marker color at a
low opacity (start at ~35 %; the implementer tunes by eye in both voices and both appearances, and
records the number), inside the span at full. Her reason: an invisible mark leaves spacing that "will look
odd"; a faint one reads as a deliberate whisper.

**What the two forms are (her question, answered here so the record holds it):** today
`MarkdownFaceCore.restyle` colors every span's markers in the muted marker color on the storage
(`:183–194`) — the `**`, `_`, `~~`, backticks and link brackets are always visible. **FADE:** the markers
render in the paper color (invisible against the page, or at a whisper of alpha) everywhere EXCEPT the span
the caret is in or the selection touches, where they show in the marker color — you see `**bold**` at full strength only while you are inside it. Nothing moves: the marks still take their width, faint but present (U-18 — never paper-colored); caret math, identity ranges, the widening rule are all untouched; TK2-safe;
cost ∝ the edit plus two lines on a caret move. **COLLAPSE:** the markers take NO width outside the caret's
span (a zero-advance font or negative kern), so `**bold**` reads as `bold` with no gap — and the width
comes BACK when the caret enters the span, so the text after it shifts right by the marks' width as you
arrive and left as you leave. That is the "view jumps when text attributes update" class TEXTKIT2 §3
records, and it puts the caret beside a mark that is re-expanding under it. Identity is still untouched
(attributes only), but the geometry moves under her hands. Fade first; collapse a follow-on if the gaps
annoy her after living with fade. True concealment through content-storage element rewriting is out
(custom `NSTextElement`s assert).

**Build:** the reveal rule is a pure function (caret/selection range × the line's spans → the marker
ranges to SHOW) in `MarkdownFaceCore` — both platforms get the brain; `restyle` takes the caret range and
the setting; a caret move restyles the old and new caret lines only. **The setting:** `markdown_marks` ∈
{`shown`, `hidden`} in the `setting` table (enum, no prose — the 14b column promise; synced like every
document setting); faces in Settings ▸ Editor and the editor's `Aa` menu; default `shown`. The read tiers
unchanged (they already hide). The tutorial's formatting lesson gains one sentence; the phone's face is a
mobile row. **Pins:** the pure reveal rule; `restyle` with a caret range → the caret span's markers in the
marker color, every other span's in the paper color; a caret-move test restyles exactly two lines; the
setting round-trips; the read tiers' pins unchanged; the phone's suite untouched. **Evidence:** type
`**bold**`, move away — the asterisks fade; click back inside — they return; toggle the setting.
**Review: Fable** (editor seam). Implementer Opus.

## 8. Process (binding on every batch)

- **The correction round's C-1…C-7 bind by reference** (`notes/plans/act10-correction-round.md` §2b) —
  **with ONE amendment, hers (U-14):** C-2's second half ("the orchestrator walks the same rows hands-on")
  is replaced by *the implementer walks and captures; the orchestrator verifies by record and capture,
  spot-checks only where thin; the author walks once at the end.* C-3 stands: no install refresh without
  that final walk.
- **The standing-17 rules** (`phase-17-standing-fixes.md`): pin before fix; measure before believing a
  number; no product invention; schema commits alone.
- **The cast's effort levels (her ruling, 2026-09-07 — the definitions live in `.claude/agents/`):**
  `opus-implementer` = Opus at xhigh; `fable-reviewer` = Fable at xhigh; `opus-reviewer` = Opus at xhigh;
  the orchestrator session itself runs at high, and any bare spawn follows the session (a Fable
  implementer, when a future round wants one, is spawned bare and so runs at the orchestrator's high —
  her "let it follow the orchestrator level"). The frontmatter `effort` key overrides the session setting
  (Claude Code's subagents documentation, checked 2026-09-07).
- **The lean orchestrator:** briefs by pointer (file:line from this plan), never whole-file reads; records
  appended here per batch (brief → record → dispositions); the ladder's findings and dispositions here;
  a handoff to a successor orchestrator at ~500k tokens (`notes/SessionResiliencyProtocol.md` — the
  recovery half is the orchestrator's; implementer briefs restate the checkpoint half).
- **Session resiliency** binds every session; **no commit trailer** lines; **walk tooling** on the
  dev-store Debug build only; captures per batch under `…-screens/<letter-batch>/`.
- **The install refresh** follows the round's last walk, at a zero-instance window, the A1 backup first.

## Records

### R-0 · The constitution (copied verbatim from `.claude/skills/architect-phase/SKILL.md`, which preserves it byte-verbatim from `notes/plans/phase-13b-make-it-work.md`; BINDING on every batch of this round)

#### The architectural rules (the 13b constitution, P-1…P-9 — PRESERVED BYTE-VERBATIM from `notes/plans/phase-13b-make-it-work.md`; phase-specific names inside them — D3/D4, Stage 0/1, `TakesViewModel` — are the rules' provenance and worked examples, kept as written; the rules themselves are general and BINDING in every phase this skill runs)

- **P-1 — One capability registry.** Every user-facing act is declared
  exactly once: verb, scope (block/take/post/book), per-mode availability
  rule, its doors (menu / context / bar / shortcut / palette), and its
  refusal copy. Surfaces render their doors FROM the registry; gating is
  data, never per-view if-statements. A registry-walk test asserts every
  declared door exists and every rendered door is declared. This kills the
  D3/D4 class structurally — the capability matrix stays green by
  construction instead of by audit.
- **P-2 — Fire-and-DO (R115).** A rendered door either performs the act —
  including any mode-switch choreography, done visibly for the user — or
  delivers the operations layer's real refusal. A door that can never act in
  its context isn't rendered. Lecture-and-redirect is retired.
- **P-3 — One text surface, one liveness authority.** ONE TK2 surface
  component (live + read modes; one measurement brain — the width-gated
  remeasure; the shared canary) that every pane composes; the live editor
  core's identity machinery (`BlockRangeIndex`, crystallization) becomes its
  live mode, not a sibling implementation. "What text does this pane show,
  and is it live" is answered by ONE pure, unit-tested authority
  (`PaneTextAuthority`); views never re-derive it. Its invariants stated as
  code: exactly one live pane; the live pane is buffer-authoritative; read
  panes are projection-authoritative once caught up.
- **P-4 — Broadcasts carry signals, never decisions.** NotificationCenter
  may announce that something happened (mode changed, post opened); no
  listener derives business state or availability from a broadcast, and no
  flow's correctness depends on broadcast ordering. Cross-feature flows
  route through composition. (Stage 0's survey enumerates today's
  notification bus; Stage 1 disciplines it.)
- **P-5 — The friction doctrine (R116).** Repeated pushback against a rule
  marks an under-architected feature. The response is never another patch:
  write the feature's DESIGN MEMO — intended behavior whole, edge cases
  enumerated on paper, refusal wordings, undo story — get the author's
  rulings on the product-flavored edges, then build to the memo. Happy path
  ships first, but the edges are *decided at design time*, not discovered by
  the author. First two memos owed: **merge** and **the W ceremony**.
- **P-6 — The tutorial is the executable spec (R113).** The guided tutorial
  flow is the contract for every happy path. It stays green — automated
  where the harness allows, screenshot-walked otherwise — and any change
  that breaks a tutorial step is a regression by definition.
- **P-7 — Find bugs before she does.** Every layer keeps a proactive
  harness: the ops-layer soaks (exist), the board/view-model invariant soak
  (Stage 1), the registry walk (P-1), the per-batch scripted screenshot
  walkthrough. Red-on-old stays absolute: no bug-class fix without a pin
  that fails on the pre-fix code.
- **P-8 — Standing law, consolidated.** P1–P3 performance invariants bind
  the rebuilt layer exactly as they bind the substrate (invalidation ∝
  realized rows; one live editor; virtualized long views). Overlays, never
  rendering attributes. Chrome `fixedSize` texts always carry a `lineLimit`
  (the b6dae25 class). `Theme/VoiceControls.swift` is THE chrome vocabulary.
  Complexity lives in the store; restraint lives in the UI.
- **P-9 — No god objects in the frontend either.** A view model mixing
  board layout, text authority, and gesture routing splits by concern
  (`TakesViewModel` at 890 lines is the standing counterexample). Same
  hygiene rule as the substrate, applied where it was being waived.

**The rules you work under (restated here; they bind):**

**THE ONE DEVIATION FROM THE BRIEF, declared up front (the brief's "zero core change is the design; if you
believe the op must change, stop and record why before touching it"):** `Operations.divideW` is changed —
ADDITIVELY, both arms defaulting to today's behaviour byte-for-byte — for two reasons found by reading the
op against the composition, both of which would otherwise be SILENT LOSSES on the new default:

1. **A parked take arrived NAMELESS.** `divideW` mints its successors through `mintFanBlock` with no
   `labels:` argument (`Operations+Structural.swift:410–414` on the old tree), so every take is born with
   `label = nil`. That was invisible while the ceremony was divideW's only caller and every parked take was
   a rare deliberate act; under keep-on-top EVERY other take parks on B at EVERY fanned divide, so a take
   she named ("the spare") would lose its name on the most ordinary gesture. The canon rule everywhere else
   in §9 is explicit — `divideDuplicating`: *"labels copied — a whole-take ride keeps its name, the
   merge-carry precedent"*; `mergeCeremony`'s carries do the same. divideW's paragraph is SILENT, which is
   an omission at 13b Stage 4 (parking arrived; labels were never threaded), not a decision. The fix belongs
   in the op because 18f's "all takes stay with the top block" preset parks takes through this same door.
   **Split halves stay unlabeled, exactly as today** (they are fresh texts, the W's own rule).
2. **The successors stopped showing the take she divided when it was not the block's rendered take.**
   `divideW` anchors each side's chosen/default on `context.rendered` (A's chosen variant). On Write that IS
   the displayed take, so nothing changes there; on the Takes board (the caret sits in ANY take's pane —
   `seedTakeForDivide`) and on the phone (a PEEKED take is the displayed one), it is not. Composed
   unchanged, keep-on-top would have made B render the OTHER take whole while C rendered the divided take's
   second half — the note reading the paragraph whole and then its tail again. Today's default on both
   platforms (`divideDuplicating`) guarantees "each successor shows your cut halves", and U-2 changes only
   WHERE THE OTHER TAKES GO. So `divideW` gains `displayedVariantID: String? = nil`; nil keeps
   `context.rendered` (the ceremony passes nil and is untouched). **This edge is also logged as
   `notes/QUESTIONS.md` #91, PROVISIONAL**, because "what does the top block render when you divided a take
   it was not showing" is product-flavoured and hers to settle.

**THE DESIGN AS BUILT (the decisions §5.1 left to the implementer, each named):**

1. **The intercept sits at `EditorTextView.insertNewline(_:)`**, not `keyDown` — the one selector both
   Return and ⇧⏎ reach (the A15 trace's own finding), so the existing soft-newline guard stays the first
   word and the list door keeps its place. **The claim is refused for a non-editable surface (a sealed
   note) and while MARKED TEXT is up** (an IME composition's ⏎ commits the composition — it is not this
   gesture).
2. **The decision is a PURE function** (`TypedReturn.act`) because it is consulted TWICE per keystroke: at
   the key, to answer "is this mine?" (which decides whether a newline is typed at all), and again at the
   act's own main-actor turn, where it is RE-DERIVED against the surface the previous act left behind. Two
   fast Returns therefore compose (⏎⏎ = a new block, then the empty block's ruled no-op) instead of racing
   a stale offset into a divide. The act rides the deferred-keystroke seam (`scheduleCrossBlockCompound` —
   chained and awaitable; its NAME is the class it was built for, the comment says so at the call site).
3. **Return at the START of a block: an empty block ABOVE, the caret staying in the text block** (§5.1's
   first option — "push this paragraph down"). The seam did not argue: `Operations.InsertPosition.before`
   already exists, so this is zero core change.
4. **The tail's road is kept, with ONE narrowing that pin (9) forces.** A note with no blocks is all tail
   and its paragraphs still crystallize (untouched); a tail WITH TEXT still crystallizes (untouched); an
   **EMPTY** open tail — what the idle mint leaves behind after ⏎-then-pause, where the tail road plans
   nothing at all — is the trap §4.1 traced as her *"several new lines"*, so the act closes that render
   artifact (the shipped `.closeTail` verdict, through the ordinary editing path, no store write) and mints
   the block. Without this the batch would have left her S1 scenario exactly as she reported it.
5. **The insert states its SEAM** (`.divide` for below, `.extract(.prefix)` for above — the degenerate
   shapes of both, which `StructuralSeamEdit`'s three guard layers and the DEBUG oracle verify): an insert
   used to re-render the whole surface from the store, free for a menu act and cost ∝ document for a
   keystroke, which is what P1 forbids. `insertBlockBelowCaret` (⌘⇧⏎) now shares that one body, so the two
   doors cannot drift.
6. **A non-empty selection is NOT this gesture** (the K5 precedent in `MarkdownActs.listReturn`, for its
   reason: the ruling is about a caret, and replacing a span is a different gesture) — recorded, not
   invented.

A list typed at a note's END therefore travels the tail road: it crystallizes ONE BLOCK PER ITEM, and ⏎ on its empty item ends the list WITHOUT making a block. §5.1 batch 2's premise *"a tail exists only after a paste/drop now"* and the R-2 record's claim that the `.openTail` arm *"simply becomes unreachable from a typed ⏎ because the intercept acts first"* are both false.**
- **Mechanism (traced):** `insertNewline` computes `list = .continueList` for a texted list line and hands the key to `insertNewlineContinuingLists`; its `.continueList` arm (`MarkdownActs.swift:388–393`) calls the `ordinary` closure, which — seeing `.continueList`, not `.ordinary` — skips `claimTypedReturn()` and runs `super.insertNewline(sender)` (`EditorTextView.swift:130`). That is R-2's residual 3 — which records the symptom and attributes it to *"the tail road, which this batch does not touch"*; the cause is the key's own list arm.
- **Evidence on this tree:** `ListContinuationTests.theDocumentEndTailGestureStillFiresAndTheLeadLandsInTheTail` (`App/Variorum/VariorumTests/WalkBuildRoundTests.swift:394–409`) is GREEN in my run — it asserts `hasOpenTail == true` and `"- milk\n- "` after a REAL ⏎ at the document end. - **Mechanism (traced):** the key claims the act synchronously (`runTypedReturn`) and the act runs on the NEXT main-actor turn (`scheduleTypedReturn` → `scheduleCrossBlockCompound`, `:1497`); both arms — `insertEmptyBlock` and `invokeGesture(.divideAtCursor)` — enter `runStructural`, which sets `isEditable = false` and then awaits `autosave.flushNow()` (a writer-queue write whenever the buffer is dirty, which it always is right after typing a paragraph), `awaitMintSettle()`, `session.runner.run` (a second writer-queue write; `OperationsRunner` is an actor over the serialized `AppDatabase.write`) and a reader hop, before `applyStructuralResult` and the `defer` re-enable editing. Any `keyDown` in that window → `interpretKeyEvents` → `insertText:` → `NSTextView.shouldChangeText(in:replacementString:)` returns false while the view is not editable → the character is discarded (NSBeep). Before 18c the same ⏎ was a synchronous content insert with no writer hop at the key; now anything else holding the writer — an autosave flush of a large buffer, a sync pull applying its batch in ONE transaction (SyncSpec §5), a purge-janitor pass — stretches the window from milliseconds to that transaction's length. The fix's record should also state the measured quiet-machine window.
- **Fix — defer, never drop:** `EditorTextView.keyDown` stashes NSEvents while the surface controller reports a flight in progress (a flag flipped beside `isEditable` in `runStructural`), and the flight's `defer` replays them through `keyDown(with:)` once editing is back — so a replayed character lands at the LANDED caret (the new block, which is where she meant it) and a replayed ⏎ chains through the same deferred seam as today. General to every structural flight (⌘⇧D then typing is the same class), scoped to `keyDown` (key equivalents route through `performKeyEquivalent` and are untouched). If the implementer disputes on frequency, the dispute returns to me; my position is that a silent drop on this key earns the deferral regardless of its rate.

- **Mechanism (traced):** seed `["alpha"]`, caret 5; she types ⏎ `x` ⏎ `y` inside one flight window and presses ⌘Q. ⏎₁ claims → arms → A1 scheduled; `x` ⏎₂ `y` stashed. `applicationShouldTerminate` → `finalizeWork()` → the guard passes (`pendingCrossBlockTask != nil`, `:553`) → its Task captures `pending` = A1 (`:557`) and awaits it. A1 completes; `finalizeWork` resumes from the ONE await it holds, runs `autosave.flushNow()` (`:560`) and the mint loop, returns; the delegate replies terminate. A2 — a real flight, at least two writer hops behind `finalizeWork`'s one — is mid-air or unstarted; `y` sits in `deferredKeyEvents`, drained only by A2's tail. **The harness already knows this shape:** `EditorTestSupport.flush()` (`:121–126`) loops precisely because *"a chained schedule replaced the handle"*; the production doors do not.

#### Considered and cleared (traced, not findings — the sanity pass's *"no road arms and reaches neither drain"*, which I set out to falsify and could not)
- **The idle gate's two conditions are exact complements, every interleaving enumerated:** (i) a flight's `defer` runs while a task is pending → declines; that task's tail runs with no flight up → drains. (ii) A task's tail runs while a MENU flight is up → declines (and clears the handle); the flight's `defer` finds the handle nil → drains. (iii) A task's own flight → its `defer` declines on its own handle; its tail drains. (iv) A task's body refused by `runStructural`'s one-flight guard (`:2417`, BEFORE the arming at `:2431`) → arms nothing; its tail declines under the flight; the flight's `defer` drains. A tail whose token was superseded (`:1516`) neither clears nor drains, and the superseding task always runs its own tail: nothing cancels the handle (grep — assigned `:1509`, cleared `:1517`, read at `EditorViewModel.swift:554/557/1703`, no `.cancel()` anywhere in the App target).
- **A stash with NEITHER a flight nor a task pending cannot exist.** The App target has exactly two arming sites (grep): the CLAIM (`EditorViewModel.swift:1552`, `scheduleTypedReturn` on the very next line — the act is queued before any key can arrive) and `runStructural` (`:2431`, after the guard, before the first `await`). `replayDeferredKeystrokes()` has exactly one caller (the gate, `:1540`); the gate has exactly two (`:1524` the tail, `:2447` the `defer`, last).
- **No nested or synchronous drain:** both gate callers are async contexts; a replayed key can only SCHEDULE (`scheduleCrossBlockCompound` / `scheduleTypedReturn`) or edit synchronously through `shouldChangeText`, never run a flight inline. The stash is copied and cleared before the replay loop (`EditorTextView.swift:156–158`), so keys a replayed ⏎'s re-arming stashes go to a fresh array — `keyDown` reads the flag per event, as the comment says.
- **Ordering inside `runStructural`'s `defer`** (`:2433–2447`): `structuralInFlight = false` → `isEditable` restored → the idle clock → `applyPendingIfClean()` → the gate, LAST — the replay always meets an editable surface with the deferred projection applied; nothing between those statements yields.
- **The view is never reused across models:** `EditorSurface.makeNSView` / `InlineEditorSurface.makeNSView` (`EditorView.swift:393–397, 480–484`) mint a fresh `EditorTextView` per representable; `EditorViewModel.attach` is the one writer of `textView` and no road nils it, so a flight's `defer` always drains the view it armed. (A re-attach INSIDE a flight window would need a mode switch inside a few ms — the click residual's class; recorded, not a finding.)
- **R2-2's decide-then-act, adversarially:** the guard (`:1544`) reads the same source the act reads (`header?.effectiveSegmentation`; nil ⇒ `.paragraph` on both roads, `:1521`/`TypedReturn.swift:92` — consistent). Under chip OFF the `.exitList` road's lead deletion stands (K5's letter, chip-independent by design — the implementer's rider) and the discarded claim result (`EditorTextView.swift:220`) runs nothing else.

**Piece 4 — THE DIVIDE SHEET'S ARRANGEMENT ROW (U-5 · U-3).** `DivideWCeremony.Arrangement`
(`keepOnTop · keepOnBottom · copyToBoth · perTake`, the ruled order) on `State`; the sheet's FIRST
control is the row of four (`VoicedChip`, the chrome vocabulary — batch 2 gives it the mockup's face),
`keepOnTop` selected on open.

- **ONE seeding brain, and it CONSUMES the instant default's.** `DivideWCeremony.arranged(_:as:seedID:)`
  routes the two parking presets THROUGH `KeepOnTopDivide.compose` / `compose(keepBelow:)` rather than
  re-deriving their arithmetic, so "the sheet's preset produces the same cuts dict as the instant
  divide, byte-for-byte" is true by construction. The SEED take is never re-placed (its ✂ is the
  gesture's, and hers once she moves it); `copyToBoth` gives the others no ✂ at all (they are duplicated,
  not cut); `perTake` fills any unplaced ✂ with the take's END — which IS U-3 — and leaves a hand-placed
  cut alone. An EMPTY take stays unmarked under a preset (it cannot park), matching
  `KeepOnTopDivide.unparkable` exactly.
- **`open` no longer seeds from `CutPropagation`** (the brief's "the proposal survives ONLY as the ⌥←/→
  strong step, never the default position"). It survives where it still answers a real question: the
  drift `refresh`'s re-seed of a take whose text moved under an open sheet, and Make Block's cross-take
  mapping. The arrangement SURVIVES a drift refresh and re-places every ✂ over the refreshed texts.
- **Confirm roads:** `keepOnTop` / `keepOnBottom` / `perTake` → `divideW(cuts:displayedVariantID:)`;
  `copyToBoth` → `divideDuplicating(displayedVariantID:cut:)`. The host protocol gained
  `runDivideDuplicating(blockID:displayedVariantID:cut:)` and `runDivideW` gained the anchor; BOTH hosts
  (`EditorSurfaceController`, `TakesViewModel`) conform.

  door):** the sheet's confirm passes the SEED as `displayedVariantID` on every `divideW` road, including

  divide could leave B rendering another take whole beside C's tail of the divided one. `divideW` ignores

**ROW 3 — THE MECHANISM, FOUND BY USE.** With §4.4's three brains green, the fault was where the plan
predicted: the sheet's gesture wiring. `DivideWSheet` armed its `@FocusState keyboardFocused` exactly
ONCE, in `onAppear`, and every control inside it takes first responder when clicked — so **←/→, ⌥←/→
and ⇥ were dead for the rest of the sheet's life after the first click on a control.** Her own session
made that click unavoidable: the lesson (and the sheet's own copy) tells you to uncheck a take before
confirming. What was left was dragging a ✂ into a 9-pt slot in a flow whose glyph overlaps its
neighbours — which is exactly *"the scissors couldn't be placed at the end of the block"*. **The
click/drag road to the end always worked** (walked: a click right of the last word parks the ✂ and the
row says so), which is why the pure pins could never have caught this.

**Three focus roads were tried and all three stayed deaf** (each walked): assigning
`keyboardFocused = true` (a no-op — `@FocusState` publishes edges), bouncing it false→true in the same
turn, bouncing it a runloop turn later; `.focusable(false)` on the chips and the checkbox did not stop
them taking first responder either. **The fix is a local key MONITOR** installed only while the sheet is
on screen (it is window-modal, so that is exactly its scope), acting on the four placement chords and
returning every other event untouched; `.onKeyPress` stays on the container as the ordinary road, and
both roads call the same two brains (`stepCut`, `stepTake`) so they cannot answer differently.
RED and GREEN both captured.

`App/Variorum/VariorumTests/CutFlowEndSlotTests.swift` (4 tests, 1 suite, green at
`-only-testing:VariorumTests/CutFlowEndSlotTests`):

- **(i) `theEndOfATakeIsALegalCutPosition` — PASSES.** `legalCutPositions(of: "Alpha beta.")` contains
  11, and the end survives every ending shape (terminator · trailing space · trailing newline · one
  word); the empty take is the one deliberate exception. `BoundarySnapping.boundaries` seeds its set
  with `[0, text.utf16.count]` before any scanner runs, so the end can never be dropped.
- **(ii) `theEndSlotIsLaidOutInsideTheFlowsOwnSize` — PASSES.** At a wrapping width whose LAST line is
  the widest (asserted in the pin, so it cannot go vacuous), the end slot's frame sits inside
  `geometry.size` in both axes. `size.width = min(widest, width)` cannot clip it: a slot is only ever
  placed at `x == 0` or where `x + slotWidth <= width`, and `widest` is taken after the end slot.
- **(iii) `aPointRightOfTheLastTokenResolvesToTheEndSlot` — PASSES.** Just past the end slot, far right
  of the row, and below the row all resolve to the end.
- Plus `steppingForwardReachesTheEndAndParksThere` (the keyboard road): → walks to the end and parks.

**Piece 1 — `ProseCutGeometry`: THE TAKE, AS PROSE.**

Her row 5 names three things and this file answers the first: *"the spacing between the words"*. The
shipped face drew each take as a TOKEN FLOW — a word, a fixed **9-pt slot**, a word, a slot
(`CutFlowGeometry.slotWidth`) — so every legal cut position occupied real width and the prose could
never read as prose. `ProseCutGeometry` lays the take out with **Core Text** instead (one paragraph at
a time, so a take's own newlines survive as content — I4), places the legal cuts as **zero-width
marks**, and the ✂ is drawn OVER the inter-word gap rather than occupying one. **The cut is not an
input to the layout**, so placing or moving it cannot move a word.

- **ONE snapping brain, literally.** The marks are handed to **`CutFlowGeometry.nearestSlot`** — row
  first, then distance, strong slots pull — so the rule `CutFlowEndSlotTests` pins stays one function
  in one place rather than a second implementation that has to agree with the first. That is also why
  `CutFlowGeometry` survives (below).
- **No TextKit anywhere near it** (TEXTKIT2 §4): a sheet is chrome, and this is a measurement. Core
  Text, drawn into one `Canvas` — the L1 architecture kept, with a different thing laid out.
- **The air above every line (`markGlyphAir`) is part of the LAYOUT, not the drawing** — the ✂ glyph
  rides in it (the mockup's `.cut::after`). Found by walking: at the shipped leading the glyph landed
  in the middle of the line above. An offset applied at draw time only would have to be subtracted
  again at hit-test time, which is the two-mechanisms class the file exists to avoid.
- **The marks are placed in ONE pass beside the lines** and `lineIndex(for:)` is a binary search. The
  first cut looked each boundary's line up linearly and measured **1,374 ms** to mount her four
  3,000-word takes; the pin below is what caught it (258 ms now).

Pins: `ProseCutGeometryTests` (9). The natural-spacing one is **RED on the shipped renderer by
construction and non-vacuous**: it asserts the prose's width against the font's own measure AND prints
`CutFlowGeometry`'s width for the same sentence beside it.

#### Findings, severity-ranked

**R1-1 · [MAJOR] · `App/Variorum/Variorum/Features/Editor/DivideWSheet.swift:280–306` (`installKeyMonitor` / `handleKeyEvent`), `:384–403` (`stepCut`) · the sheet's key monitor is PROCESS-wide, not window-scoped — it swallows ⇥/←/→ typed in ANY of the app's windows while the sheet is up, and moves the ✂ with them.** Evidence: `NSEvent.addLocalMonitorForEvents(matching: .keyDown)` sees every key event the app dequeues; the only guard is `ceremony.state != nil` (`:283`), and `handleKeyEvent` returns `true` (event swallowed, `:284`) whenever `stepCut`/`stepTake` do — `stepCut` returns `true` for EVERY ←/→ under a preset, because the seed is always aimable (`:367–371`, `:387–402`; even when the cut does not move it sets `activeTakeID` and answers `true`). The sheet is window-modal for ONE window, and the app has others with live editors: the per-note `WindowGroup` (`VariorumApp.swift:295` → `NoteWindowView`), the Quick Note window (`:331`), the helper (`:351`), Settings (`:357`). Inputs → outcome: "Divide choosing takes" open in note window A; she clicks into note window B (open in its own window) and presses → / ⌥→ / ⇧→ to move or extend the caret — the monitor swallows it and steps the ✂ in A; B's caret never moves; under "Choose per take…" with two checked takes ⇥ in B is eaten too. `handleKeyEvent` also ignores ⌘/⌃ (it reads only `.shift`/`.option`), so ⌘→ (line end) is eaten the same way. The codebase already owns the correct shape of this door and this batch built a second, unscoped one beside it: `PageTurnKeyMonitor` (`Core/Views/PageTurnKeys.swift:90–98` — the Act 10 correction round's R1-5 — guards `event.window === window` and refuses every chord), and `PaneFocusCatcherView` (`Workspace/PaneFocusCatcher.swift:115–123`) — which compares **by `windowNumber`**, with the recorded reason ("`event.window` … answers nil for a window with no device — which is every window a test builds"). Fix: replace the inline `@State` monitor with a zero-size `NSViewRepresentable` monitor view inside the sheet (the `PageTurnKeyMonitor` shape: install in `viewDidMoveToWindow`, remove when the window goes), guarding `event.windowNumber == window.windowNumber`, refusing ⌘/⌃ chords, its decision an exposed `handleKeyDown(_:) -> Bool` body so a pin can drive it with a real `NSEvent` and a real second window's number; `DivideWSheet` keeps `handleKeyEvent`'s brains and drops the two install/remove functions. **Pin (red-on-old):** mount the sheet in an `NSWindow` exactly as `DivideCeremonyCostTests.mountSheet` does (which fires `onAppear` and installs the monitor in the test host), make a second `NSWindow`, post a → `NSEvent.keyEvent(… windowNumber: other.windowNumber …)` and settle — on old the seed's cut steps; on new it does not; the same event carrying the sheet window's number steps it on both (non-vacuity). If the host does not deliver posted events to a local monitor (the `PaneFocusCatcher` measurement warns it may not — it measured `sendEvent`, not `postEvent`), the honest form is the precedent's: assert installation + drive the exposed body with both window numbers, and record it as the rig's form (batch 1's own row-3 disposition).

**R1-2 · [MAJOR] · `EditorSurfaceController.swift:1445–1464` (`confirmMergeCeremony`'s preset branch) → `:376–391` (`runInstantMerge`, the unguarded read at `:379`), `:608` (`runCarryAllMerge`), `:673` (`runMergeChain`) · the two preset roads act on ENTRY INDICES captured when the sheet opened (`:1282`), after the sheet sat open for as long as she liked — and `runInstantMerge` indexes the projection with them unguarded.** Evidence: before this letter `runInstantMerge` ran in the same turn as its plan (the ⌘⇧M road, and `openMergeCeremony`'s open-time fallthrough); U-5's row makes it the CONFIRM of a sheet that can sit open while the projection re-renders — a sync apply landing under it (the drift class the pairing road already guards against, `:1466–1490`), or a menu chord that stays live under a window-modal sheet (`DivideWCeremony.swift:45–48`'s own note). Inputs → outcome: a two-block note `[A, B(fanned)]`, ⌥⌘⇧M at the seam → the sheet with `entryIndices 0...1`; block A dies (a remote tombstone, or Delete Block from the menu bar) and the index re-renders to ONE entry; "Only the two shown" → `model.index.entries[1]` (`:379`) → index out of range → the app traps. With blocks above the pair the same road does not trap but reads the WRONG entry's length: the caret lands off the join and the seam it reports (`.merge(leadingIndex:)`, `:387`) names the wrong entry, so `StructuralSeamEdit.derive` refuses (`StructuralSeamEdit.swift:208–211`, `fresh[i].blockID == mergedID`) and the differential apply silently becomes a full render. `runCarryAllMerge` (`:640`) and `runMergeChain` (`:676`) guard the trap (`index < count ? … : 0`) but keep the stale lengths — same wrong caret. The pairing road is immune (it re-reads both fans and merges by ID). The rule this breaks is the file's own: `runPlainDivide` `:404–411` — *"Re-resolved by BLOCK ID because the fallback road reaches here after a flush, and an index taken before a suspension can address a re-tiled surface."* Fix: in the dispatcher (`:1445`), re-resolve `state.blockIDs` against the CURRENT index at confirm time; any block absent → refuse in the refresh road's own voice ("These blocks' takes changed — try the merge again."), dismiss, touch nothing; pass the fresh indices to the three roads — and harden `runInstantMerge`'s length/seam reads to resolve by block ID so no future stale caller can trap it. **Pin (red-on-old, no trap):** a four-block note, the sheet on blocks 1–2 (the second fanned), block 0 deleted through ops + `reload()` under the open sheet, "Only the two shown", confirm → the caret sits at the join (`selectedRange().location == merged entry + leading length + 1`); on old it lands at the stale entry's arithmetic (one unit off with the fixture's lengths). The two-block shape traps on old — recorded here, deliberately not used as the pin.

**R1-3 · [MINOR] · `DivideWCeremony.swift:449–477` (`arrangementSentence`) with its call site `DivideWSheet.swift:115–118`; `MergeArrangement.swift:87–107` (`MergeArrangementCopy.sentence`) · the ONE sentence under each row is ungrammatical in the singular and double-counts empty takes — and the batch PINNED both defects.** Evidence: `takes(1)` + `" stay whole"` → **"1 other take stay whole on the top block"** on every TWO-take divide (the commonest fan), pinned as-is at `DivideArrangementTests.swift:289` (`"1 other take stay"`, "singular counts"); with an empty other take: **"2 other takes stay whole on the top block; … 1 empty take can't be placed and stays with the original block"** — `others` (`State.otherTakes.count`) includes the unparkable, so the first count is false by one; pinned as-is at `:274` (`"2 other takes"` with `unparkable: 1`). The merge row: **"1 other take come along whole"** / **"1 other take stay with the released blocks"**, pinned at `MergeArrangementTests.swift:276`. The J8 copy-truth doctrine (the record's own citation) says a sentence may claim only what the operation will do. Fix: conjugate by count and say the parked count (`others − unparkable`) for the two parking presets (copy-to-both keeps `others`: `divideDuplicating` duplicates an empty take too — see R1-5); re-pin the corrected words. **Pin (red-on-old):** `arrangementSentence(.keepOnTop, others: 2, unparkable: 1)` contains `"1 other take stays whole"`; `(.keepOnBottom, others: 1, unparkable: 0)` contains `"1 other take stays"`; `MergeArrangementCopy.sentence(.bringEveryTake, blocks: 2, otherTakes: 1)` contains `"1 other take comes along whole"`.

**R1-4 · [MINOR] · `ProseTakeCard.swift:85–86` (`status(.original)`), `:130` (`footerNote`); `DivideWCeremony.swift:481–499` (`presetRowNote`), `:647–650` (`uncheckedRowNote`) · the unchecked take's card dropped the 13f W10a answer the mockup keeps, and the two batch-1 copy homes of that answer went DEAD behind pins that stay green.** Evidence: mockup figure A, state 2, unchecked take: *"not cut — stays on the original block, in Block History → Came from"*; built: `"Not cut — stays whole on the original block, in lineage"` + footer `"original block · lineage"` — the PATH is gone from the row. 13f W10a (her sitting question, verbatim in the file: *"how do I even see the original one?"*) put the path on the row precisely because that is where she was looking. `presetRowNote` and `uncheckedRowNote` were batch 1's homes for the row copy; after batch 2 NO production caller remains (grep: definitions only) — while `OriginBlockDoorTests.swift:59` and `NoteTrayTests.swift:413` keep asserting `uncheckedRowNote.contains(TrayPath.originalsPath)` — green over a string no surface speaks (the F-3 vacuity class recorded in this very file's header, `DivideWSheet.swift:34–41`). The sheet's resting footer line still names the path, so the promise is half-kept, not lost. Fix: `CeremonyCardCopy.status(.original)` names `TrayPath.originalsPath` (the mockup's own words), the card becomes the ONE home (retire `presetRowNote`/`uncheckedRowNote`, or have the card read them), and the two pins point at the live home. **Pin (red-on-old):** `CeremonyCardCopy.status(.original, words: nil).contains(TrayPath.originalsPath)`.

**R1-5 · [MINOR] · `ProseTakeCard.swift:60–62` (`CeremonyCardCopy.destination`) · an EMPTY other take under "Copy takes to both" is told it stays on the original block, but `divideDuplicating` duplicates it onto BOTH successors.** Evidence: `if isEmpty { return marked && arrangement == .perTake ? .empty : .original }` runs BEFORE the `.copyToBoth` rule at `:62`; `arranged(.copyToBoth)` marks every take (`DivideWCeremony.swift:412–418`); `Operations+Structural.swift:598–606` fetches every other active take with no emptiness filter and `:640` mints `[half] + others.map(\.workingText)` on both sides. **R1-1 · AGREE (MAJOR).** Re-traced: `NSEvent.addLocalMonitorForEvents(matching: .keyDown)` sees every
key event this PROCESS dequeues; `installKeyMonitor` (`DivideWSheet.swift:280–286`) guards only
`ceremony.state != nil`, and `handleKeyEvent` (`:294–306`) returns the step's own answer, which for ←/→
under a preset is ALWAYS `true` — `stepCut` (`:384–403`) answers `true` even when the cut does not move
(`else { activeTakeID = takeID }`), so the event is swallowed at every boundary, including the ends. The
app really does have the other windows named (`VariorumApp.swift:47`, `:295`, `:331`, `:351`, `:357`),
and both cited precedents are as quoted (`PageTurnKeys.swift:88–98` guards `event.window === window`;
`Workspace/PaneFocusCatcher.swift:113–124` compares `event.windowNumber == window.windowNumber` with its
recorded reason). **Two things the fix must carry, from the walk that produced this monitor** (the record's
piece 6): (a) it exists because THREE focus roads were tried and all three stayed deaf — plain assignment,
a same-turn `@FocusState` bounce, a next-turn bounce, plus `.focusable(false)` on the chips and the
checkbox — so the replacement must keep working while an AppKit control inside the `ScrollView` holds
first responder, which a `viewDidMoveToWindow`-installed monitor does and a focus re-arm does not; and
(b) `windowNumber`, not `event.window`, is the right comparison for exactly `PaneFocusCatcher`'s recorded
reason, which is what makes the pin's second window drivable at all. I would add one thing to the fix's
scope, from the same trace: **the swallow should follow the STEP, not the aim** — `stepCut` answering
`true` when nothing moved is what makes ←/→ eaten at a take's ends even in the sheet's own window, and it
is one `return next != nil && next != take.cut` away.

#### ROUND 1 — THE RAISE'S FINAL WORD (fable-reviewer)

**The raise (R1-1's dropped `ceremony.state != nil` guard) — CONFIRMED and FIXED, `5c848a79`.** Traced against the tree: `DivideWSheet.state` is `ceremony.state ?? presented` (`DivideWSheet.swift:72–74`); after `state = nil` (Cancel, ⎋, a landed confirm) the sheet's view is still mounted — SwiftUI's dismissal animation, or a host that never unmounts it — so `stepCut` read the PRESENTED snapshot, found a take with boundaries and a `next != cut`, called `placeCut`, which no-opped inside `DivideWCeremony.placeCut`'s own `guard var current = state` (`DivideWCeremony.swift:526–532`), and answered `true`: the key was swallowed for nothing. Batch 1's monitor had `guard ceremony.state != nil else { return event }` as its first line (`installKeyMonitor`, the pre-fix `:283`); my R1-1 fix moved the guard to the window and did not carry that one. Narrow (a chord inside the dismissal) and correctly sized (one line). **Fix:** `guard ceremony.state != nil else { return false }` at the top of `handleKeyEvent`, before the chord rule. **Pin:** `DivideKeyMonitorTests.aKeyAfterTheCeremonyClosedIsNotTheSheets` — the sheet's own → is consumed while open (non-vacuity), `ceremony.cancel()`, the view still watching (asserted), then → / ← / ⇥ all answer `false` and nothing reopens. **Red on `50d47d85`, recorded:** `DivideKeyMonitorTests.swift:204 monitor.handleKeyDown(→) == false` failed and `:206 (←) == false` failed (⇥ passed on both sides — a preset never swallows it — and is kept as a guard, not evidence). Green: `DivideKeyMonitorTests · DivideCeremonyCostTests · DivideArrangementTests · DivideCeremonyRowTapTests · DivideWCeremonyTests · TakesDivideTests · OriginBlockDoorTests` → **`✔ Test run with 67 tests in 7 suites passed after 6.290 seconds.`**

**The walk fact — another app window's raise DISMISSES the divide sheet — my reading: a RECORDED BEHAVIOUR with an owner, not a round-2 finding.** It is outside this letter's diff (untouched by batch 1, batch 2 and this pass; the implementer's grep stands — `ceremony.cancel()` has one caller), so a fresh round-2 reviewer of `db02623a..HEAD` would rightly not be reviewing it; it is also a real thing she would feel (a half-arranged ceremony lost to a glance at another window — or to Quick Note from the File menu). One look at the mechanism's neighbourhood: the workspace tracks the key window through `WindowKeyReporter` / `WindowRegistry.keyWindowID` (`Workspace/WindowRegistry.swift:192–231`), and the note window's content is keyed `.id(postID)` (`NoteWindowView.swift:91`); the `.sheet(item: $model.divideWCeremony)` presenter (`EditorView.swift:185`) is dismissed when whatever the key-window change re-composes tears the presenter down — SwiftUI then writes nil into the item binding, which IS the cancel road without anyone calling `cancel()`. That is a sketch, not a trace: the exact re-composition is one read further than this pass owed, and it is the workspace's window family, not the ceremony's. **Owner, recommended:** a standing-fixes **17 entry at her word** (her own 17 rule — a quick bug she'd notice, hers to add), with `notes/KnownIssuesAndTechDebt.md` carrying the row until then under **13u2's pane/window family** if she declines; the round's closeout writes the row (the closeout owns this round's KnownIssues writes). Two notes for whoever takes it: (1) the merge sheet (`.sheet(item: $model.mergeCeremony)`) almost certainly shares the behaviour — check it in the same entry; (2) the R1-1 fix stands independently of it — the process-wide monitor also ate keys aimed at panels the sheet does not own (the implementer's Character Viewer case), and the pinned mechanism (a key for another window number) is exactly what a second window would send if the sheet survived the raise.
