#### Findings, severity-ranked

**R2-1 · [MAJOR] · `App/Variorum/Variorum/Features/Editor/EditorSurfaceController.swift:1574–1602` (`refreshMergeCeremony`), with `:1160–1198` (`MergeCeremonyState`'s three DEFAULTED fields) and `:1468–1479` (R1-2's dispatcher guard) · the pairing road's drift REFRESH rebuilds the state WITHOUT `blockIDs`, `otherTakes` and `arrangement` — so a drift under "Pair by hand…" silently flips the sheet to "Bring every take", hides her pairings, lies about the count, changes the sheet's identity, and R1-2's presence guard goes vacuous over an EMPTY `blockIDs`.** Evidence (traced, inputs → outcome): a pair `[A, B]` with B fanned (tail + spare); ⌥⌘⇧M → the sheet on `.bringEveryTake` (`openMergeCeremony:1305–1313` sets `blockIDs: [A, B]`, `otherTakes: 1`); she picks "Pair by hand…" (`setMergeArrangement`); a sync round lands an edit to a take's text while the sheet is up; ⏎ → `confirmMergeCeremony` → the `.pairByHand` branch's drift check (`:1501–1517`) → `refreshMergeCeremony(from:…)` → `:1588–1594` constructs `MergeCeremonyState(firstBlockID:, secondBlockID:, firstRenderedID:, secondRenderedID:, firstTakes:, secondTakes:, pairings:)` — the MEMBERWISE init, so `blockIDs = []`, `otherTakes = 0`, `arrangement = .bringEveryTake` (`:1168`, `:1176`, `:1186`). Four consequences, each read off the tree: **(1)** `MergeCeremonySheet.swift:84` renders `pairingBody` only under `.pairByHand`, so the refreshed sheet shows the PRESET preview with "Bring every take" selected — her pairings survive in `next.pairings` (`:1597–1599`) but are no longer on screen, while the status says *"review the pairings before merging"* (`:1601`); **(2)** `arrangementSentence` (`:1213–1217`) reads `otherTakes == 0` → *"There are no other takes to bring."* — false for a fanned pair; **(3)** `id` is `blockIDs.joined(separator: "+")` (`:1198`) → `""`, so `.sheet(item: $model.mergeCeremony)` (`EditorView.swift:187`) sees a NEW item and re-presents the sheet; **(4)** the second ⏎ takes the dispatcher's preset branch, where `state.blockIDs.allSatisfy { entryIndex(of: $0) != nil }` over `[]` is TRUE by vacuity, and `runCarryAllMerge` lands the carry-all where she asked for her hand-placed pairings. The existing pin `MergeCeremonySheetTests.confirmRefusesToJoinDriftedText:342–345` (*"Confirming the refreshed sheet lands"*) is GREEN FOR THIS WRONG REASON — its one pairing IS the carry-all's pair (head + rendered tail), so the rows coincide and the flipped road is invisible to it. Contrast the divide side: `DivideWCeremony.refresh` (`DivideWCeremony.swift:703–710`) carries `arrangement` and re-arranges over the refreshed texts — batch 1 did the divide half and not the merge half (`21806a53` added the three fields with defaults and left `refreshMergeCeremony` untouched); R1-2's fix (`20e7cfd4`) then made the dispatcher's safety depend on the very field the refresh drops. Inside this letter's diff on both counts. **Fix:** `refreshMergeCeremony` carries `blockIDs: state.blockIDs`, `arrangement: state.arrangement`, `runBlocks: state.runBlocks`, and recomputes `otherTakes` from the fresh fans (`max(0, firstFan.count − 1) + max(0, secondFan.count − 1)`); harden the dispatcher's guard against vacuity (`!state.blockIDs.isEmpty && …`). **Pins (RED on `5c848a79`):** (a) in `confirmRefusesToJoinDriftedText`, after the refresh: `state.arrangement == .pairByHand`, `state.blockIDs == [a, b]`, `state.otherTakes == 1`, `state.id` unchanged; (b) the behavioural pin — under "Pair by hand…" `removeMergePairing` the default and `pairMergeTakes(firstID: head, secondID: spare)`; drift the rendered TAIL's text through ops; confirm (refreshes); confirm again → the merged block carries ONE take reading head + " " + spare's text and the tail stays in lineage (`stayBehindCount` 1) — on old, the flipped carry-all mints head + tail joined WITH the spare carried (two takes on the merged block).

**R2-2 · [MINOR] · `EditorSurfaceController.swift:1468–1493` (the preset branch) vs `:1495–1517` (the pairing branch's drift check); `runCarryAllMerge:641–645` · the two preset roads confirm against ACT-time "shown" takes while the sheet displays the OPEN-time ones, and no drift check stands on them.** Evidence: `openMergeCeremony` captures `firstRenderedID`/`secondRenderedID` (`:1301–1304`) and the preview columns mark exactly those as *"＋ pairs with →"* (`MergeCeremonySheet.swift:180–212`); `runCarryAllMerge` composes from `model.index.entries.first { $0.blockID == leadingID }?.variantID` at act time (`:642`, `:644`), and `runInstantMerge` → `ops.merge` reads the store's CHOSEN. Inputs → outcome: the sheet open on `[A(fan h, h′), B]`; a sync apply re-points A's chosen to h′ and the projection adopts it (nothing suppresses adoption under the sheet — the pairing branch's own comment at `:1495–1500` says so); ⏎ on "Bring every take" joins h′ + B while the sheet showed h ＋ B, and the receipt says *"the takes you were looking at joined"*. The pairing road refreshes on ANY drift (*"instead of confirming what the author wasn't shown"*); the preset roads check only presence (R1-2). Narrow — a remote chosen re-point in the window, and ⌘⇧M made the same read within one turn before U-5 — but the sheet's open-ended window is what widens it, and the S4-23 drift doctrine is this letter's own. **Fix:** compose the carry-all from the STATE's rendered ids (`firstRenderedID`/`secondRenderedID`; a rendered take no longer live → `CarryAllMerge.compose`'s own nil → `takesChangedMerge`), or give the preset branch the pairing branch's check (rendered ids or texts changed → `refreshMergeCeremony`, which R2-1 makes safe). **Pin (red-on-old):** the sheet on a fanned pair, `.bringEveryTake`; re-point the trailing block's chosen to its spare through ops + `reload()` under the open sheet; confirm → the joined take reads head + the ORIGINAL tail (or the sheet refreshes and nothing lands) — on old it reads head + spare.

**R2-1 · AGREE (MAJOR) — and it is BATCH 1's, with a root cause worth naming.** Re-traced line by line:
`refreshMergeCeremony` (`:1588–1594`) calls `MergeCeremonyState(firstBlockID:secondBlockID:firstRenderedID:secondRenderedID:firstTakes:secondTakes:pairings:)`
— the MEMBERWISE init — so the four defaulted fields take their defaults: `blockIDs = []` (`:1168`),
`otherTakes = 0` (`:1176`), `runBlocks = []` (`:1181`), `arrangement = .bringEveryTake` (`:1186`). All
four consequences check out on the tree: the sheet renders `pairingBody` only under `.pairByHand`
(`MergeCeremonySheet.swift:84–89`, else `previewColumns`), so her pairings leave the screen while the
status still says *"review the pairings before merging"*; `arrangementSentence` takes the
`otherTakes > 0` guard's else branch (`MergeArrangement.swift:96–99`) and says *"There are no other takes
to bring"* about a fanned pair; `id` is `blockIDs.joined(separator: "+")` (`:1198`) → `""`, a new item to
`.sheet(item:)`; and the dispatcher's `state.blockIDs.allSatisfy { … }` (`:1473–1478`) is vacuously true
over `[]`. And the pin is green for the reason stated: `confirmRefusesToJoinDriftedText:342–345` asserts
only `landed.count == 1` after the second confirm, and its ONE pairing is the pre-pair (head + rendered
tail), which the carry-all also mints — the difference (the carry-all CARRIES the spare, so the merged
block ends with two takes rather than one) is a fact the pin never looks at.

**Whose miss, precisely, and why two reviews missed it:** batch 1 (`21806a53`) added the three fields to
`MergeCeremonyState` **with defaults** and updated the two OPEN sites (`openMergeCeremony:1305`,
`openMergeRunChoice:1379`) — and not the third construction site. Swift's memberwise init makes an
omitted defaulted argument **silent**: no warning, no diagnostic, nothing for a reader to notice. That is
the whole reason this survived a batch record, a cold round and a sanity pass. Worse for me: I DID apply
the rule on the divide side in the same batch — `DivideWCeremony.refresh` carries
`arrangement: current.arrangement` and re-arranges over the refreshed texts (`DivideWCeremony.swift:703–715`),
with a comment saying why — so the letter states the rule and implements it on one side only. R1-2 then
made a safety guard depend on the field the other side drops, which is what turns a display bug into a
road change.

**A rider on the fix, offered because it is the class and not the instance:** carrying the four fields in
`refreshMergeCeremony` and hardening the guard against vacuity are both right and necessary. The thing
that would have PREVENTED it is one line further out — **give `MergeCeremonyState` an explicit
initializer with no defaults**, so a construction site cannot silently omit a field and a future one
fails to compile instead. The run arm's `runBlocks`/`otherTakes` and the pair arm's `firstTakes` already
have to be supplied at every site anyway; only the defaults make omission possible. The reviewer's two
pins are the right pair — the state assertions catch the shape, the behavioural one catches the road —
and I would add one assertion to the first: `state.id == before.id`, since the identity change is what
re-presents the sheet under her.

**PIECE 5a — THE MEASUREMENT, and what it changed (the standing-17 rule 4).** Reporting on every caret
move meant a `UserDefaults` write per keystroke. Measured rather than assumed
(a throwaway probe, 10,000 calls, deleted after): **`CurrentBlockMemory.remember` ~103 µs per call, of
which ~102 µs is `UserDefaults.standard.set` itself** on this machine. O(1) in document size, so P1 is
not at risk — but ~100 µs of main-thread IPC per keystroke for a value nothing reads until a landing is
not a price worth paying. So the memory SPLIT: **the session dict takes every report (free); the
persisted copy is written when the block or its take changes, and once more when the note leaves the
screen** — `CurrentBlockMemory.persist(postID:)`, called from `CommandRouter.unregisterDetail` and from
`registerDetail` when the note changes. A caret walking inside one block now touches `UserDefaults` zero
times. The only thing a hard quit can cost is the offset's drift within the block she was last in — the

- `FocusedBlock` gains `utf16Offset: Int?` (`BlockHistoryPane.swift`) — **nil is UNKNOWN, never zero**;
  the name is `LandingTarget`'s on purpose.
- `CurrentBlockMemory` persists `blockID|variantID|utf16Offset`; a two-field string written before this
  batch reads back with a nil offset (the behaviour it had when it was written). **`remember`'s nil rule:
  a report with no offset for the SAME block keeps what is known** — Blocks' focused row and the
  outline's card hold no caret, and letting them erase her place would land her at the top of the
  paragraph she was standing in the middle of, which is the whole complaint. A report for ANOTHER block
  resets it.
- **`CommandRouter`: the offset rides BESIDE the observed identity, never in it.** `focusedBlock` is now
  a computed read that merges a `private` observed `focusedBlockIdentity` (assigned only when the block
  or its take changes — row 33's cadence, unmoved) with an `@ObservationIgnored` `focusedOffset`
  (rewritten on every report). **Why:** the offset must be fresh at caret rate, and the one view that
  registers a `body` dependency on this fact (the Block History pane's jump door) must not re-render on
  every keystroke — which is the cost row 33's own comment exists to refuse. One value, one truth, two
  lifetimes. `noteFocusedBlock` gains `utf16Offset: Int? = nil`; `registerDetail`'s restore, the
  teardown and `forgetCurrentBlock` move both halves together.
- **Reporters:** Write's `updateCaretContext` now reports on EVERY caret move (the block-change guard is
  retired *for the report* — an offset stale by one paragraph of typing is the defect; the decor pass
  keeps its own guard); `TakesViewModel.notePaneSelection` reports the LIVE pane's caret (the live pane
  only — a read pane's selection is not a caret, P-3's line); Read's `edit` pane gains
  `onSelectionChange` → `BlockTOCViewModel.notePaneCaret`. Blocks' row and the Library's Open report nil
  and land at the start, as today.
- **THE TRACE THIS BATCH FOUND, AND ITS FIX (measured, not read):** with only the above, the round trip
  landed at **113 — the block's END**. A probe named the culprit: *a take pane going live reports its
  block's END* (`[probe] TAKES pane reports offset 54`), because a read pane's `view.string = text` had
  left AppKit's selection there and the ring's responder claim reported it. That report became the
  note's remembered offset. The honest answer is the brief's own walk step (*"→ Takes → the live pane's
  caret is there"*): **a pane going live LANDS at the note's remembered place.** `PaneSurfaceView`/its
  representable/its coordinator gain `caretOnGoingLive: Int?`, applied on the live TRANSITION
  (`noteLiveness`'s existing one-shot occasion) and **before** the responder claim, so the pane's own
  report is that place. Armed by the models at the focus door — `TakesViewModel.armPaneCaretLanding`
  (both `focus` and the N9 `landAuthorityFocus`; the room's `focusWithCaretAtEnd` clears it — the END was
  asked for explicitly) and `BlockTOCViewModel.makeLive` — and **only for the note's CURRENT block**, so
  a click into another block keeps the place the click brought. Read at render through
  `caretLanding(forVariant:)`, `@ObservationIgnored`: a caret place is data, not a signal.

**PIECE 2 — Write's landing (DONE).** `bareArrivalLanding(fact:)` = the block's start + the remembered
offset, clamped to the block's CURRENT length (it may have shrunk while she was away; landing past its
end would put her in the next block — worse than the start) and to the document; a nil offset is the
block's start, unchanged. The bare arrival's reveal is **`JumpPrimitive.jump`**, not
`scrollRangeToVisible` (TEXTKIT2 §2 / the Phase 6 hybrid road), with the arrival's next-turn responder
retry kept.

**One neighbouring pin edited, justified:** `BlockHistoryPaneTests.withNote` now forgets its note's
current-block memory on entry and exit. Every world mints the SAME post id (`.incrementing` from zero)
and the memory persists per note into `UserDefaults.standard`, so one suite's caret arrived as this
suite's remembered offset and its whole-fact equality read `utf16Offset: 0` — the order-dependence the
Act 10 batch-G record already names, widened by one field. The pin's assertion is untouched.

**PIECE 3 — the reveal (DONE; row 20).**

- **ONE reveal for every landing in Write** — `EditorViewModel.revealLanding(_:textView:)`, consumed by
  all three arms of `applyFocusSeeds`: the bare arrival, the `pendingCaretSeed` arm (the Blocks
  workbench's Open in Write, the Index column's "Jump to block in Write", Read's `onJump`, the canvas
  card's — all of them `PostDetailView.jump(to:)`), and `applyWriteIntent` (the fire-and-DO landing,
  which had the same hole: a follow-up gesture that runs off-screen is a gesture she cannot see happen).
- **It is PARKED, not performed on the spot — and that is the finding of this piece.** The first cut
  jumped inline and measured `caret line top 6937 · visible 24.0…743.0`: at landing time
  `setSurfaceContent` has just replaced the storage, the text view's FRAME is still the pre-fill height,
  so `JumpPrimitive`'s scroll range (`docHeight − viewport`) is a couple of dozen points and the
  correction loop clamps there. The reveal is therefore spent at the **N14 layout-settle hop**
  (`overlayLayoutDidSettle`'s async turn — the same post-layout occasion the badge/decor family already
  waits for, and the first moment the frame is honest). Safe by construction: every caller sits inside
  `applyFocusSeeds`, which runs only on the INITIAL RENDER, so a geometry generation always bumps first
  and the hop always arrives. **After: `caret line top 6944 · visible 6944.1…7663.1`** — the landing is
  pixel-exact at the viewport top, the Phase 6 memo's promise.
- **The reveal is GUARDED, and this is a judgment call worth her eye (J-note below):** a caret already
  inside the visible rect scrolls nothing. Reveal means *make visible*, never *move* — without it a bare
  arrival would haul the caret's line to the viewport top on every ⌘2-then-⌘1, overriding the scroll
  anchor `renderFull` had just restored. Pinned both ways (block 200 → the page jumps and lands exact;
  block 2 → `visible.minY == 0`, the page never moves). The reveal also abandons itself if the caret has
  moved since it was parked — a second jump must never yank her away from a place she chose.
- `JumpPrimitive` gains **`lineTop(ofOffset:in:)`** — the geometry the jump itself steers (fragment frame
  + container origin), so "is it on screen?" and "put it on screen" can never disagree. The pin reads the
  same function rather than a copy of it.

**R1-5 · MAJOR (timing-dependent — traced by reading, not observed; the pin drives the ordering explicitly) · `App/Variorum/Variorum/Features/Editor/EditorViewModel.swift:1917–1931, :1938–1953, :2845–2869` (with `:352`, `:1002`, `:626–636`) · the parked reveal can be spent by a settle hop scheduled for an OLDER geometry generation, i.e. against the pre-fill frame the park exists to wait out — the row-20 defect recurring under a timing window.** Mechanism: `attach` bumps the generation to G₁ (`:352`); the empty editor's first display pass runs `overlayLayoutDidSettle` (`:2845`), which schedules hop(G₁) via `DispatchQueue.main.async`. The projection's first value arrives as a main-actor job (`observeSlots` → `applyProjection`, `:626–636`) — FIFO on the same main queue as the hop. If the fetch completes between `attach` and that display pass, the delivery job sits AHEAD of hop(G₁): the next drain runs `renderFull` (`storageDidEdit` bumps to G₂, `:1002`) and `applyFocusSeeds` parks the reveal (`:1931`), then hop(G₁) runs `consumePendingReveal` (`:2858`) with no display pass in between — the text view's frame is still the pre-fill height (the record's own measurement: *"the text view's FRAME is still the pre-fill height, so `JumpPrimitive`'s scroll range … is a couple of dozen points"*), the caret is not visible, `jump` clamps at `docHeight − viewport ≈ 24–48`, and the park is cleared (`:1940`). The following display pass sees G₂ ≠ delivered G₁ and schedules hop(G₂), which finds nothing parked. Landing short — *"puts your cursor in the right place but doesn't move you there"*. The record's "a geometry generation always bumps first and the hop always arrives" is true; what it misses is that a hop for the EARLIER generation may already be queued behind the park. Fix (one line each side): stamp the park with `overlayGeometryGeneration`; the hop consumes only when its captured `generation >= pendingRevealGeneration`. Pin (red on this tree; needs `overlayLayoutDidSettle` and `pendingRevealOffset` test-visible, the `pendingIntentTask` precedent): attach → `overlayLayoutDidSettle()` (hop for G₁ queued) → `applyProjection(slots)` synchronously with a current-block fact far down the note (parks) → drain the main queue → `pendingRevealOffset != nil` (red: nil — consumed by the stale hop).

#### Findings, severity-ranked

**R2-1 · MAJOR · `App/Variorum/Variorum/Features/Editor/JumpPrimitive.swift:113–150` (`lineSpan`; the `offsetBy: clamped` at `:124`) + `:158–222` (`jump`; `:192`) + `Features/Editor/EditorViewModel.swift:1953–1977` (`consumePendingReveal`) + `:1992–1998` (`bareArrivalLanding`) · a landing at the NOTE'S VERY END — the bare arrival with the caret remembered at the end of the last block, the commonest resting place after writing — is never counted visible and the jump cannot correct, so the page is hauled to `maxScroll` (the last line at the viewport top, the typewriter room below) on every ⌘2 → ⌘1 from there; on a short note the whole note scrolls off except its last line. J18(2)'s accepted rule — "a landing whose caret is already inside the visible rect scrolls nothing" — is falsified at the document's end.** Mechanism: with no open tail `bareArrivalLanding` = `last.location + min(len, len)` = `index.documentLength` (`:1996–1997`); `landing > 0` (`:1887`) parks the reveal; at the settle hop `lineSpan(ofOffset: documentLength)` builds `target = location(offsetBy: documentLength)` — the document's END location — and TK2's `enumerateTextLayoutFragments(from:)` yields NO fragment for it (the end location is inside no element's range), so `span` stays nil (`:143`) and the visibility guard at `:1970–1974` is skipped; `jump(toOffset: documentLength)` (`:1976`) runs the same enumeration from the same location inside `JumpCorrectionLoop`'s closure, `targetMinY` answers nil, the loop returns `converged: false` after its first `scroll(to: estimate)` — and the estimate is `1.0 × textHeight`, clamped to `maxScroll = docHeight − clip`, which with the typewriter room is exactly "the last line at the top". Before the batch a bare arrival was always a block's START, so this road did not exist; the reveal that replaced `scrollRangeToVisible` does not handle the one landing that sits inside no fragment. **Measured (the scratch worktree):** a probe on the 250-paragraph rig seeded at the end — `seed 30891 · docLength 30891 · span nil · visible 8647.5…9366.5 · docHeight 9366.5 · room 702.0` while `lineSpan(ofOffset: 30890)` answers `(8647.1, 8664.1)`; and a THREE-block note entered as the bare arrival with the memory at the last block's end — `visible 72.0…791.0 · docHeight 791.0 · room 702.0 · span nil`: the text occupies 0…89 pt, the viewport shows the last line and 700 pt of room. Road: Write with the caret at the end of the last block → `updateCaretContext` reports `(last, len)` → ⌘2 → the pane goes live at `.offset(len)` = its END → ⌘1 → the lurch (on a long note the walk's warm anchor restore puts the page where she left it and the hop then moves it by up to a viewport; on a short note the note vanishes but for its last line). Reach: the bare arrival only — `WriteIntent.caretAtDocumentEnd` is never minted (grep: the declaration and its consumer), and the seed arm seeds block starts. **Pin (written and run in the scratch worktree; RED on this tree):** `LandingOffsetTests.aBareArrivalAtTheNotesEndTheViewportAlreadyShowsDoesNotScrollThePage` — three blocks; `registerDetail` + `noteFocusedBlock(last, v, postID, utf16Offset: lastRange.length)`; `EditorView(caretSeed: nil)` mounted in a window; after the settle `JumpPrimitive.lineSpan(ofOffset: index.documentLength, in: editor) != nil` and `scrollView.contentView.bounds.minY == 0`. Red: `span nil`, `minY 72.0`. **Fix (validated in the worktree — the pin green at `visible 0.0…719.0 · span (72.0, 89.0)`, and the landing family green: `LandingOffsetTests` · `CurrentBlockContinuityTests` · `PaneSurfaceTests` · `TakesLandingTests` · `JumpCorrectionLoopTests` · `BlocksArrivalMeasureTests` · `ReadArrivalMeasureTests` · `JumpAndUndoTests` · `BookOutlineLandingTests` · `CanvasArrivalTests` · `ReadLandingTests`, 47 tests / 10 suites):** resolve the document's END to the last fragment's last line in BOTH `lineSpan` and `jump` — enumerate from `clamped − 1` when `clamped == length && length > 0`, keeping `clamped` as the local offset handed to `FragmentLines.lineIndex(atLocalOffset:)`, whose past-the-last rule already answers the last line. The guard then sees the line and the jump converges (on the long note the last line lands at 8647.1 against `maxScroll` 8647.5 — the room's 17-pt shortfall, pre-existing and negligible).

**R2-2 · NIT · `App/Variorum/Variorum/Surface/PaneSurface.swift:225–234` (the flag's doc) + `:1003` + `Features/TOC/BlocksWorkbenchView.swift:856` · the doc's "it can never outlive the gesture that set it" overclaims: a read→read render KEEPS the flag by design (R1-2's refinement), so on a host whose click flips nothing it survives — the workbench panel's read pane of a LOCKED take (`isLive` stays false while `makeLive` moves the authority) keeps `clickBroughtPlace` armed until its next transition, and the panel is `.id`'d by block, not by lock state, so an in-place unlock then goes live keeping the click's place instead of the armed `.offset`/`.start`.** Benign (the click's place is arguably the better landing; the panel reports nothing; every reporting host flips on the click), so the mechanism is real and the consequence is nil — the comment is what is wrong. #### ROW 16 — MEASURED FIRST, AND IT IS REAL (not hollow)

The brief said *"TRACE FIRST — measure before believing"*, and the measurement **changed the fix**. The
brief's proposed remedy — *"run `ensureLayout(for: documentRange)` on the PANE after a SHRINKING edit
then remeasure"* — **is already what the shipped code does on every measurement**
(`PaneMeasurement.height` called it before reading), and it does **not** fix the row. Recorded because
the next reader would otherwise repeat the guess.

**The probe** (a live pane, 400 pt wide, 30 lines of prose; lines 6–30 deleted through the real
responder path — select + `deleteBackward`):

| turn | text | `usageBoundsForTextContainer` | `PaneMeasurement.height` | the pane's frame |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| mounted | 30 lines | 1223.0 | 1235.0 | 1235.0 |
| after the delete | 5 lines | 1189.0 | 1201.0 | 1235.0 |
| +1 turn … +6 turns | 5 lines | **1189.0 (unmoved)** | **1201.0 (unmoved)** | **1201.0 (unmoved)** |

So a five-line take kept a **1201-pt frame** — ~1000 pt of dead gap under it — and no number moved for
six main-queue turns. That is her *"empty gap… until you switch modes"* exactly: only a remount (a mode
switch) mints a fresh text container, and a fresh container starts its high-water mark over.

**The mechanism, named:** on macOS 26 `NSTextLayoutManager.usageBoundsForTextContainer` is a **HIGH-WATER
MARK for its container's life** — it grows and never shrinks. Two remedies were measured and BOTH
failed: the `ensureLayout(for: documentRange)` already in the measurement (1189 → 1189), and an explicit
`invalidateLayout(for: documentRange)` ahead of it (1189 → 1189). What tracks the text is the fragments'
own geometry: after the same deletion the last laid-out fragment's bottom read **198.0**, and after ten
lines were typed back it read **608.0**, while the property sat at 1189 throughout — so the ratchet is
one-way in BOTH senses (a pane that shrank could not grow back to an honest number either).

**The fix (ONE place — the one measurement brain, P-3):** `PaneMeasurement` reads the laid-out
fragments' own bottom instead of the property, falling back to the property when a document lays out no
fragment at all (the EMPTY document — the only shape where the two differ).

**Why it moves no converged pane by a point** — measured at steady state on eight shapes:

| shape | property | fragments |
|---|---|---|
| empty | 17.0 | 0.0 → falls back to 17.0 |
| one line | 17.0 | 17.0 |
| trailing newline | 41.0 | 41.0 |
| two trailing newlines | 58.0 | 58.0 |
| blank lines between paragraphs | 113.0 | 113.0 |
| one long wrapping line | 340.0 | 340.0 |
| 30 lines | 1223.0 | 1223.0 |
| 400 lines | 16393.0 | 16393.0 |

**Cost (P1, measured):** 0.58 ms vs 0.41 ms per measurement on a 400-line / 16,393-pt pane; 0.12 ms at
30 lines. `.ensuresLayout` does the layout the old call did; the added work is one frame read per
fragment, and a pane's document is ONE take by construction — the bound is the unit on screen, which is
the same P1 argument `PaneSurface.swift` already makes in its header for full-document `ensureLayout`.

**The pin:** `TakePaneMeasureTests.aPaneThatLosesMostOfItsTextShrinksWithinOneTurn` — mounts a live
30-line pane, deletes 25 lines through the responder path, and asserts the frame falls below a third of
its old height within ONE main-queue turn (plus a regrow arm, and two non-vacuity assertions). Beside it,
`aFreshPanesMeasurementIsUnchangedByRow16sFix` states the no-regression half (green on both sides
deliberately — it is not the pin). **RED-ON-OLD PROVED by behavioral revert** (the fragment read swapped
back for the property, on the committed tree): 2 issues —
`(short → 1201.0) < (tall / 3 → 411.67)` failed, and the regrow arm
`(pane.bounds.height → 1201.0) > (short + 200 → 1401.0)` failed. Green again on restore.

**For 13u2's kickoff (row 32, the general pane-stability trace — this row is item 1's member):** the
high-water mark above is a *class*, not a one-off. Anything in the app that sizes from
`usageBoundsForTextContainer` inherits it; the full-document EDITOR is the other surface kind and was
NOT examined here (out of this batch's one surface). 13u2 should start from that question.

#### ROW 6 — THE RING FOLLOWS THE PREFERENCE, THROUGH THE ONE COMPONENT

**Her U-7, verbatim:** *"the take mode always shows a ring around what piece you're editing — it doesn't
follow the preference on cursor being enough, wanting background wash, or ring"*; **U-19 (5)** confirms
the preference governs EVERY live pane.

**The traced mechanism (confirmed by reading, then by the revert):** `PaneSurfaceView.strokeColor`
returned `tokens.ring` whenever `isLive` and read no setting at all, while the Write surface has honoured
the three styles since R14/R22 (`BlockDecor.renderIndicator`, `:513–535`: `.off` draws nothing,
`.outline` strokes `tokens.ring`, `.background` fills `tokens.wash`). So the setting she chose was
honoured in Write and overridden in every pane.

**R22's reason, recorded as the brief requires — and PRESERVED, not overruled.** R22's ring exists
because *among many editable surfaces the ring is how you find the one live editor*, and that is exactly
what `.outline` still does: it is the shipped look, it stays the default, and it is what a pane wears
wherever the appearance push has not reached (the pins, the tutorial samples). What her ruling changes is
narrower and right: the pane may no longer OVERRIDE a preference she set — under `.off` the caret is
enough (her words), and under `.background` the live pane wears the same wash Write puts behind the caret
block, in the same token. Nothing about "find the live editor" is lost; the mark just obeys her.

**The shape — ONE decision, in the ONE component (P-3):** `PaneDecoration` (`Surface/PaneSurface.swift`)
is a pure `resolve(isLive:indicator:tokens:)` returning stroke · lineWidth · fill; `PaneSurfaceView`
renders it (a `.background` fill and an `.overlay` stroke on the SAME rounded shape, so the two can never
disagree and the composition's padding stays the card's). No host contains ring or wash logic.

**The push (the brief's road, followed exactly):** the style rides in beside `tokens` —
`PaneSurfaceView.indicator`, defaulting to `.outline` — the way `EditorAppearance` already carries theme
facts into the Write surface. A **View** reads the store; the component never pulls a setting. The
fallback is a decision, so it has exactly ONE copy: `ThemeStore.editingIndicator(of:)`, which every host
calls. **All TEN production construction sites in eight files pass it** (audited by grep after the
change): `TakesShared` (the cell both boards compose) · `TakesBoardView` ×2 (the mini card, the stack
card) · `CompareBoardView` ×2 · `CanvasView` · `WriteTakesPanel` · `ReadEditPane` · `BookIndexView` ·
`BlocksWorkbenchView`. Lenses reaches every pane through `TakesCellView`, so it needs no site of its own.

**The three hosts that drew their OWN ring now CONSUME the decision** (`PaneDecoration.hostRing`, nil ⇒
"draw the frame you draw at rest"): `ReadEditPane.swift` (the overlay the brief names), `BookIndexView`
(the same shape, found by grepping `tokens.ring` — the brief named only Read's), and
`BlocksWorkbenchView`'s row card (`ring : line` — the third, same grep). No second rule survives in the
app.

**Pins** (`PaneSurfaceTests`): `theLivePanesDecorationFollowsTheIndicatorPreference` (the three styles
plus the read-pane arm across all cases) · `aHostsOwnFrameConsumesTheSameRule` ·
`aPaneWithNoPushKeepsTheShippedRing` (the default is a decision, so it is stated) ·
`theIndicatorNeverMovesThePanesHeight` (mounted under all three — the decoration is a background and an
overlay, so it can never re-open the batch-12 clipped-take class one setting over).
**RED-ON-OLD proved by behavioral revert** (the pre-fix rule restored: the ring whatever the setting):
**3 issues** — `off → PaneDecoration(stroke: #3F7FD6FF, lineWidth: 1.5, fill: nil)` ≠ the resting
hairline; `background.fill → nil` ≠ `tokens.wash → #EEF0EAFF`; and `background.stroke == rest.stroke →
false`. Green again on restore.

**Stated honestly:** the three HOSTS' own frames are walked, not pinned — the rig cannot mount those
whole surfaces (KnownIssues' rig row; the brief's own "pin brains, walk faces"). The rule they consume is
pinned; that they consume it is a one-line read and a capture.

#### ROW 14 — THE CHOSEN BAR RUNS THE CARD'S FULL HEIGHT

**Her punchlist 11, verbatim:** *"the chosen green line doesn't go all the way down"* (image 6 —
`greenchosenlinedoesntgoallthewaydown.png`, which I read: the STACK style, wash on, block 4/8, a 581-word
chosen take whose card runs past the viewport while the green bar stops about a third of the way down).

**The traced mechanism:** `TakeCardFrame` drew the 3-pt bar as an HStack SIBLING of the content. A
flexible `Color` inside a stack is sized against the height the stack has RESOLVED — and beside a
`PaneSurfaceView` whose measured height publishes on a LATER main-queue turn (`PanePublisher`'s
deliberate deferral, and the A47b FRAME LEVER which moves the AppKit frame directly), the height the
stack resolved with is a previous one. The card's own background and border chase the settled content;
the sibling bar does not.

**The fix:** the bar is an `.overlay(alignment: .leading)` of the finished card (the brief's own
prescription), laid out against the card's resolved height rather than beside it, so it is the card's
height by construction however many turns the pane takes to settle. The content keeps its exact leading
inset (the 3 pt the bar's column used to occupy is now a `.padding(.leading, 3)`), so nothing moves.

**The geometry oracle** (`TakeCardGeometry`, the `LensesGeometry` DEBUG pattern one surface over): the
bar and the card each report their frame in the card's own coordinate space; the oracle keeps EVERY
report rather than last-one-wins, because a board draws many cards.

**MEASURED, both sides, by behavioral revert (the HStack sibling restored in place — no `git checkout`
this time):**

| arm | pre-fix | fixed |
|---|---|---|
| the real STACK board (her image 6's surface), tallest card vs tallest bar | **card 1246.0 · bar 1220.5** | **card 1246.0 · bar 1246.0** |
| a bare synthetic 40-line card, ten settle turns | equal | equal |

**Stated honestly:** the SYNTHETIC arm is green on both sides — a bare mount settles and the pre-fix
HStack catches up, so it states the law without catching the defect. It is kept for the law (a future
card composition that never reaches a board still owes it) and the arm that CATCHES the row is
`theChosenBarRunsTheWholeCardOnTheRealStackBoard`. The board arm compares MAXIMA, because the oracle
cannot say which bar belongs to which card; `max(bar) < max(card)` still means some card's bar falls
short, which is her report exactly.

**Pins:** `TakesCardHeightTests.theChosenBarRunsTheWholeCardOnTheRealStackBoard` (the pin) ·
`…theChosenBarRunsTheWholeHeightOfALongCard` (the law). Suites at this commit:
`TakesCardHeightTests` · `WriteTakesPanelTests` · `TakesBoardTests` · `TakesPresentationTests` ·
`TakesBoardSoakTests` — **38/5 green** (`WriteTakesPanel` composes `TakeCardFrame` too).

#### ROW 15 — THE FIRST BLOCK CAN BE MADE WHERE SHE WAS LOOKING

**Her punchlist 10, verbatim:** *"you should be able to make a first block there"* (image 3 —
`cantstartintakes.png`, which I read: an empty note in Takes, slot-split style, offering the line

**The traced mechanism:** the empty state of BOTH takes-shaped boards rendered one door — into Write —
and the article's own `＋ new block` door was gated on `!slots.isEmpty` (`TakesBoardView`), so it
appeared only once a block already existed. The CAPABILITY was never missing: `.addBlockAtEnd` is native
to the take family (`CapabilityRegistry`, availability `takeFamily`, which does not look at the block
count) and it is already on the bottom bar and the menu bar. What was missing is the DOOR on the surface
she was looking at — a P-2 shape: the one place a first block is wanted was the one place it could not
be made.

**The fix:** ONE shared face, `TakesEmptyStateView` in `TakesShared.swift` (that file's stated purpose —
the grammar both boards share, in one home, so two empty states can never drift). It renders
`TakesEmptyState.doors == [.newBlock, .write]`: the new-block door leads, wearing the SAME dashed
grammar the article's end-of-note door already wears (so the act reads as the one she knows), with
"Start writing (Write mode)" beside it, byte-unchanged in style. Both boards compose it; neither keeps a
copy.

**Copy truth (J8's rule).** The old line *"Nothing here yet — blocks are born by typing."* stopped being
the whole truth the moment a door here mints one, so it now reads **"Nothing here yet — make the first
block here, or start writing."**

second half already parks focus (`TakesChoreographer.parkFocus`) so the minted pane takes the ring when
its slot arrives — P3's ONE live pane through `PaneTextAuthority`, exactly as the brief requires. The
minted block is legal EMPTY (I10: one live variant, empty text), and 18c's Return rule makes it an
ordinary block from the first keystroke.

the real-click rig cannot mount a board (KnownIssues' rig row; "pin mechanisms, walk faces") ·
`bothBoardsRenderTheOneDoorList` · `theDoorMintsTheFirstBlockAndItsPaneTakesTheRing` (the act at the
model: one block, one live EMPTY variant, and the ring on its pane).

#### Rows 17 + 27 — FIXED (the CORE change committed alone, `9e75ded9`, ahead of its face)

**Row 17, traced myself.** `markPostsAsVersions` resolves each post's FIRST live block and mints the
`version_of` edge between them; a blockless post had nothing to anchor on, so it threw
`postHasNoBlocks` — on a note she had only just made. **Fix (U-19 (1), "a is good"):** the anchor is
MINTED in the same transaction — one ordinary block, one live EMPTY take, placed at the end. Nothing is
special-cased: it is the block a note's first Return would have made, and U-19 (2) governs it from then
on, so `unmarkPostsAsVersions` removes the LINK and leaves the block standing.

**Two consequences I decided and record as decisions, not omissions.** (a) The mint stamps
`last_touched_at` and never churn — AppSpec §9's structural rule, because a block appearing in the note
is restructuring it and restructuring must never reshuffle the meaningful sort. (b) It refuses under a
SEALED post, since minting a block is exactly what the seal freezes; the LINK itself stays free under a
seal, like tagging and adding to a reading, so a sealed post that HAS blocks marks as a version exactly
as before. No undo entry: `markPostsAsVersions` is the tags/locks class and its own inverse door is the
recovery.

**Pins:** `VersionOperationsTests.aBlocklessPostGainsAnEmptyAnchorBlockAndTheLinkLands` — RED on
`3730f39c` with `postHasNoBlocks`; it holds the minted block's shape, both-sides-blockless, the recovery
door leaving the block, and the touch-without-churn stamps. Beside it
`.theAnchorMintIsGatedByTheSealButTheLinkItselfIsNot`. The old suite's blockless-refusal clause is a
JUSTIFIED EDIT — its claim is what the ruling replaced. **`swift test` at that commit: 1495 / 162.**

**Row 27 — and a FINDING against the brief's designed shape.** The brief said *"`VersionActs.words`
gains the case; Compare's door uses it"*. `VersionActs.words` already HAS a `postHasNoBlocks` sentence,
it belongs to the note-MOMENTS family ("nothing in this note to save a version of yet"), and Compare's
peer door has never routed through it — it routes through `OpsRefusalCopy.message`, whose `default:`
printed `Refused: <enum>`. And after row 17 that error cannot arise on the link road at all. So the
live raw-error surface is a DIFFERENT one: **`postsAlreadyVersionLinked`** — pressing the row twice
printed the enum WITH BOTH POST UUIDs. Its inverse (`versionLinkNotFound`) has spoken since Sitting 9;
this was that pair's missing half. Both it and `postHasNoBlocks` (for the surviving copy roads — "make
outline note", duplicate-as-version) are worded in `OpsRefusalCopy`. `VersionActs` is untouched.

**Pin:** `CompareBoardTests.theVersionsDoorSpeaksInWordsAndLinksABlocklessNote` — both halves end to end
through the real door. RED on `9e75ded9` with 3 issues (the raw dump). Its row-17 half re-measured by a

#### Row 10 — FIXED · **THE HYPOTHESIS WAS WRONG, and that is the row's finding**

The trace guessed the title field's all-digit prompt (the note's date) made AppKit read it as a
verification-code field. **It does not.** One Sonnet lookup (the CLAUDE.md exception, read-only):
on macOS 26 the "Fill code · From Messages" suggestion is **time-and-focus based and content-agnostic**
— Apple's documentation of the opt-out key states every text-input-capable field in every Mac app is
eligible while Messages or Mail has detected a one-time code, a field has focus, and under three
minutes have passed (hence the same popover reported over spreadsheet cells and terminal emulators).
No documented signal reads a placeholder. **So the brief's API-free fallback — the date as a `Text`
behind an empty-prompt field — would have changed nothing.** There is no per-field opt-out.

**Fix:** the one documented opt-out, `NSAutoFillRequiresTextContentTypeForOneTimeCodeOnMac` (macOS 26+,
default NO). With it YES only a field annotated `.textContentType(.oneTimeCode)` is offered the
suggestion; Variorum annotates that nowhere, and credential AutoFill (`.password` / `.newPassword` /
`.username` in the auth views) is a separate mechanism, untouched.

**MEASURED, because the delivery road is not obvious:** an `INFOPLIST_KEY_<name>` build setting for
this key is **silently dropped** — Xcode's generated-plist road only carries key names it knows
(verified absent from the built bundle). The target therefore gains a PARTIAL `Info.plist` that Xcode
merges its generated keys over (`GENERATE_INFOPLIST_FILE` stays YES). Verified by diffing the built
bundle's key set against the installed Release bundle: **a strict superset — no generated key lost.**

**Pins:** `OneTimeCodeAutoFillTests.theBundleRequiresAnExplicitContentTypeForOneTimeCodes` (red before
the plist; it pins the value's TYPE too, since a string "YES" is not what the system reads) and
`.noFieldInTheAppClaimsToBeAOneTimeCodeField`, which states the key's one cost — a code field added
later must be annotated. **Not walkable by me: triggering a fresh SMS code is hers.**

#### Row 13 — FIXED · **and the column's fit math had to follow**

**Traced myself.** Two mechanisms in one function. `header()` padded `groupPadding + rowPadding` while
sitting INSIDE groups that already pad `groupPadding`, so its words landed 12 pt inboard of the rows
beside them (measured: 32.0 against 20.0). And its 22-pt box with the text bottom-aligned and nothing
under it left the words touching the first row's wash (measured gap: **0.0**). **Fix:** a header inside
a padded group pads `rowPadding` only — exactly the edge `rowChrome` gives its content — and its row is
the column's own 30-pt pitch with 6 pt below the words.

**The consequence I chased rather than left:** `SidebarLayout.groupHeaderHeight` (22) is what the column
BUDGETS per headed group in its compress-or-not math. A header drawn at 30 against a budget of 22
under-counts the chrome by 24 pt at three groups — a column that fails to compress when it should, and
silently. The constant moves to 30 and `SidebarView.headerHeight` READS it, so the two can never drift.
`fewRowsNeverCompressInAShortWindow` is a justified edit with its claim intact (it described "five areas
alone" while taking the default three headed groups, and passed on 17 pt of slack the growth consumed;
the combination it asserted is unreachable — a rail alone is seven rows).

**Pin (red-on-old):** `ShellChromeTests.theSidebarHeadersSitOnTheirRowsEdgeWithAirBeforeTheWash` — BOTH
headed groups through a real `RootView` mount, since the defect was one rule wrong in one place and
would return the same way. RED with **4 issues** (12.0 pt of misalignment and 0.0 pt of air, twice);
green at 20.0/20.0 and 6.0. **21 / 3.**

**Coordination kept for 18d batch 1:** `SidebarGeometry.railGroupHeight` still publishes the rail
group's measured height, and the header rule above is the one its note box inherits.

#### Row 9 — FIXED (the geometry pinned; the z-order and the cursor are the walk's)

**Traced myself — three mechanisms, not one.** (1) The grip was a 9-pt `.overlay` on the 1-pt line, so
it was not a layout participant and had no frame of its own. (2) The detail is the HStack's NEXT
sibling, so it drew and hit-tested AFTER the divider and took every point right of the line — about four
points were reachable, on the sidebar side only. (3) The cursor came from `.onHover` +
`NSCursor.push()`, which loses to the text view's own cursor rects the moment the mouse moves inside the
grip — that is her *"sometimes the I looking pointer"* — and the push/pop pair could be left unbalanced
besides.

**Fix:** the grip is a ZStack SIBLING of the line at 14 pt, centred on the seam; the divider carries
`.zIndex(1)` so the seam hit-tests above the detail; and the cursor comes from an AppKit cursor rect
plus a `.cursorUpdate` tracking area (`SeamCursor`), whose view returns nil from `hitTest` so clicks and
the SwiftUI drag pass through untouched. Nothing is pushed, so nothing can be unbalanced.

**Pin (red-on-old):** `ShellChromeTests.theSeamsGripIsWideCentredAndReachesIntoBothSides` — RED under an
in-place revert to the overlay shape: grip `(206.0, 52.0, 9.0, 792.0)` against a line at x 210 — nine
points wide, reaching only the sidebar side. Green at `(203.5, 52.0, 14.0, 792.0)`, seven points into
each side. **The z-order and cursor halves are the walk's, and say so here:** a pushed `NSCursor`
against a text view's cursor rects is not something a mounted view can be asked about.

**AND THE WALK FOUND MY FIRST FIX'S CURSOR HALF DOES NOT WORK** (`9bee2a16`). Three cuts, each captured
on the running build, all kept in the file's own comment so the next reader does not repeat them:
(1) `.onHover` + `NSCursor.push()` — the I-beam wins back on every mouse-moved event (captured, four
points from the seam); (2) an AppKit representable owning a cursor rect and a `.cursorUpdate` tracking
area — with `hitTest` nil the I-beam STILL won (a view outside the hit-test chain gets neither), and
taking the hits and the drag produced the plain ARROW, never the resize cursor, because `NSHostingView`
manages the pointer for its own subtree; (3) **SwiftUI's own `.pointerStyle(.columnResize)`** (macOS 15+,
target 26) — captured showing the column-resize pointer exactly where the I-beam used to win. The DRAG
stays SwiftUI's; re-walked after the rewrite, a drag started five points INSIDE the detail moved the
seam from 300 pt to 230 pt (pixel-probed x 600 → 460).

**A build-log finding carried in that commit:** the row-10 partial plist had joined the synchronized
source folder's Copy Bundle Resources phase and Xcode warned the target was copying its own Info.plist
into Resources. Moved to `App/Variorum/VariorumInfo.plist`; verified after — zero warnings, the key
still `true` in the built bundle, no stray `Resources/Info.plist`.

#### Findings, severity-ranked

**[MAJOR] · `App/Variorum/Variorum/Surface/PaneSurface.swift:101–110` (the fallback) + `:73–85` (the
claim it rests on) · row 16's fix leaves the EMPTIEST case of her own gesture unfixed, and the doc
states the opposite as fact.**

*Mechanism, traced from the batch's own two measurements and the code in front of me.*
`extent(of:)` returns `bottom ?? layoutManager.usageBoundsForTextContainer.height` — the ratcheting
property is the fallback whenever the enumeration yields no fragment. The record establishes both
halves of the trap itself: (i) *"the EMPTY document … lays out no fragment at all"* (the steady-state
table's first row: `empty | property 17.0 | fragments 0.0 → falls back to 17.0`), and (ii) the
property *"is a HIGH-WATER MARK for its container's life … it grows and never shrinks"* (1223 → 1189
after 25 of 30 lines went, unmoved for six turns). Put together: a take that is emptied **completely**
— select the rest and delete, or backspace through the last character — lays out zero fragments,
takes the fallback, and reads the container's tallest-ever height back. The pane does not merely fail
to shrink; it shrinks as she deletes and then **jumps back to ~1223** when the last character goes.
That is her punchlist 13 (*"delete a lot of text from a take… empty gap… until you switch modes"*) at
its endpoint, inside the row the batch reports FIXED.

The doc's justification is falsified by the record's own finding: *"the EMPTY document … while the
property still reports one empty line's 17 pt; the fallback below keeps that shipped number"* (`:81–
85`) is true only of a container that never laid out more — which is exactly the container the
fallback is not needed for. For the container the fallback IS reached on in use, the property is the
high-water mark the fix was written to escape.

*Pin that would prove it (red on the current tree):* in `TakePaneMeasureTests`, beside
`aPaneThatLosesMostOfItsTextShrinksWithinOneTurn` and on its exact rig — mount the live 30-line pane,
select the WHOLE document and `deleteBackward`, pump one turn, assert `pane.bounds.height` is within a
line or two of a fresh empty pane's (≈ 17 + insets) rather than the 30-line height. **Stated honestly:
this is the one link I could not measure read-only** — whether an EMPTIED (as opposed to born-empty)
TK2 document really enumerates zero fragments. The record measured the born-empty case; if an emptied
container keeps one fragment for its empty paragraph the pin is **green on both sides and this finding
is hollow**, and I would rather say that here than have the ladder say it. One run decides it.

*Fix shape if red:* stop letting the ratchet be the fallback — take the property only when the layout
manager has never laid out (or gate on `documentRange.isEmpty` and return the typography's own empty-
line height), so the fallback can never hand back a number the text has outgrown.

**[MAJOR] · `App/Variorum/Variorum/RootView.swift:462–467` · `:474–476` · `:736–746` · `:748–750` ·
the parked `blockTarget` is never cleared by the `openHere` doors — CONFIRMED, and batch e adds a new
way to park one. (This is J29 (a), confirmed with the mechanism the adjudication asked for — and its
proposed one-line fix is wrong.)**

*Mechanism, traced end to end.* `open(_:blockID:in:)` (`:736`) parks `blockTarget =
BlockTarget(containerID:blockID:)` when a block is named and **nils it otherwise** (`:743`);
`adopt(_:in:)` (`:462`) — which is all `opener(_:)`/`openHere` does (`:474–476`) — never touches the
field. Nothing else in the file assigns it (`blockTarget` appears at `:59`, `:741`, `:743` only), so a
park is **never consumed and never expires**: `target(for:)` (`:748`) keeps answering for that
container id forever. The consumers re-land it on every mount — `PostDetailView(initialBlockID:
target(for: postID))` with `.id("\(postID)#\(target(for: postID) ?? "")")` (`:634`, `:637`) and
`PoolDetailView` the same (`:666`, `:667`).

Concretely, and in one view: the Library's block hit parks a target (`:601`, `onOpenBlock` →
`open(picked, blockID:)`); the Library's ordinary row (`:600`, `onOpen: openHere`) then re-enters that
same note without clearing it, so the caret lands on the old block instead of the caret her note
remembers. Every `openHere` door has the same exposure — the Shelf (`:594`), the Library (`:600`),
Pool posts (`:612`), the folder (`:643`), Recovery (`:674`, `:677`) and Archived (`:683`). **What this
diff changes:** batch e's card door now parks a target for a POOL container (`:626`), a shape that
never parked one before — open a snippet card (parks `(poolX, B)`), go anywhere, come back to that
group through Recovery's `openPool` (`:677`) or the folder/Library road, and the caret lands on the
clicked-an-hour-ago snippet. That directly contradicts row 42/U-20's ruled promise ("every door into
Write lands at the remembered caret"), which 17o batch b shipped two batches ago.

*The record's proposed fix is wrong as written.* R-9 says *"it is one line (`blockTarget = nil` inside
`adopt`)"* — but `open` **sets** the target and then calls `adopt`, so clearing inside `adopt` would
erase every park at the moment it is made and delete the Stage C landing road entirely. The correct
one-liner is on the other side of the pair: `opener(_:)` becomes
`{ destination in open(destination, blockID: nil, in: pane) }` (`:474–476`), which is the same
navigation plus the nil the road already knows how to write.

*Pin that would prove it (red on the current tree):* the field is `@State` on `RootView`, so the honest
pin is a DEBUG oracle on the parked target (the round's own `SidebarGeometry`/`ShellGeometry`
pattern) read from a `PaneMountTests`-shaped mount: open note X at block B through the block door,
navigate to Y through `openHere`, return to X through `openHere`, and assert `target(for: X) == nil`
(and, on the same mount, that the editor's landing is the remembered caret, not B). Red today at the
first assertion.

**[MINOR] · `App/Variorum/Variorum/Surface/PaneSurface.swift:96–100` · the new per-fragment walk is
justified by a sentence that is false for half the brain's call sites — two of them are WHOLE-POST
surfaces, one of them per-keystroke.**

*Mechanism.* The doc argues P1 holds *"for the reason this file already states: a pane's document is
ONE take by construction, so the bound is the unit on screen."* By grep, `PaneMeasurement.height` has
four production call sites, and only two are panes: `PaneSurface.swift:1241` and `:1440`. The other
two are full-POST documents — `Features/ReadTier/ReadPostViewModel.swift:263` (the read tier's
`remeasure`, one post) and `Features/Editor/EditorView.swift:559` (`InlineEditorSurface`'s
`remeasure`, the book-view inline editor), and the second one is wired to
`NSTextStorage.didProcessEditing` (`:539–549`), i.e. it runs **once per keystroke**. The old body read
one property after `ensureLayout`; the new one reads a frame per fragment, so the added work at those
two sites is O(fragments in the post) per edit — by the batch's own numbers ≈ 0.4 µs/fragment
(0.58 ms vs 0.41 ms at 400 fragments). This is not a NEW P1 class (the old `ensureLayout(for:
documentRange)` was already document-scaled there, and `InlineEditorSurface`'s per-edit remeasure is
a recorded measured cost) — it is an amplification of one on a typing path, plus a justification that
tells the next reader the site set is something it is not.

*No red-on-old pin exists for this and I say so* — nothing behaves wrongly; the traced degradation is
the per-keystroke cost at `EditorView.swift:559` and the false premise in the comment. Fix: state the
true call-site set (two panes, two whole-post surfaces) and hand 13u2 the measured question the record
already opens (*"the full-document EDITOR … was NOT examined"*) with these two sites named.

|---|---|

What the widening does NOT reach is the finding below.

#### Findings, severity-ranked

**[MAJOR] · `App/Variorum/Variorum/Features/Takes/PostDetailView.swift:458–460` +
`App/Variorum/Variorum/RootView.swift:641` · `:673` + `App/Variorum/Variorum/ShellRouter.swift:62–80`
· the park is not ONE-SHOT, and a re-mount is not a navigation — so U-20/row 42's promise is still
breakable, by the same mechanism the round just spent a MAJOR on.**

*Mechanism, traced end to end on the post-fix tree.* The fixed rule is *"a navigation expires the
park"* — `adopt` clears, nothing else does, and **nothing clears it on consumption**. So after
`open(.post(X), blockID: B)` the park `(X, B)` stands for as long as she stays in X. Meanwhile the
landing is applied by `PostDetailView.onAppear` — `if let initialBlockID { jump(to: initialBlockID) }`
(`:460`) — which fires on **every mount**, and `RootView` re-mounts that view whenever the pane stops
being the live one: `paneDetail` renders `PostDetailView` only `if live` (`RootView.swift:639`), and
`live` is `PaneMount.kind(of:focused:windowIsKey:) == .live`, i.e. `windowIsKey && pane == focused`
(`WorkspaceNavigation.swift:90–92`). **Neither input is changed through `adopt`.** Pane focus moves
through `router.workspace.focus(pane)` (`RootView.swift:657`, `:722` — the read-cheap tier's own
click-to-focus door); window key-ness moves through `WindowRegistry`.

Concretely, two ordinary roads:

- **Split.** Library block hit lands note X at block B in pane A (park `(X, B)`); she moves her caret
  into block 1; she clicks into pane B; pane A goes read-cheap and its `PostDetailView` is gone; she
  clicks back into pane A — it re-mounts with `initialBlockID: target(for: X) == B` and `onAppear`
  jumps her to block B again, not the caret she left.
- **Two windows.** Same park in window 1; window 2 becomes key, so window 1's pane goes read-cheap
  (the sticky key gate); back to window 1 — same re-jump. Each window has its own `ShellRouter`, so
  the park is right there waiting.

This is a RESIDUAL of MAJOR-2, not a regression the fix introduced: pre-fix the park never expired at
all, so both roads were already broken and worse. But the fix's stated rule reads as if the class is
closed (*"so 'the park expires' needs no second mechanism and no door can forget"*,
`ShellRouter.swift:65–69`), and it is not — the doors that forget are the ones that are not doors.

*Pin that would prove it — RED ON THE CURRENT TREE (this is a new finding, so red-on-old is not the
test; red-on-HEAD is):* on `ShellLandingMountTests`' exact rig, after step 2 (the caret remembered in
block 1), split with `router.openBeside(.post(noteY.id))` — or simply
`router.workspace.focus(.secondary)` then `router.workspace.focus(.primary)` — and re-assert the last
expectation: the editor's selection is `blockOneStart + 4`. It is `blockThreeStart` today, and
`router.landing(for: noteX.id)` is still `"…007"`.

*Fix shape (the reviewer's, for the orchestrator to arbitrate):* make the park a one-shot the mount
CONSUMES. The obstacle is that `target(for:)` also keys the view's identity
(`.id("\(postID)#\(target(for: postID) ?? "")")`) precisely so a NEW park for the container
re-creates the editor — so consuming it inside that same identity would loop. The shape that does not:
give the park a monotonically increasing generation on `ShellRouter`, key the `.id` on the generation
rather than on the block, and have the landing consumed (`router.park(nil)`) once applied — a second
park for the same container still bumps the generation and still re-lands. A cheaper variant, if the
identity coupling is wanted kept: leave `.id` alone and have `PostDetailView` consume through a
closure after `jump(to:)`, accepting one extra body pass.

#### 17o c/d/e round 2 — the orchestrator's arbitration (same-model flow)

- **MAJOR (the park is not one-shot; a re-mount is not a navigation) — CONFIRMED → batch e.** The mechanism is exact: `adopt` is the only clearer, `.onAppear`'s `jump(to: initialBlockID)` re-fires on every mount, and `RootView` re-mounts the note whenever the pane stops being live (pane focus through `workspace.focus`, window key-ness through `WindowRegistry` — neither passes `adopt`). U-20/row 42 is the spec. Fix shape: the park is SPENT when it lands — consumed on the mount that applies it (the router's `target(for:)` becomes a take, or the mount clears it after the jump), so a later re-mount of the same note lands at the remembered caret; `adopt`'s clear stays as the navigation rule. Pin: the reviewer's — `ShellLandingMountTests`' rig plus one `focus` round-trip, red on the current tree.
- **MINOR-1 ("order is the fix" has no pin) — CONFIRMED → batch e, in the same pass.** Fold the landing into `adopt(_:in:landing:)` so a reversed order cannot pass green (`open` is private; the pins reach `router.park` and the detail views directly today), and pin it through the real `open` road.
- **MINOR-2 (NIT-2's liveness JOIN is a behavioural delta with no pin) — CONFIRMED → batch d.** A core pin: a live placement over a tombstoned block → the anchor is the live empty block (minted), never the dead one, and the `ensureUnlocked` refusal; red-on-old against the inline copy.
- **MINOR-3 (27 of 35 `.fixedSize()` sites carry no `lineLimit`) — CONFIRMED AS A CLASS, RECORDED, not patched in the ladder (J32).** The reviewer is right that two-of-29 is not a fix and that P-8's letter is wider than its provenance (the b6dae25 class was an UNLIMITED text inflating a window's min-height probe). **MAJOR (the park is not one-shot; a re-mount is not a navigation) — CONFIRMED and FIXED.**

The reviewer's trace held at every step, verified myself before touching anything: `adopt` was the only
clearer; the landing is applied by `.onAppear`'s `jump(to: initialBlockID)`, which fires on every mount;
and `RootView` re-creates the detail whenever the pane stops being live — `PaneMount.kind` is
`windowIsKey && pane == focused`, and pane focus moves through `router.workspace.focus` while window
key-ness moves through `WindowRegistry`, neither passing a navigation door.

**The park is SPENT when it lands.** The shell's mount calls `router.spendLanding(for:)`, and the
detail's view identity keys on a **per-container landing GENERATION** (`ShellRouter.landingGeneration(for:)`)
rather than on the parked block — the reviewer's shape A. That is what makes the spend safe: a NEW park
bumps the generation and re-creates the editor (so "open it again, at another block" still re-lands
her), while spending one does not, so the spend cannot rebuild the view it just landed. A container she
never opened at a block sits at generation 0 forever and its identity never churns.

**One thing I got wrong first and am recording because the comment now carries it:** `.onAppear` has to
sit **below** the `.id`. Above it, the modifier wraps the identified child and keeps its own lifetime
across an identity change, so it never fires again — the first cut sat there, the park was never spent,
and the pin caught it (2 issues). Measured, not reasoned.

merely untaken; `open(_:blockID:in:)` is a one-line forward, and `ShellRouter.BlockLanding` gains the

#### Findings, severity-ranked

**[MINOR] · `App/Variorum/Variorum/ShellRouter.swift:88–91` (`park`'s RULE ONE) + `:100` (`func park`) ·
`App/Variorum/Variorum/RootView.swift:470–476` · round 2's MINOR-1 fix is structurally right for the road
it fenced and its doc claims MORE than the fence delivers — "no door can express 'park, then navigate'"
is false while `park(_:)` is module-visible, and the ladder's own pins are the proof.**

*Mechanism, traced on the post-fix tree.* The fold is real and I checked it: `adopt(_:in:landing:)`
(`RootView:461`) clears-and-installs in **one statement** (`:477`), `open(_:blockID:in:)` is a one-line
forward (`:773`), and `ShellRouter.BlockLanding`'s failable init decides which destinations can hold a
landing — so **a caller that goes through `adopt` cannot express the wrong order.** What the doc then says
is wider: *"`RootView.adopt` calls this on every navigation, in one statement, so **no door can express**
'park, then navigate'"* (`ShellRouter:88–91`), echoed at `RootView:474–476` (*"makes the wrong order
**UNEXPRESSIBLE** rather than merely untaken"*).

`park(_:)` is **internal** — no `private`, no `fileprivate` — on a class every view in the module holds
(`RootView` takes `router` as a parameter; `paneDetail`, `openBeside`, the palette and the chips all speak
to it). So `router.park(ShellRouter.BlockLanding(containerID:blockID:)); adopt(dest, in: pane)` is
expressible today, in one file, by any door; it compiles, it silently deletes the landing (`adopt`'s
`park(nil)` runs after), and **the suite stays green — because the two `ShellLandingMountTests` pins park
exactly that way themselves** (`ShellLandingTests.swift:213`, `:318` — `router.park(...)` called directly,
with a comment saying it is "performing the two halves `RootView.open(_:blockID:)` performs"). The one pin
that drives the real door (`ShellLandingDoorTests:420`) goes through `blockNamingDoor` → `open` → `adopt`,
so it holds `adopt`'s order and nothing else.

*Traced degradation.* This is the identical shape round 2 raised, one layer out: 18d batch 1 is named in
this file's own comments as the next editor of the sidebar/shell, and a next author who reads `park`'s
doc concludes the ordering class is structurally closed, reaches for `router.park(...)` from a new door
(the natural thing to do — it is the router's public-looking verb, and the tests model it), and loses the
landing with every pin green. The guarantee that exists is *"no door **that navigates through `adopt`**
can express it"*, which is a convention over `adopt`'s callers plus one pin — strictly stronger than round
1's two statements, and strictly weaker than the sentence.

*No red-on-old pin exists for this and I say so* — nothing behaves wrongly today (I re-ran the three
`ShellLanding*` suites plus `ShellChromeTests`: **8 tests in 3 suites passed**). It is a claim-versus-code
finding, and it is exactly the class this ladder has now spent three dispositions on (round 1's MINOR-3
`mastheadWidth` doc, round 2's NIT-1 stale line numbers, round 2's NIT-2 `resolveTitles`).

*Fix shape (the reviewer's; the orchestrator's to route).* Either **(a)** make the sentence true — narrow
`park(_:)` to the one production caller (`private` plus a `#if DEBUG` seam for the two mount pins, the
`blockNamingDoor` pattern the same fix pass already established two members up), which also removes the
tests' modelling of the wrong shape; or **(b)** make the doc true — say *"no door that navigates through
`adopt` can express it; `park` itself is the primitive `adopt` is built from, and a door that calls it
directly is outside the fence"*, at both sites. (a) is the one the round-2 finding's own argument
("structure over test, which is cheaper and stronger") points at.

**[NIT] · `App/Variorum/Variorum/RootView.swift:660–664` · the comment that exists to stop the next reader
repeating the implementer's own measured mistake gives the instruction INVERTED against the source it sits
in.**

The line reads *"**BELOW the `.id`**, deliberately and measured: a modifier **ABOVE it** wraps the
identified child, so it keeps its own lifetime across an identity change and never fires again — the first
cut of this line sat there and the park was never spent."* In view-tree terms that is exactly right
(`.id(…)` is applied last, so it identifies the subtree containing `.onAppear`, which is therefore
re-created and re-fires). In the **source text a reader is looking at**, `.onAppear` (`:665`) sits
**above** `.id` (`:671`) — so a reader who follows the words literally moves `.onAppear` to the line below
`.id`, which is the broken arrangement the comment was written to prevent. Two vocabularies (tree depth
vs. line order) are inverted with respect to each other in the one place this batch already got wrong once.

*Bounded, and I say so:* `ShellLandingMountTests.aRemountAfterAFocusRoundTripLandsAtTheRememberedCaret`
catches the wrong arrangement (the record's own number: 2 issues), so the hazard is a wasted debugging
cycle, not a shipped defect. Fix: say it in one vocabulary — *"`.id` comes LAST in this chain, so it
identifies the `.onAppear` above it and a new identity re-fires the spend; moving `.onAppear` after the
`.id` makes it outlive the identity and it never fires again (measured — the first cut sat there)."*

**[NIT] · `App/Variorum/Variorum/ShellRouter.swift:136–145` (`static var blockNamingDoor`) +
`App/Variorum/Variorum/RootView.swift:315–317`, `:778–785` · a process-global DEBUG closure is published by
every `RootView` mount and cleared by exactly ONE of the eight mount sites in the test target.**

*Mechanism.* `publishBlockNamingDoor()` runs in `RootView`'s `.onAppear` (`:315`) and assigns
`ShellRouter.blockNamingDoor` — a `static var` — a closure capturing that shell (its `session`, its
`router`, its `@State` boxes). Eight `RootView(` mount sites exist across six test files (`PaneSplitTests`,
`BookAscentTests`, `ShellChromeTests` ×3, `WindowsTests` ×2, `WorkspaceNavigationTests`,
`ShellLandingMountTests` ×2); **only `ShellLandingDoorTests` clears it** (`ShellLandingTests.swift:409`).
So after any other mount the global holds a closed window's shell, and `ShellLandingDoorTests`' settle
(`:413–417`) waits for `blockNamingDoor != nil` and `#require`s **whatever is there** without checking it
is its own — a stale door would navigate a foreign router and the test's own assertions would go red.

*MEASURED, and it does not reproduce today — recorded honestly rather than filed as a defect.* I ran the
adverse order myself: `xcodebuild test … -only-testing:VariorumTests/ShellChromeTests
-only-testing:VariorumTests/ShellLandingDoorTests -only-testing:VariorumTests/ShellLandingMountTests` →
**`✔ Test run with 8 tests in 3 suites passed after 1.516 seconds`**, with `ShellChromeTests`' three shells
and `ShellLandingMountTests`' two mounting first. The reason is that `NSHostingView` + `makeKeyAndOrderFront`
runs the first SwiftUI update (and therefore `onAppear`) synchronously enough that the static already holds
the CURRENT shell before the settle's first predicate evaluation. That is a property of AppKit's mount
timing, not of the code, so what remains is a latent order dependence plus a DEBUG-only retention of one
closed window's shell. Fix (cheap, either): key the publication (`[windowID: door]`) or have the door pin
set `ShellRouter.blockNamingDoor = nil` **before** it mounts, so it can only ever take its own.

**[NIT] · `App/Variorum/Variorum/Features/Takes/TakesBoardView.swift:1509–1530` (`TakeCardGeometry`) · the
only APPEND-ONLY oracle in the round; every other DEBUG probe here is last-write-wins.**

`TakeCardGeometry.record` does `reports.append(…)` and nothing prunes it; `reset()` has exactly two callers,
both in `TakesCardHeightTests` (`:594`, `:634`). The probe is installed on every take card and on every
chosen bar (`takeCardGeometryProbe(.card)` / `(.chosenBar)`), driven by `.onGeometryChange`, so in a DEBUG
build — the dev-store build the walks use — the array accumulates for the process's life, and `latest`/
`tallest` scan the whole history. Contrast the diff's six other new oracles (`ShellGeometry`,
`SidebarGeometry.headerTextFrames`, `BookIndexGeometry`, `MastheadGeometry.titleFieldFrame`/
`titleLabelFrame`, `PostDetailOracle.titleShown`, `TakesEmptyStateDoors`), every one of which stores a
single value or a keyed last-write.

*Honest bound on the rate:* `.onGeometryChange` fires on CHANGE, and a card's frame in its own coordinate
space changes only when the card resizes (a line-count change, a width change, a take added or removed) —
not per keystroke. So the growth is slow, and this is a NIT, not a leak worth a fix pass. Fix if touched:
keep a last-per-slot plus a running max (which is all `latest`/`tallest` ask for), or `reset()` on the
board's appear.

`EditorViewModel`, no lifecycle touched. **The shadow itself is PRE-EXISTING and is now a KnownIssues
row** (owner 13u2's pane/mount-stability family) with what it still exposes written out — the quit,
lock and adjacent-block doors read `active` too; nothing is known to be lost there (the quit door
flushes per POST through `QuitFinalizeRegistry`, not per editor), but they are answering about the
wrong object. Capture `03-FINDING-before-the-bar-came-from-the-caret.png` is the before.

index's arrival seed calls `select(…, report: false)` deliberately: `indexAnchorPostID` is W21's CARRY

different one, so it got its own report (`BookViewModel.noteIndexSelection`) written by every

#### Piece B — the brains, before any pixel

Four pure pieces, none of which needs a window:

- **`Core/Views/NoteBox.swift`** — `NoteBoxState.from(selected:live:)` (the three states; **LIVE WINS**,
  so the box never says *"edit here"* about a note under the caret), `NoteBoxIdentity` (what the BOOK
  knows: title · chapter · place in the reading order — the sidebar never re-derives it), `NoteBoxFacts`
  (words · blocks · fanned blocks · the two stamps), and `NoteBoxCopy` (the header, the empty state's two
  lines, the door, the editing mark, and the four line-builders).
- **`Features/BookView/BookNoteBox.swift`** — the book's own rule: which modes show the box (every
  EDITING mode, never Read) and which note each one POINTS AT. **It deliberately disagrees with
  `BookAnchor`**, and the file says why: the anchor always falls back to the standing place (a carry
  that lands nowhere is indistinguishable from one that never happened), so under it a book she has ever
  put anywhere points at that note forever — and *"no note selected"* would be a state the box could
  never reach. Her ruling names that state outright, so the box's rule has no fallback.
- **`SidebarLayout.railGroupHeight(rowHeight:railRows:)`** — THE ONE MEASUREMENT the rail and the box
  share (her *"measured to take up the same amount of room"*). A function of the DRAWN row height, not a
  constant, because the column compresses; a constant would hold at the generous pitch and lie in a short
  window, which is the silent drift row 13 fixed one layer down.
- **`NoteBoxCopy.takesLine` — hoisted** from `BookOutlineRows.gutterLine`. U-17 retires the details
  gutter and state 2 carries the facts now, so the function moved to its only remaining consumer rather
  than being called across a feature boundary (the hoist-at-next-touch rule). Claim unchanged; **its pin
  moved with it** (`BookOutlineFacesTests.theGutterCarriesTheTakesFactAndNoWordCount`, a justified edit).

still a day; an autosave moves the edited stamp; the saved stamp follows a savepoint on an UNRENDERED
take and on any block; a deleted block's moments leave the note's stamp with the cascade.

The fix asks a different question: `EditorRouter.editing`, published by the model that computes a caret context (which needs a live text view and a landed projection) — an assignment in `updateCaretContext` and its clear in `teardown`, beside the `active` assignment that always lived there; no mount, projection, identity or lifecycle change. **The shadow itself is PRE-EXISTING** → a KnownIssues row (owner 13u2; the quit, lock and adjacent-block doors read `active` too — nothing known lost, the quit door flushes per post — but answering about the wrong object). The 18d Opus reviewer weighs the touch; the round-end Fable pass sees it again.
- **A canon delta owed at 18d's close:** AppSpec §12's book-mode paragraph — the DETAILS GUTTER the Act 10 correction round put on Outline's right is RETIRED by U-17; the note's controls live in the sidebar's box in every book editing mode (this record is the source).

  the mockup's other two properties.

  inspector column at 280 pt and a generous target is C-7's standing rule.
  **(c)** on a take row the **stamp truncates** (`deleted Sep 8, 20…` in Study, `deleted s…` in
  Terminal) while the clock never does — that is row 63's shipped two-slot rule, not new: the lead is
  the truncatable slot, the clock is the uncompressible one, and the take row carries two buttons. The
  kind label moving the block's name UP off that line gave the lead MORE room than it had, not less.

**What the batch does NOT touch:** `Sources/VariorumCore/Sync/` (zero), the schema (zero — the memory
is local-only view state, no migration, no lockstep event), `BlockRangeIndex`/`EditorTypeView`, and

#### The store — the decision the brief left open

**UserDefaults, not a local-only table.** The count does not argue: ONE key per note per surface
family, `surfaceSize.outline.<postID>` / `surfaceSize.flow.<postID>`, ~40 bytes each — exactly the
shape the app already ships twice (`currentBlock.<postID>` from the Act 10 correction round's batch C,
`postMode.<postID>`). A thousand notes browsed in both surfaces is ~2,000 keys ≈ 80 KB. A table would
owe a migration for view state that a `defaults delete` should be allowed to end. **No schema commit
is owed and none was made.**

**The write cadence — the batch's real design.** `remember` is called at GEOMETRY cadence (every
report while a surface loads, and on every keystroke's height change in the Outline's live editor,
`followsShrinks: true`), and `UserDefaults.standard.set` costs ~100 µs a call on this machine
(measured at 17o batch b). So `remember` writes the SESSION record only; the disk is written by
`persist`, called from `StableSurface`'s existing `settled` announcement (ladder fix 2, R2-2) — the
moment a surface has held one size for the settle interval, adopted it and dropped its reservation.
A settle that re-adopts the size already on disk writes nothing (`written` cache). This is why NO
change to `StableSurface` was needed: the seam it needed already existed, and the Outline simply
started passing the `settled:` closure it had been leaving nil.

**The typography stamp (the brief's "voice + fontSize").** The app has NO font-size setting — grepped:
`font_size`/`textSize`/`fontScale` appear nowhere in `Sources/` or `App/`. What actually moves a note's
height at the SAME width is the resolved typography: the voice (Terminal's 14-pt monospace ↔ Study's
16-pt Iowan) and inline comments (a strip's room per paragraph). So each record carries `w|h|fingerprint`
and a record whose fingerprint is not the current one is refused exactly as a record at another width is.
Two fingerprints, one per key space, because the two surfaces are typed by different things:
`EditorTypography.fingerprint` (fontName-pointSize-paragraphGap, derived from `Resolved` itself so a
future dial moves it for free) for the Outline, and `FlowHeightEstimate.fingerprint` (`page-16-13-6`)
for the flow, whose page is a fixed system serif and voice-independent — one app-wide stamp would have
dropped every remembered story on a voice switch that moved nothing on that page.
