#### The finding the walk turned up (recorded, not fixed — and why)

**`BookView.surfacePlaceholder` reads the memory's HEIGHT and does not compare its WIDTH**
(`BookView.swift`, the `surfacePlaceholder` property). The walk made this visible: the height an
expanded note holds in the first frames after a relaunch comes from the PLACEHOLDER (the row starts
`nearViewport == false`), not from `StableSurface`'s reservation — so the width refusal I pinned governs
the reservation, while the first frame stands on the record's height whatever width it was taken at.
**Left as it is, deliberately, and now said out loud in the code:**
- A placeholder is a GUESS, and the alternative when it refuses is `unmeasuredSurfaceHeight` (800 pt).
  A 20 000-pt note measured at 696 pt is ~28 000 at 500 pt — the mismatched memory is wrong by the width
  ratio; the fallback is wrong by twenty-five times. Refusing would make the guess strictly worse.
- The place a wrong width must never be believed is the RESERVATION, and it refuses there
  (`stableSurfaceWidthTolerance`, ladder R1-1) — pinned twice in this batch, once on a persisted record.
- The record's TYPOGRAPHY *is* checked for the placeholder (`SurfaceSizeMemory.size` refuses a foreign
  stamp), because there the fallback is the honest answer: another voice's height is not a better guess,
  it is a different note. Walk step 4 shows exactly that fallback happening.
- The asymmetry is PRE-EXISTING (the Outline's placeholder never compared width; the flow's one brain,
  `FlowHeightEstimate.honestHeight`, does — R2-1 — because the flow HAS an estimate to fall back to and
  the Outline has none). Persistence makes it reachable across launches as well as across a mid-session
  resize. If the ladder wants it closed, the honest shape is a width for the Outline column reported ONCE
  by the column (never per row — that is a geometry observer per row, P1/P3) and consulted here; it is a
  small change and I did not make it, because on the argument above it would degrade the guess.

  (the cadence, counted) · `.aPersistedMemoryIsCorrectedByTheSettleInBothDirections(stored:)` (400 and 120,

  Not a bug-class row (`HERS (ruled)`), so no red-on-old is owed; the pre-fix behaviour is quoted from
  the diff above and pin 1 states it beside the new one.
- **DEFERRED — none.** **DISMISSED AS HOLLOW — none.**
- **PROVISIONAL — none, and no QUESTIONS entry is owed.** Everything decided here was decided by §5.4's

#### THE SCOPE CALL, FIRST (the orchestrator's question 1)

**J34's `EditorRouter.editing` touch is NOT the editor seam. This round stays with Opus.** The change is
two guarded assignments — `EditorViewModel.swift:2861–2863` (in `updateCaretContext`, above the existing
body) and `:527–529` (in `teardown`, beside the `active` clear it mirrors) — publishing a `weak var` on
`EditorRouter` (`EditorRouter.swift:40`). It touches no mount, no projection, no `BlockRangeIndex`, no
`EditorTextView`, no identity attribute, no undo registration, no lifecycle, and no default's meaning; the
briefs' own seam list (`BlockRangeIndex`/`EditorTextView`, custody/keychain, `Sources/VariorumCore/Sync/`,
a default's meaning) is untouched, and `git diff --name-only` confirms the only `Sources/` file in the
whole range is the additive `Queries/NoteStamps.swift`. What the touch DOES create is a second
"which editor" answer beside `active`, which is MINOR-1 below — an architecture finding, not a seam.

#### Findings, severity-ranked

**[MAJOR-1] · `App/Variorum/Variorum/Features/Tutorial/TutorialSeeder.swift:929–932` (and `:958–959`) ·
the field guide teaches the control 18d batch 2 retired.** The lesson "the tray & the Trash" says, verbatim:
*"The tray has two sections. Archived holds… Leaving holds everything of this note's that is counting down —
the blocks it deleted, the takes deleted on their own **(folded away until you open them)**, and any original
riding a family's countdown."* Batch 2 retired both facts: there are no stacked SECTIONS (a segmented
`Leaving · Archived` choice — `TrayPanel.viewChoice`), and there is no FOLD (`takesDisclosure` and
`RecoveryCopy.trayTakesDisclosure` are gone; the takes are a filter chip carrying their own count). The
later paragraph at `:958–959` still routes Delete Now to *"the Leaving **section** of a note's own tray."*
**Mechanism:** she opens Help ▸ the field guide (or restores the tutorial, which re-seeds this exact text),
follows it to the tray, and looks for a disclosure triangle that no longer exists under cards that are no
longer stacked under headers. **This is the row-44 class the 18f ladder already routed as a real fix** (that
row's own note: *"MUST land before her restore act at the round's end (the restore re-seeds the lesson)"*),
and P-6 makes the tutorial the executable spec. Batch 2 fixed the one adjacent copy line it met
(`BlockHistoryPane.swift`, *"choose Leaving ▸ takes"*) and did not sweep the seeder. **Pin (red-on-old):** a
tutorial copy-truth assertion in the `Tutorial*Tests` spine — the tray lesson's paragraphs contain neither
`"two sections"` nor `"folded away"`, and name the tab words `RecoveryCopy.trayLeavingTab`/`trayArchivedTab`
and the `takes` filter; RED on `86f01d64` (both strings are in the seeded text today), green after the
rewrite. **Fix:** rewrite the two paragraphs to the shipped control (two views at the top, one shared
`all · blocks · takes` filter, every card naming its kind), and replace "the Leaving section" with
"Leaving" wherever the seeder routes to it (`:903`, `:958`, `:1180`, `:1187`).

**[MAJOR-2] · `App/Variorum/Variorum/Core/Views/SideColumn.swift:210–217` · the shared draggable seam still
carries ledger row 9's defect, and batch 3 put it on three more boundaries.** `SideColumn`'s grip is a 9-pt
`Rectangle` in an `.overlay` of a 1-pt divider, with no `zIndex` and with `NSCursor.push/pop` on `.onHover`.
Ledger row 9 — her *"the hitbox for adjusting the size of the left bar… too small… sometimes the I looking
pointer"* — is exactly this shape, and 17o batch d fixed it for `ShellSplit` **three ways**
(`Workspace/ShellSplit.swift:59–67, 90–91, 104–110`): the grip became a real layout participant at
`gripWidth = 14`, a ZStack sibling at `.zIndex(1)` in the HStack so the seam hit-tests **above** the detail,
and the cursor became an AppKit cursor rect (the record says the `onHover` road took three cuts before it was
abandoned). **Mechanism, traced:** in an `HStack` later siblings sit above earlier ones, and for a LEADING
column the order is `sidePanel, divider, content` — so the ~4 pt of the grip that overhangs into the content
is hit-tested by the content, which in Outline is the prose column and in Read is the page; the usable grip
is ~5 pt of the 9. **Evidence from this round's own record:** R-12's walk, verbatim — *"An earlier attempt
read 190 after a relaunch — a drag whose press had **missed the 9-pt grip**, so nothing was ever written."*
That is row 9's symptom, observed by the implementer, on the new boundary. The class is pre-existing in
`SideColumn` (its trailing consumers had it), but batch 3 tripled the exposure — the book navigator, the
book Index's chapter panel and the note Read contents column — after her U-13 asked for exactly this
boundary to be draggable. **Pin (red-on-old):** a geometry oracle on the seam, the shape row 9's own pin
took — `SideColumn` reports its GRIP's frame (it already reports the divider's, via `onDividerFrame`) and a
mount asserts the grip is ≥ `ShellSplit.gripWidth`, centred on the line; RED on `86f01d64` (nothing reports
a grip frame, and the overlay is 9 pt), green after. **Fix:** port `ShellSplit`'s three-part fix into
`SideColumn` — grip as a sibling at `.zIndex(1)`, `gripWidth` shared with `ShellSplit` (one constant, the
hoist rule), the AppKit cursor rect in place of `onHover`.

**[MINOR-1] · `App/Variorum/Variorum/EditorRouter.swift:16, 40` + `notes/KnownIssuesAndTechDebt.md` (the new
row) · two routers of record, and the row's "nothing is known to be lost" is scoped narrower than it reads.**
The app now answers "which full-document editor is current" two ways: `active` ("the last text view to
attach") and `editing` ("the model that computed a caret context"). Exactly one caller — the note box
(`RootView.swift:570`) — uses the correct one; the other five keep `active` and therefore answer about the
Outline's projection-less shadow whenever a note is focused there. The KnownIssues row argues the quit and
lock doors are covered (`QuitFinalizeRegistry` registers per POST) and concludes *"nothing is known to be
lost."* **Two doors are lost, and the row should say so:** (a) `EditorCommands.swift:554/559` —
`previousBlock`/`nextBlock` (⌃⌘↑/↓) call `active?.jumpToAdjacentBlock(±1)`; enablement is attachment-level,
so the menu items are ENABLED and the act silently does nothing while an Outline note is focused, which is a
straight P-2 break (*"a rendered door either performs the act… or delivers the operations layer's real
refusal"*); (b) `ShellActions.swift:246` — `exportCaretBlock` guards on `editor.caretBlockID`, nil on the
shadow, so it SPEAKS the unavailable note instead of exporting the block she is in. Architecturally, P-3's
doctrine is one authority per question; this diff adds a second field with no stated rule for which door
reads which, and the two doc comments that were supposed to state it are both wrong (MINOR-6). **No
red-on-old pin is owed for the doc half** (it is documentation truth). For the code half the honest pin is a
mount asserting `editorRouter.editing` and `editorRouter.active` name the same model in Write and disagree in
Outline — green on both sides today, i.e. hollow as a bug pin; the real fix is the shadow, which is 13u2's.
**Fix (this round):** amend the KnownIssues row to name the two doors as ACTUALLY wrong today, and put one
sentence at `EditorRouter.active` saying which question each field answers and that `editing` is the one a
door about "the editor she is writing in" should ask.

**[MINOR-2] · `App/Variorum/Variorum/RootView.swift:308` + `Theme/EditorTypography.swift:49, 83` ·
on a cold launch in the STUDY voice the persisted surface memories are refused for the first frames — U-12's
"perfect after the first time" degraded to "perfect after the theme lands".** `EditorTypography.current` is
initialised to the TERMINAL resolution (`EditorTypography.swift:49`) and is corrected only by
`.onChange(of: theme.settings)` — **without `initial:`** — so it is not adopted until `theme.start()` has
loaded settings that DIFFER from the default. `SurfaceSizeMemory.size` calls `fingerprint()`
(`EditorTypography.fingerprint`) on every read (`SurfaceSizeMemory.swift:156–158`). **Mechanism:** launch in
Study → `RootView` renders → `BookView`'s Outline rows realize → `surfacePlaceholder` reads
`rememberedSurfaceSize` → the disk record's stamp is `IowanOldStyle-Roman-16-8`, the live stamp is still
`.AppleSystemUIFontMonospaced-Regular-14-7` → refused → the row falls back to `unmeasuredSurfaceHeight`
(800). Worse, a geometry report arriving in that window calls `remember`, which stamps the SESSION record
with the Terminal fingerprint (`:163–166`) and so clobbers the loaded disk record in `records`; a `persist` inside
the window would then write a Terminal-stamped record over her Study one. Everything converges once the
theme lands and the surface settles, so nothing is corrupted — but the first frame after every Study launch
is the picture her ruling exists to remove, and the batch's walk only ever demonstrated the refusal
deliberately (step 4 planted a TERMINAL stamp) and never tested "a Study record, honored on a Study launch".
**Pin (red-on-old):** seed a Study theme in the store, drive `RootView`'s theme adoption, and assert
`EditorTypography.fingerprint` names Iowan BEFORE the first `SurfaceSizeMemory` read — or, mechanism-level and
window-free, assert that `EditorTypography.current` equals `resolve(voice: loaded.voice, …)` immediately after
`theme.start()` returns. RED today (it equals the terminal default until an `onChange` fires). **Fix:** adopt
the resolved typography where the settings LAND (an `initial: true` on that `onChange` plus adoption at
`theme.start()`'s completion), or make `SurfaceSizeMemory` answer nil rather than "refused" until the voice is
known.

**[MINOR-3] · `Features/Library/SidebarView.swift:740, 741, 746` and `Features/Editor/CommitBar.swift:827` ·
four new SINGLETON DEBUG oracles, added into the exact class this round measured as broken under Swift
Testing's parallel suites.** R-12's own record: *"the three DEBUG geometry oracles were single statics, and
Swift Testing runs SUITES in parallel — a book mounted by `BookIndexEditingTests` landed in the same static as
mine (measured: four chapter rows in a two-chapter book…)"*, and batch 3 keyed its three by id. Batch 1
(earlier in the same letter) added `SidebarGeometry.noteBoxFrame`, `noteBoxHeaderFrame` and the
`noteBoxFaces` COUNTER, plus `CommitBarGeometry.mounted`, all process-global and all unkeyed. `.serialized`
on `NoteBoxGeometryTests`/`NoteBoxCompositionTests` orders tests WITHIN a suite; it does not stop another
suite mounting a `SidebarView` or a `CommitBar` concurrently. **Mechanism:** (a)
`aBookOpeningPutsTheBoxOnTheColumnSayingNoNoteSelected` waits on `noteBoxFrame != nil && noteBoxFaces["empty"] > 0`
and then compares that rectangle against a rail height captured from ITS OWN mount — a concurrent suite's box
satisfies both and the compare is meaningless; (b) `noteBoxFaces` is incremented on appear and decremented on
disappear, so a cross-suite increment makes `> 0` pass spuriously and SwiftUI's mount-before-unmount ordering
can leave it at 2 or −1 within one suite; (c) worst, `theBooksEditingSurfacesMountNoBarOfTheirOwn` — **the
U-17 retirement's own pin, the one measured red at 3 issues** — asserts `mounted["horizontal"] == 0`, which any
concurrently-mounted `EditorView` in another suite turns red. **No red-on-old pin applies** (this is harness
hygiene, not product behaviour) and I label it as such rather than let the ladder call it hollow. **Fix:** key
all four by the subject's id, as batch 3 did (`[String: CGRect]` / `[String: [String: Int]]`), and give the
suites live UUID generators; then answer the orchestrator's standing question — **yes, the sweep is worth a
row**: `MastheadGeometry`, `TakeCardGeometry`, `CompareGeometry`, `LensesGeometry`, `SidebarGeometry`,
`BlocksWorkbenchOracle` belong in a KnownIssues row under 13u2's harness family beside the c/d/e cap's own
oracle row, because the failure mode is a green pin that proved nothing.

**[NIT-2] · `Features/Tray/TrayPanel.swift:486` · a reveal overwrites her session tray memory.** `applyReveal`
calls `select(view:)`/`select(kind:)`, and both call `remember()`, which writes `AppSession.trayViewMemory`.
So opening the tray from a lineage door doesn't just land on the revealed row's view — it becomes "the last
view" for the rest of the session, and the next unrelated ⌫ press opens there instead of where she last chose.
§5.4 says *"Remembered: the last view and filter per session"*, which reads as her choice, not a landing.
One line: set `view`/`kind` directly in the reveal arm without `remember()`.

**[NIT-3] · `Core/Views/SurfaceSizeMemory.swift:180` · `forget` has no production caller.** Its stated
precedent, `CurrentBlockMemory`, is evicted from production code (`CommandRouter.swift:225`,
`currentBlocks.forget(postID:)`); this one is called only from `SurfaceSizeMemoryTests.swift:352`. So a
deleted or purged note leaves one or two `surfaceSize.*` keys in UserDefaults forever. Harmless at the record's
own arithmetic (~40 bytes), and view state a `defaults delete` may end — but the asymmetry with the precedent
it cites is worth one line either way (wire it to the same occasion, or say at the code why it does not).

#### Considered and cleared (traced, so the next reader does not re-raise them)

- **The walk's `.deleteTake` observation — the board's context door IS wired; a pin for it would be green on
  both sides, i.e. hollow.** I traced the whole path: `TakesBoardView.washedCell:791` builds `TakesCellView`,
  which passes `menuItems: { menuSpecs(resolved:) }` (`TakesShared.swift:185`) into `PaneSurfaceView`, which
  forwards it (`PaneSurface.swift:936`) to `PaneSurfaceRepresentable`, which sets `view.variorumMenu` in BOTH
  `makeNSView` (`:1032`) and `updateNSView` (`:1060`), and `PaneTextView.menu(for:)` (`:361–380`) inserts the
  specs ABOVE the inherited menu. `menuSpecs` contains `TakeCardMenuCopy.deleteTake` (`TakesShared.swift:276`)
  and can never return empty. So the board IS a `.contextMenu` renderer for `.deleteTake` by construction, the
  registry's `doors: [.contextMenu, .surface]` (`CapabilityRegistry.swift:427`) is satisfied on this surface
  and not merely by the union, and P-1 is not violated. The walk's *"only AppKit's own text menu"* is
  unreproduced by reading; the plausible remaining explanations are environmental (the right-click landing on
  the card's chrome/overlay rather than the pane's text view, or the cell falling to its `· · ·` gap branch
  when `resolvedTake` is nil). **Recommendation: do not open a row.** A mount pin asserting
  `PaneTextView.menu(for:)` carries the delete row would pass on the pre-batch tree too — the hallucination
  guard's own definition of hollow. If she sees it again, the evidence owed is a walk that records where the
  pointer was.
- **`BookView.surfacePlaceholder` standing on a remembered height without a width compare (batch 4's argued
  non-fix) — the argument holds; I set out to falsify it and could not.** The record's reasoning is sound in
  both directions: the reservation, where a wrong width would actually mis-lay the page, DOES refuse
  (`stableSurfaceWidthTolerance`, pinned twice here including once on a persisted record), and the placeholder's
  alternative is `unmeasuredSurfaceHeight` (800), which is wrong by ~25× where a foreign-width memory is wrong
  by the width ratio. The TYPOGRAPHY half is checked, which is the half where the fallback is honestly better.
  The asymmetry is pre-existing (the flow's `FlowHeightEstimate.honestHeight` compares because it has an
  estimate to fall back to; the Outline has none). One thing the record does not say and that the closeout
  should: the harm is asymmetric — a memory taken NARROW and used WIDE over-reserves and pushes the next
  chapter off screen (the walk's capture 04 picture, at a planted value), and that direction self-corrects in
  ~4 s at the settle. Accepted as recorded, not a finding.
- **The P39 refinement (question 2) — the composition is clean.** `BookView` publishes a VALUE and a CLOSURE
  upward (`onNoteBox`, `BookView.swift:44`); `RootView` composes (`noteBoxView`, `RootView.swift:555–589`),
  reads `session.editorRouter.editing` (a router it owns) and builds `CommitBar(model:axis:.box)` itself;
  `SidebarView` receives `var noteBox: AnyView?` (`SidebarView.swift:183`) and only RENDERS it. No feature
  constructs, holds, or calls into a sibling's view model; P39b (`WriteTakesPanel` → `TakesViewModel`) is
  untouched. The gate that keeps a stale report off the column is real and correct: `noteBoxView` re-derives
  the focused pane's showing book rather than trusting the stored report, and `adoptNoteBox` stamps CLEARS with
  their publisher so SwiftUI's mount-before-unmount ordering cannot erase the arriving book's box.
- **The leading column and `layoutPriority` (question 5) — respected, and the pin that would catch it rides
  green.** `SideColumn.body` puts `content()` into the HStack with only `.frame(maxWidth: .infinity)` and no
  container of its own, so Outline's `clickOutMargin · prose(.layoutPriority(1)) · clickOutMargin` HStack
  keeps deciding; the priority is applied OUTERMOST at `BookView.swift:1389` (after `.frame(maxWidth:)` and
  `.padding(.vertical:)`), which is the order batch 1's closing suite proved is load-bearing;
  `OutlineWritingSurfaceTests.outlineProseSitsOnWritesOwnMeasure` was re-run green in batch 3's closing run.
- **The tray's populations under the new filter (question 4) — byte-unchanged.** `TrayContents` is assembled
  from the four listings the model already held (`TrayPanel.swift:343–346`), `TrayFilter.rows` only SELECTS from
  them, `count` is defined as `rows(...).total` so a chip cannot advertise a size the list does not hold, and
  `putBackDeleted`/`putBackOriginal`/`putBackArchived`/`takeRow`/the purge confirm are unmodified. The two
  truncation lines are correctly re-gated to the cell that renders their rows. The archived · takes cell being
  empty by construction is honest (it names Block History), and `viewHolding` asks only the two block
  populations because a reveal names a block.
- **Zero `Sources/VariorumCore/Sync/`, zero schema, zero migration, no lockstep event owed.** Confirmed by
  `git diff --name-only ce6eb9cb..86f01d64` — the only `Sources/` files are `Queries/NoteStamps.swift` and its
  test. `SurfaceSizeMemory` and the three column widths are UserDefaults, local-only, never synced (S1–S5
  untouched); no default's meaning moved.

#### CLEAN BILL — load-bearing things I checked myself and found solid

- **`Queries.noteStamps` (piece A) — run, not trusted.** `swift test --filter NoteStampsTests` in this tree:
  `Test run with 5 tests in 1 suite passed after 0.105 seconds`. The query is one indexed read over the note's
  own rows (`Sources/VariorumCore/Queries/NoteStamps.swift:38–56`), returns nil for a missing or tombstoned
  container (the `containerHeader` convention SyncSpec §5 asks read sides for), and its `savedAt` correctly
  joins through LIVE variants and LIVE blocks and LIVE placements, so an unrendered take's savepoint counts and
  a cascade-tombstoned block's does not — exactly what the four pins claim.
- **U-17's retirement is complete and the dead code is gone, not parked.** `EditorView.BarPlacement.side`,
  `CommitBar.Axis.vertical` with `verticalBody`/`railPair`/the `bookSideRailCollapsed` preference,
  `BookView.outlineGutterWidth`/`outlineGutterSpacing`/`outlineFocusedRowWidth`/`gutterDetails`, the row's
  `meta` state and `BookOutlineRows.gutterLine` are all absent from the tree; the spread's editor
  (`SpreadBookView.swift:358`) and the Outline's focused row (`BookView.swift:1872`) both pass
  `.inSidebarBox`. `loadFacts`'s whole-note read is correctly gated on the COLLAPSED form

  is a function of the DRAWN row height, the column budgets the box as `railEquivalentRows` in both `rowCount`
  and `headedGroupCount`, and the box takes it as a fixed frame with an internal `ScrollView` — so the Open

  reads `editingOrActive`**, a new one-line accessor (`editing ?? active`) whose fallback keeps every
  door's behaviour outside the Outline byte-identical: a freshly attached editor that has not yet
  reported a caret is still the only editor there is.

  — a book in Outline, a note focused, then **the shadow reproduced deliberately**: a second
  `EditorViewModel` for the same post attaches a text view and takes `active`, exactly as the trace
  describes. The pin asserts the doors' own expressions — `editingOrActive` is non-nil and its
  `caretBlockID` is the block she is in (what Export ▸ This Block would name), and

*(the batch-4 implementer, resumed; TWO findings — MINOR-2 · NIT-3. One is CONFIRMED and fixed as

**MINOR-2 (a Study cold launch refuses the persisted memories until the theme lands) — CONFIRMED and
FIXED at `1a1bea5c`.** I traced it myself before touching anything, and the trace is slightly sharper
than the finding: `ThemeStore.start()` never RETURNS (it is an `AsyncValueObservation` loop for the app's
lifetime), so "adoption at `theme.start()`'s completion" has no such moment — the settings LAND at
`settings = value` inside the loop, once per arrival, and that is the only honest adoption point. The
old road was `RootView`'s `.onChange(of: theme.settings)`: a VIEW noticing, which is (a) one SwiftUI
update cycle later than the landing, (b) conditional on the loaded value DIFFERING from the compile-time
default — a store whose settings equal the default never fires it at all — and (c) absent entirely in any
host that runs the store without that view. **The fix, in three parts:**
- `EditorTypography` gains the one adoption door — `adopt(_ resolved:)` / `adopt(_ settings:)` and the
  `isAdopted` flag — and `applyVoiceChrome` routes through it (a surface taking a real voice IS an
  adoption). `RootView` keeps the markdown palette, which depends on the color SCHEME too and so is
  genuinely a view's question; its typography line is gone with a comment saying where it went.
- `ThemeStore.start` adopts at the landing. The store is the theme's authority; the adoption belongs to
  it, and it now happens for every arrival including the first, whatever the value equals.
- `EditorTypography.fingerprint` is `String?`, **nil until the voice is known**, and
  `SurfaceSizeMemory.remember` DROPS a report with no stamp. This is the finding's second half — the one
  that could destroy something rather than merely delay it: a geometry report in the window stamped the
  session record with the leading voice, overwriting the record loaded from disk, and the settle a second
  later wrote that guess over the height she measured in her own voice. Losing one early report costs
  nothing (the surface reports again as it loads; the settle decides in any case).

**Pins (both new, in `SurfaceSizeMemoryTests`):**
`theTypographyIsAdoptedWhereTheSettingsLandNotWhereAViewNoticesThem` — forces a known ADOPTED Terminal
state (so its failure cannot be an accident of whatever a parallel suite left in the process global —
batch 1's MINOR-3 class), writes `setThemeVoice(.study)`, runs `ThemeStore.start` in a task, waits for
the value to land, and asserts `EditorTypography.current == resolve(voice: .study, …)`; it restores what
it found. `aReportBeforeTheVoiceIsKnownNeitherStampsNorClobbers` — pure, its own defaults suite: the
first half REPRODUCES the old mechanism (a wrong-but-present stamp replaces her record and the settle
writes the guess to disk — green on both trees, it is the trace), the second half is the pin (with no
stamp, the report is dropped and her record survives the window in the very memory that saw it).

**NIT-3 (`SurfaceSizeMemory.forget` unwired) — the PREMISE is FALSE; fixed anyway, in the direction the
underlying observation points. `1a1bea5c`.** The finding's argument is an asymmetry with a precedent:
*"its stated precedent, `CurrentBlockMemory`, is evicted from production code (`CommandRouter.swift:225`)"*.
`:225` is the body of `CommandRouter.forgetCurrentBlock`, and **`forgetCurrentBlock` has no production
caller either** — `grep -rn "forgetCurrentBlock\|currentBlocks.forget"` over `App/Variorum` returns the
declaration plus **35 call sites, every one of them a test**, which is exactly what that method's own doc
names first (*"A pin's reset (or a deleted note)"*). So the two memories were in identical states and
wiring only mine would have CREATED the asymmetry the finding wanted removed. What the observation IS
right about survives the correction: a deleted note's keys outlive it, in both memories. **So the fix
goes at the shared occasion, not at my memory alone:** the new static `SurfaceSizeMemory.forgetPersisted(_:defaults:)`
drops a note's records in EVERY key space (`Namespace` is now `CaseIterable`, so a future key space is
covered by construction), and `CommandRouter.forgetCurrentBlock` — the app's one "this note's memories
go" door — calls it beside `currentBlocks.forget`. Static because the instances live on per-book
`BookViewModel`s the router cannot reach, and because the disk is the part that outlives the note: a live
model's session record for a note that no longer exists is asked for by nobody and dies with the model.
One occasion, every per-note memory; the next one is a line there, not a new eviction road. The instance
`forget` stays with its callers (the pins) named at the code.

**[MAJOR-1] · `App/Variorum/Variorum/Theme/EditorTypography.swift:71–74, 207–212` · MINOR-2's fix is
defeated by its own SECOND adoption door, inside exactly the window the guard was built for — and the
record's residual sentence is therefore not true on that path.** The fix's guard is
`EditorTypography.isAdopted`, whose doc says it tells "whether `current` is the STORE's answer or still
the compile-time default". Two doors set it: `ThemeStore.start`'s landing (correct), and
`NSTextView.applyVoiceChrome`, which calls `EditorTypography.adopt(chrome.typography)` on the argument
its host hands it. **Both hosts build that argument from the store's UNLANDED value:**
`EditorView.swift:72–74` and `ReadTier/ReadPostView.swift:47–49` are both
`themeStore?.settings ?? Queries.ThemeSettings()`, and `ThemeStore.settings` is initialised to
`Queries.ThemeSettings()` (`ThemeStore.swift:21`), whose `voice` is `.terminal`
(`Sources/VariorumCore/Queries/AppearanceQueries.swift:14`) — the exact compile-time guess. The store's
own value arrives from an async `AsyncValueObservation` started by `RootView`'s `.task`
(`RootView.swift:326`). **Mechanism, traced:** launch in Study with a text surface materializing in the
first pass (a restored Write note, or the Outline's read-cheap `ReadPostView` rows, which call
`applyVoiceChrome` at `ReadPostView.swift:152`) → `applyChrome` runs before the observation returns →
`adopt(terminal)` → `isAdopted = true` and `EditorTypography.fingerprint` is non-nil and WRONG → the
`guard let stamp` at `SurfaceSizeMemory.swift:180` no longer drops → `remember` stamps the session
record with the guessed voice and OVERWRITES the record `record(_:)` just loaded from disk
(`:223–233`), which is precisely the clobber the fix's second half exists to make impossible. The
disk half is reachable too, on the flow's own immediate-persist road:
`ReadingFlowView.swift:919–923` calls `memory.remember(...)` and then `settledHere()` →
`memory.persist(...)` **in the same turn**, so a guessed stamp is written straight over her record with
no settle interval to save it. **The honest bound:** which of two async reads wins is a race, so I
cannot promise the bad order on every launch — but a guard whose correctness depends on winning a race
is not a guard, and the batch-4 record's own residual (*"the window is now bounded by the theme's own
DB read … nothing can be written under a guess inside it"*) states the opposite of what this door
allows. The batch's walk cannot distinguish the two doors: she opened the Sherlock book by hand,
seconds after launch, by which time either door had adopted. **Pin (RED on the tree as it stands):** in
`SurfaceSizeMemoryTests`, seed her Study record; put the process global in the unadopted state
(`EditorTypography.isAdopted = false`, restored in a `defer` as the sibling pin already does); apply the
chrome an unlanded store hands out — `EditorTextView.makeInlineEditor().applyVoiceChrome(
EditorSurfaceChrome(tokens: Queries.ThemeSettings(), dark: false))`; then `remember` + `persist` a size
and assert her record survives in memory and on disk. Red today (adopted with a Terminal stamp, her
record gone — the `aReportBeforeTheVoiceIsKnownNeitherStampsNorClobbers` first half, reached through a
production door); green once the latch is fixed. **Fix:** let `applyVoiceChrome` keep writing
`EditorTypography.current` (surfaces still agree) but NOT set `isAdopted` — adoption belongs to the
settings' one authority, which is what the fix's own doc says — or carry an `authoritative` flag on
`EditorSurfaceChrome`, set only when the store has landed, and adopt on that. Whichever is chosen, the
residual paragraph in the batch-4 record should be re-worded to what remains true.

#### Findings, severity-ranked

**[MINOR-1] · `App/Variorum/Variorum/Theme/EditorTypography.swift:215–231` (`applyVoiceChrome`) +
`:125–130` (`fingerprint`) · round 2's MAJOR-1 closed the LATCH and left the VALUE the latch guards
writable by a drawing host — so a second window's un-landed `ThemeStore` can still make
`EditorTypography.fingerprint` non-nil AND WRONG, which is the state the fix exists to make
impossible.** The fix's rule is stated twice, as a rule: *"only the settings' authority adopts"*
(`:71–79`) and *"a claim made under a guess outlives the guess"* (`SurfaceSizeMemory.swift:173–175`).
But the stamp is not derived from the adoption — it is derived from `current`
(`fingerprint`: `guard isAdopted else { return nil }`, then `let resolved = current`), and
`applyVoiceChrome` still writes `current` unconditionally on every chrome application. **Mechanism,
traced:** the app mints FOUR `ThemeStore`s, one per window kind — `RootView.swift:144`,
`Workspace/NoteWindowView.swift:55`, `Features/QuickNote/QuickNoteView.swift:118`,
`Features/Settings/AppSettingsView.swift:38` — each starting its own observation
(`.task { await theme.start() }`) and each holding `Queries.ThemeSettings()` (voice `.terminal`,
`ThemeStore.swift:22`) until its own DB read returns. `isAdopted` is a process-global, monotone latch
already set by the FIRST store's landing. So: her Study main window is up and adopted → she opens a
note in its own window (`NoteWindowView` → `PostDetailView` → `EditorView`, or its read-cheap
`ReadPostView`) → that window's chrome is `themeStore?.settings ?? Queries.ThemeSettings()`
(`EditorView.swift:72–74`, `ReadTier/ReadPostView.swift:47–49`) = the Terminal placeholder →
`applyVoiceChrome` sets `EditorTypography.current` to the Terminal resolution while `isAdopted`
stays true → `fingerprint` hands out `.AppleSystemUIFontMonospaced-Regular-14-7` as if it were her
answer → `SurfaceSizeMemory.remember`'s `guard let stamp` passes and a Study-measured Outline height
is recorded, and `persist` (whose new guard only asks `fingerprint() != nil`) writes it to disk. Her
record is replaced by a mis-stamped one, which the next Study launch REFUSES — the U-12 degradation
round 1's MINOR-2 and round 2's MAJOR-1 both exist to prevent, arriving through the third door.
**Why MINOR and not MAJOR** (said plainly so the arbitration can weigh it): round 2's door was on
the ORDINARY launch path; this one needs a second window opened inside its own store's DB-read
window AND a surface reporting geometry into the stamp-bearing `.outline` memory in that gap — narrow,
and the damage is one launch's first frames of view state, never store truth. It is nonetheless the
same rule broken one step further along, and it falsifies `adopt`'s own new doc sentence, which says
the guess is now distinguishable from her answer. **Pin (red on the tree as it stands; designed, and
I did NOT measure it — see the machine note at the end):** in `SurfaceSizeMemoryTests`, adopt Study
(`EditorTypography.adopt(EditorTypography.resolve(voice: .study, inlineComments: false))`), seed her
record through a memory wired as `BookViewModel` wires it (`fingerprint: { EditorTypography.fingerprint }`),
then drive the PRODUCTION door — `EditorTextView.makeInlineEditor().applyVoiceChrome(EditorSurfaceChrome(tokens: Queries.ThemeSettings(), dark: false))`
— and assert `EditorTypography.fingerprint` is unchanged; the second arm replays the flow's
`remember` + `persist` and asserts her record survives in memory and on disk. Red today at the first
`#expect` (the stamp moves to the monospace), green after the fix. The window must be one statement
long and the globals restored before asserting (round 2's NIT-2). **Fix, one line + a doc:**
`applyVoiceChrome` writes `current` only while `!EditorTypography.isAdopted` — after adoption the
store's own `adopt` is the only writer, and every chrome the hosts build once their store has landed
carries exactly that value, so nothing visible changes on the normal path. (The alternative round 2
itself named — an `authoritative` flag on `EditorSurfaceChrome` set only from a landed store — is
larger and buys the same thing.)

**[MINOR-2] · `Features/Library/SidebarView.swift:735` · `RootView.swift:646–676` ·
`Core/Views/SeamGrip.swift:142–145` · the oracle-KEYING rule that rounds 1 and 2 each confirmed is
unfinished at three sites the round's OWN new pins read.** Round 1's MINOR-3 keyed the box's
rectangles and the bar's mount counter; round 2's MINOR-2 keyed the seam oracle and made
`SideColumn.subjectKey` required. Three holes of the same class remain, and two of them are read by
pins minted in this letter: **(a) `SidebarGeometry.railGroupHeight` is still an unkeyed
`CGFloat?`**, published by any `SidebarView` whose rail draws (`SidebarView.swift:568`), and BOTH box
geometry pins take their reference height from it — `NoteBoxMountTests.swift:166–180`
(`theBoxTakesTheRailGroupsOwnHeight`: nil it, wait for ANY non-nil, then compare the keyed
`noteBoxFrames[book.id]` against it) and `:375–401` (`aBookOpeningPutsTheBoxOnTheColumnSayingNoNoteSelected`,
same shape with no arithmetic guard at all). A concurrently mounted rail in another suite supplies
that number: at the same `generousRowHeight` the pin passes about another window (round 1's own
*"a green pin that proved nothing"*), at a COMPRESSED row height it goes spuriously red — so the
half of the compare the fix keyed is protected and the half it did not is not. **(b)
`RootView.paneSeamFamily` + `subject: "\(index)"`** — the pane seam's "subject" is the divider's
INDEX in the row, i.e. `paneDivider|0` for every split in every suite and every window, which is
exactly the per-host-constant shape round 2's MINOR-2 rejected (`SideColumnGeometry`'s `widthKey`);
`ShellChromeTests.swift:430` reads that key, and `ShellLandingTests.swift:297–338` mounts a real
`RootView` in a displayed window and opens a second pane, publishing into it. **(c)
`SeamGeometry.reset()` clears EVERY subject's entries**, so a suite that resets (`ShellChromeTests.swift:409`,
`OutlineRoomTests.swift:456`) can wipe frames another suite has already published — and
`onGeometryChange` only fires on CHANGE, so a wiped rectangle is never republished and the waiting
`#require` fails: keying does not protect against the reset. **No red-on-old pin applies** — this is
harness hygiene, not product behaviour, and I label it so rather than let the ladder call it hollow.
**Fix:** key `railGroupHeight` by the rail's post (the `noteBoxFrames` shape) and let the two mount
pins read their own; give the pane seam a real subject (the window's or the router's id, minted live
in the pin); make `reset()` take the subject it is resetting, or have each pin clear only its own
keys. All three belong in J41's owed oracle-sweep row either way, which is the orchestrator's to
carry.

**[MINOR-3] · `Core/Views/SideColumn.swift:21–22` and `:37` · `Features/BookView/BookView.swift:125` ·
`Features/ReadMode/ReadModeView.swift:143` · four live comments still describe the shipped seam as
a 9-pt grip with the old cursor road — the J8 copy-truth class round 1's MINOR-6 swept once and
MAJOR-2's fix re-created.** MAJOR-2 replaced the 9-pt `.overlay` with the shared `SeamGrip` at
`width = 14` and `.pointerStyle(.columnResize)`, and round 2's MINOR-1 finished the job at the fourth
seam. The component's own header says so; the HOSTS' prose does not: `SideColumn`'s header still
tells the next reader the divider *"carries the pane row's own drag grammar (a 9-pt grip, the resize
cursor — `WorkbenchSeam`'s, batch C)"* and that the leading edge brings *"the 9-pt grip"* with it,
`BookView` says the navigator's boundary carries *"the 9-pt grip, the resize cursor"*, and
`ReadModeView` the same. **Mechanism (the degradation, since no pin applies):** the next reader
measuring or moving a seam reads a number the app does not use, and the two files that DO say 14
(`SeamGrip`, `ShellSplit`) then look like the exception rather than the rule — the same failure
round 1 fixed by hand five comments at a time. **Fix:** four one-line edits naming `SeamGrip` and its
14 pt; the historical sentences at `RootView.swift:638`, `SeamGrip.swift:36` and `SideColumn.swift:228`
are correct as they stand (they describe what the shape WAS) and must not be swept with them.

**[NIT-1] · `Core/Views/SurfaceSizeMemory.swift:204–215` · `persist`'s new guard is justified by a
road that cannot carry the defect.** The doc says the promise matters because *"`FlowStoryRow`'s
empty-read branch calls `remember` and then `settledHere()` → `persist` in the SAME turn, so there is
no settle interval standing between a wrong stamp and the disk"* — but that road writes through the
FLOW memory, whose stamp is `FlowHeightEstimate.fingerprint` (`ReadingFlowView.swift:695`), a
compile-time `let ... = "page-\(…)"` that is never nil (or through `ownSizes`, the session-only
memory whose closure is `{ "" }`). The unknown-voice window exists only for the `.outline` memory
(`BookViewModel.swift:398`), which that branch never touches. The guard is right to exist — the
genuinely same-turn road is `StableSurface.report`'s own settle closure (`StableSurface.swift:206–211`:
`remember(size)` then `settled?()` → `persist`), which EVERY consumer uses including the Outline's —
so the fix stands and only its stated reason is wrong. **No pin is owed** (documentation truth).
**Fix:** one clause naming the settle closure instead of the flow's empty-read branch.

**[NIT-2] · `Features/Library/RecoveryView.swift:472–478` · the eviction door's `!item.isVersion`
exclusion is unexplained, and the KnownIssues row that enumerates what the door does not reach does
not name it.** `forgetLocalMemories` fires only for `kind == .note, !item.isVersion`; the doc beside
it explains Delete-Now-only and Empty-Trash-excluded at length and says nothing about versions, and
the new KnownIssues row lists Empty Trash, another device's janitor and a never-purged note as the
accepted leak. A version is a container with its own id, so if any per-note key can ever be written
under it the keys outlive the purge; if none can (a version's one home is Note ▸ Versions and it
mounts no `StableSurface`), the exclusion is right and the reason belongs at the code. **Fix:** one
clause either way — and if it is a leak, one word in the row.

**[NIT-3] · `notes/KnownIssuesAndTechDebt.md:53–56` · the new Outline-shadow row contains a blank
line, which ends the markdown table: the row's OWNER cell (`| **13u2** … |`) renders as body text
rather than as the table's third column.** CLAUDE.md's tracking rule is satisfied in substance (the
owner is named in the text), and the file already carries one earlier blank at `:43`, so this is
cosmetic and pre-existing in kind. **Fix:** fold the second paragraph into the same cell (the
file's other long rows do exactly that) or split it into a second row with its own owner cell.

#### Considered and cleared (traced, so the next reader does not re-raise them)

- **`AppSession.trayViewMemory` referencing a Mac-only type from `App/Variorum/Shared/` is NOT a
  cross-target break.** I checked this properly rather than trusting the batch's "iOS BUILD
  SUCCEEDED": `Shared` is a `PBXFileSystemSynchronizedRootGroup` in BOTH targets
  (`project.pbxproj:184` and `:254`) and `TrayViewMemory` is declared only in
  `Features/Tray/TrayFilter.swift:165`, which the phone does not compile — but the property sits
  inside `AppSession.swift`'s `#if os(macOS)` region (`:432`…`:542`), so the phone never sees it.
- **The pane seam's conversion really is layout-neutral.** `SeamGrip`'s own frame is
  `SeamGrip.lineWidth` = 1 (`SeamGrip.swift:93`), the same 1 pt `RootView.dividerWidth` already
  subtracts from the row's width budget (`RootView.swift:607`), and `.zIndex(1)` orders drawing and
  hit-testing without touching layout. The walked drag (seam + 4 pt inside the right pane, 1131 → 925)
  is the evidence for the half a rectangle cannot prove.
- **`StableSurface` cannot feed a guessed reservation back into a record.** `onGeometryChange` is
  applied to `content()` BEFORE `.frame(minHeight: reserved)` (`StableSurface.swift:177–180`), so the
  reservation never inflates the size the surface reports — the read-a-guess half of round 2's
  MAJOR-1 fix cannot become a written guess by that route, which is the first thing I tried to
  falsify about it.
- **`size`'s guess and `persist`'s cache do not fight.** `record(_:)` seeds `written[key]` with the
  stored string (`:268`), so a record merely READ under an unknown voice and then persisted after the
  voice lands short-circuits at `:218` — the disk keeps her own stamp rather than being rewritten
  under the new one.
- **The two caret doors read the right field and the fallback cannot reopen the blank-bar road.**
  `EditorCommands.swift:561–569` and `ShellActions.swift:242–252` go through `editingOrActive`;
  `RootView.swift:574` (the box's bar) still reads `editing` ALONE, so the shadow can never build a
  bar. `teardown` clears both fields (`EditorViewModel.swift:521–529`) and `updateCaretContext`
  claims `editing` only on a change (`:2856–2863`).
- **The tray's populations and counts are still defined by the rows.** `TrayFilter.count` is
  `rows(...).total` by construction (`TrayFilter.swift:126–128`), the reveal arm sets `view`/`kind`
  past `select` so a landing never becomes her remembered choice (`TrayPanel.swift:497–500`), and it
  is latched inside `if !loaded` (`:466`) so a later snapshot cannot move the tab under her hand.
- **`Queries.noteStamps` is one indexed read over the note's own rows** — `container_block` by
  container, `variant` by block, `commit_point` by variant — nil for a missing or tombstoned
  container, and it counts every live take's savepoint, which is what its four pins claim. Cost ∝ the
  note, never the corpus.

#### A MACHINE NOTE THE NEXT SESSION NEEDS (not a finding)

While measuring MINOR-1's pin in a scratch worktree I filled the boot volume: it was already at
**100% (418 GiB used of 460)** before this round's builds, and a cold `DerivedData` for the scratch
tree took the last of it — every write on the machine failed with `ENOSPC` until I recovered. **What
I did:** deleted `Build/Intermediates.noindex` from every `~/Library/Developer/Xcode/DerivedData/Variorum-*`
(regenerable; the NEXT Mac test run in the shared tree therefore rebuilds from scratch and will be
slow), deleted the scratch tree's own DerivedData, removed the scratch worktree and pruned. The
volume now reads **8.0 GiB free (99%)**, and `git worktree list` is back to `variorum` + `variorum-mobile`
with the shared tree clean. **Consequences for the orchestrator:** MINOR-1's pin is DESIGNED and
traced but NOT measured — I abandoned the run rather than spend the last GiB, and the fix pass should
measure it; and there are stale `DerivedData` trees for `/tmp` worktrees of dead sessions
(`Variorum-bgnjmuhyqftzrndfopqjtwnunidq`, `-cfoyfrajdavtgjepnirbkimhllxa`, `-dijrdsajvkduxjfjneufblvwflrw`,
`-etepviktypyfugcnvtvjpezglkbj`, `-ffanmtlfpjcfrxcbwxvlnqwnbbyz`, `-ghjhsouhamvzvzdbjjyappyjpzyj`,
plus two under `.claude/worktrees/`) whose paths no longer exist — several GiB that are the author's
to reclaim, not mine to delete unasked.

#### Findings, severity-ranked

**[MAJOR-1] · `App/Variorum/Variorum/RootView.swift:586–587` (`noteBoxView`'s `caretLabel`) · with
`EditorViewModel.swift:2854–2884` (`updateCaretContext`) and `SidebarNoteBox.swift:47` · THE SHELL
RE-EVALUATES PER KEYSTROKE while a book's note is live — the box's identity line reads the editor's
caret ordinal from inside the shell's body.**

*Mechanism, traced.* `RootView.noteBoxView` (`:559–589`) is evaluated inside the `sidebar:` closure
handed to `ShellSplit` (`:157–168`), which `ShellSplit.body` runs (`ShellSplit.swift:89`). When a book
note is live (state 3, `barModel != nil`) it reads `$0.caretOrdinal` and `$0.blockCount` off the live
`EditorViewModel` (`:586–587`). Both are plain `@Observable` stored properties, and `updateCaretContext`
— called from `textViewDidChangeSelection` (`EditorView.swift:618`), i.e. on EVERY keystroke — assigns
them unconditionally on every call (`:2870 caretOrdinal = nil`, `:2872 blockCount = …`, `:2884
caretOrdinal = i + 1`). Observation's registrar notifies on every assignment with no equality check
(the implementer knew this: the `editing !== self` guard two lines up, `:2861`, exists for exactly that
reason), so each keystroke invalidates **`ShellSplit`** — the view whose body registered the access —
and its body re-runs BOTH closures: `SidebarView(…)` is re-constructed with a fresh `AnyView`
(non-comparable ⇒ `SidebarView.body` re-runs: the starred rows, the areas, the Open strip), and
`paneRow` re-runs → `paneHost` → `BookView(session:readingID:…)` is re-constructed — its `init` mints
and discards a `BookViewModel` + `BookStructureModel` per pass (`BookView.swift:74–81`) — and, carrying
three closure fields (`onPaneFocusRequest`, `onRevealConsumed`, `onNoteBox`), it cannot compare equal,
so `BookView.body` re-runs: the leading `SideColumn` (closure fields ⇒ its body too), the mode's
`outlineBody`/`spread`, the navigator's `ForEach` of chapter and note rows, and `noteBoxReport`'s
entry walk (`.onChange(of: noteBoxReport)` re-computes it each pass, `:745–752`). Before 18d nothing
at keystroke rate was read inside those closures (the old side rail read `caretLabel` inside
`CommitBar`'s OWN body, one small view); the horizontal bar still does. So this diff moves a
keystroke-rate observation from the smallest view in the tree to the largest.

*What degrades.* Not corpus-scaled — the shell is the viewport, so P1's letter holds — but it is a
per-keystroke re-diff of the sidebar column and the whole book pane on the typing path of the very
surface 18d reworked, which is the "invalidation ∝ realized rows" letter of P-8 and the churn class
13u1 exists to hunt. Two view-model allocations per keystroke thrown away is the concrete cost a
profiler will show first. I am NOT claiming a visible stutter (unmeasured — the fix pass measures);
I am claiming the mechanism, which is certain.

*Pin that would prove it (RED on the tree as it stands):* a DEBUG counter on `SidebarView.body`
(`SidebarGeometry.sidebarBodyEvaluations`, the oracle pattern) and a keyed DEBUG door on `BookView`
publishing `{ model.focus($0) }` under `BookOutlineGeometry` (the `blockNamingDoor` /
`beginTitleEditing` precedent, KEYED by `readingID` per J41); the pin mounts a real `RootView`
(`NoteBoxMountTests`' rig), opens an Outline book, focuses a note through that door, settles until
`session.editorRouter.editing?.postID` is the note and `CommitBarGeometry.mounted("box", post:) == 1`,
snapshots the counter, calls `editing.updateCaretContext()` twenty times (the per-keystroke call,
without needing the rig to type), pumps, and asserts the sidebar's body ran fewer than five more times.
Red today (≥ 20); green after the fix. **Fix:** the label crosses the observation boundary as a
CLOSURE, not a value — `SidebarNoteBox.caretLabel: (() -> String?)?`, evaluated inside the box's own
`body` (`:187`), and `RootView` passes `{ BlockLineLabel.caret(ordinal: model.caretOrdinal, of:
model.blockCount) }` — so the only view that re-runs per caret move is the box (which already carries
the bar). Features receive closures (CLAUDE.md's own wording); the sidebar still holds no model.

**[MINOR-1] · `App/Variorum/Variorum/Theme/EditorTypography.swift:231` (`applyVoiceChrome`) with
`:125–130` (`fingerprint`) · J44's MINOR-1 — CONFIRMED on its mechanism.** `applyVoiceChrome` writes
`EditorTypography.current = chrome.typography` unconditionally; `fingerprint` is `current` whenever
`isAdopted`; `isAdopted` is a process-global latch set by the FIRST `ThemeStore.start` landing
(`ThemeStore.swift:44–45`). Four stores are minted, one per window kind (`RootView.swift:144`,
`Workspace/NoteWindowView.swift:55`, `Features/QuickNote/QuickNoteView.swift:118`,
`Features/Settings/AppSettingsView.swift:38`), each holding `Queries.ThemeSettings()` — `.terminal` —
until its own observation returns, and both chrome-building hosts read
`themeStore?.settings ?? Queries.ThemeSettings()` (`EditorView.swift:72–74`, `ReadPostView.swift:48`).
So in a Study session, opening a note window or the quick-note window applies a Terminal chrome under
`isAdopted == true` → `current` = Terminal → `fingerprint` = the monospace stamp → (i) `size()`
(`SurfaceSizeMemory.swift:176–180`) REFUSES her Study-stamped Outline records for as long as that
`current` stands (the first-frame picture round 1's MINOR-2 was raised about, back through a third
door), and (ii) a `remember` + settle `persist` in that window writes a Study-measured height under the
Terminal stamp over her record, which the next Study launch refuses. Round 2 closed the LATCH; the
VALUE the latch guards is still writable by a drawing host, which falsifies `adopt`'s own doc
(*"only the settings' authority adopts"*). MINOR, as the cap said: a second window inside its store's
DB-read window, view state only, self-healing at the next settle. **Pin (red on HEAD; designed by the
cap, UNMEASURED — I measure it in the fix pass):** `SurfaceSizeMemoryTests` — adopt Study
(`EditorTypography.adopt(.resolve(voice: .study, inlineComments: false))`), seed her record through a
memory wired `fingerprint: { EditorTypography.fingerprint }`, drive the production door
`EditorTextView.makeInlineEditor().applyVoiceChrome(EditorSurfaceChrome(tokens: Queries.ThemeSettings(),
dark: false))`, assert `EditorTypography.fingerprint` is unchanged (red: it becomes
`.AppleSystemUIFontMonospaced-Regular-14-7`), then replay `remember` + `persist` and assert her record
survives in memory and on disk; the globals restored before any assertion (round 2's NIT-2). **Fix:**
`applyVoiceChrome` writes `current` only while `!EditorTypography.isAdopted`; after adoption the store's
`adopt` is the only writer. Strictly better for the drawing hosts too: `EditorDocument.baseFont` reads
`EditorTypography.current` (`EditorDocument.swift:24`), so a surface materializing in a not-yet-landed
window now materializes in the ADOPTED voice rather than Terminal-then-flip. Checked: every
`EditorSurfaceChrome` is built from a `ThemeSettings` (`EditorTypography.swift:192–199`), so a landed
store's chrome carries exactly the adopted resolution — nothing a host draws changes on the normal path.

**[NIT-1] · `Core/Views/SurfaceSizeMemory.swift:211–213` (`persist`'s doc) · J44's NIT-1 — CONFIRMED.**
The guard is justified by *"`FlowStoryRow`'s empty-read branch calls `remember` and then `settledHere()`
→ `persist` in the SAME turn"* — but that road runs through the FLOW memory, whose stamp is
`FlowHeightEstimate.fingerprint` (`ReadingFlowView.swift:695`), a compile-time `static let` that is never
nil, so it cannot carry an unknown-voice write. The genuinely same-turn road for the `.outline` memory
— the one whose stamp CAN be nil — is `StableSurface.report`'s settle closure (`StableSurface.swift:208–210`:
`remember(size)` then `settled?()` → `persist`), which every Outline row uses. The guard is right
(belt-and-braces: with `remember` dropping, `records[key]` holds only the disk record, which `written`
declines to rewrite); its stated reason is wrong. **Fix:** one clause (doc; no pin).

**[NIT-2] · `Features/Library/RecoveryView.swift:477` (`!item.isVersion`) · J44's NIT-2 — CONFIRMED
as a missing reason, and the exclusion is RIGHT.** Traced: `currentBlock.<id>` is written only through
`CommandRouter.noteFocusedBlock` (`:167–183`) from caret-reporting surfaces, and `surfaceSize.*` only
by the Outline's and the flow's `StableSurface` consumers; a version's ONE home is Note ▸ Versions
(`NoteVersionsPane.swift` mounts no `ReadPostView`/`PostDetailView`/`StableSurface`/`EditorView` and
opens nothing — grepped), a version rides no book membership, and a PROMOTED version is a note whose
`isVersion` reads false at delete time and so IS evicted. Hence no per-note key can exist under a
version's id and the exclusion is exact. **Fix:** one clause at the guard saying so (doc; no pin).

**[NIT-3] · `Features/BookView/BookView.swift:745–752` (`identity(of:)`) with
`BookViewModel.swift:27` (`entryWindow = 300`) · the box's *"N of M in this book"* takes M from the
WINDOWED entries, and a note past the window has no identity line at all.** `model.entries` is the
observation's first 300 rows (`:106–107`, `truncated` held beside it); the box says "5 of 300" for a
400-note book and shows no title/place for note 301+ (`firstIndex` → nil). Beyond her library's scale
(Sherlock is 13), so NIT; `model.truncated` is at hand. **Fix:** omit the total (or say "of 300+")
when `model.truncated`; the identity for an out-of-window note is a separate read the box does not owe
today. Pin if fixed: a pure `NoteBoxCopy.whereLine` arm, or a `BookNoteBoxSubjectTests` case over a
truncated model (green on both sides for the copy half — a copy-truth pin, not a red-on-old).

**[NIT-4] · `Core/Views/NoteBoxFactsModel.swift:56–63` (`load`) · a superseded read can land its
subject over a newer one — no cancellation check after the await.** `.task(id: noteBoxFactsKey)`
cancels the previous task on a key change, but `database.read` is not cancellation-aware mid-flight,
and `load` assigns `subject = postID; facts = read` unconditionally after the await — so a selection
changed twice inside one read (a few ms) can have the OLD note's read finish last, leaving `subject` on
the old note and `facts(for: new)` nil until the next selection change. Bounded (a missing facts line,
never a wrong one — `facts(for:)`'s subject check is what keeps it honest), hand-reachable only by
two clicks inside a read. **Fix:** `guard !Task.isCancelled else { return }` before the assignments
(one line). A deterministic pin needs an injectable slow read the model does not take; labelled as the
bounded race it is rather than dressed as a bug pin.

  and installs in one statement; `open` is a one-line forward; `spendLanding` fires in the mount's

#### ROUND-END FABLE PASS round 1 — the implementers' responses (18d batch 1)

*(the 18d batch-1 implementer, resumed — the box and the shell. FOUR findings are mine: MAJOR-1 ·
MINOR-2 · NIT-3 · NIT-4. **All four AGREED, none disputed.** Every mechanism below was re-traced in
this session against `HEAD`, at the file:line the reviewer names; where my trace adds or narrows
something the reviewer's does not say, it is marked as a RIDER and is offered to the fix, not argued
against it. I touched no code and no test — the fix pass is the reviewer's.)*

**[MAJOR-1] — AGREE, and the mechanism is worse in one detail than the finding states.**

*Re-traced.* `RootView.body` hands `ShellSplit` two `@ViewBuilder` closures (`RootView.swift:143–169`);
`ShellSplit.body` CALLS both (`ShellSplit.swift:87–99` — `sidebar()` at `:89`, `detail()` at `:98`), so
everything either closure reads is registered against **`ShellSplit`'s** body evaluation, not
`RootView`'s. `noteBoxView` is evaluated inside the `sidebar:` closure (`RootView.swift:147` →
`:558–589`), and at `:586–587` it reads `$0.caretOrdinal` and `$0.blockCount` — both plain
`@Observable` stored properties on the live `EditorViewModel`. `updateCaretContext` assigns them on
EVERY call, unconditionally (`EditorViewModel.swift:2867–2884`: `caretBlockID = nil`, `caretOrdinal =
nil`, `blockCount = index.entries.count`, then `caretOrdinal = i + 1` in the loop) and is called from
`textViewDidChangeSelection` (`EditorView.swift:617–619`), which typing fires per keystroke. The
Observation registrar has no equality check — which I knew, because the `editing !== self` guard I
wrote two lines above at `:2861` exists for precisely that reason. So the reviewer's chain holds end to
end: a keystroke in an Outline note invalidates `ShellSplit`, whose body re-runs BOTH closures.

*The detail I would add (a RIDER on the severity's reasoning, not on the verdict).* The reviewer says
the pane closure re-runs and `BookView.init` mints and discards two view models per pass. Confirmed at
`BookView.swift:74–81`. What makes it certain rather than probable is the thing the reviewer only
implies: `BookView` carries three closure fields (`onPaneFocusRequest`, `onRevealConsumed`, `onNoteBox`
— `:26–40`), and function values never compare equal, so SwiftUI cannot elide the re-render even in
principle. The same is true of `SidebarView`, whose `noteBox: AnyView?` is non-comparable by
construction — I chose `AnyView` there deliberately, and this finding is its bill.

*What I do NOT claim, and neither should the fix's record.* I have not measured a stutter, and the
reviewer explicitly does not either. The honest claim is the mechanism plus its allocation cost; the
pin is what turns it into a number.

**RIDERS ON THE FIX SHAPE** (the coordinator asked for these by name):

1. **What the closure must NOT capture: `self`.** `caretLabel` becomes `(() -> String?)?` and `RootView`
   must build it from the LOCAL `barModel` — `{ BlockLineLabel.caret(ordinal: barModel.caretOrdinal,
   of: barModel.blockCount) }` — never `{ self.… }` and never through a stored property. A closure that
   reaches back through `self` re-introduces exactly the dependency being removed the moment anything
   inside it touches an observed field of `RootView`'s own state.
2. **Capture the model STRONGLY, not weakly.** `EditorViewModel` is owned by `EditorView`'s `@State`;
   a `[weak]` capture would make the where-line silently lose its *"block 3/41"* under any teardown
   race, and the box's whole purpose is that the identity line and the bar agree. The closure lives one
   render pass of the box and cannot leak the model beyond it.
3. **`EditorRouter.editing`'s observation does NOT already scope this — and the finding is right to
   name `caretOrdinal`/`blockCount` specifically.** `noteBoxView` also reads
   `session.editorRouter.editing` (`:573`), which IS observed — but I assign it only on a change
   (`EditorViewModel.swift:2861–2863`), so it fires once per editor change, not per keystroke. It
   scopes nothing here. The per-keystroke reads are the two caret properties on a different object, and
   moving those two is the whole fix.
4. **The pin must be evaluation-counted, not lifecycle-counted.** A `SidebarView.body` counter has to
   increment INSIDE the body's evaluation (the `let _ = { … }()` idiom); `.onAppear` and
   `.onGeometryChange` fire on mount and layout, not on body re-runs, and would measure the wrong
   thing — the pin would pass on the unfixed tree.
5. **The pin should also assert the label still WORKS**, or deleting the feature satisfies it. After
   the fix the box's OWN body must still re-run per caret move (that is the intent — the smallest view
   in the tree), so a second arm — move the caret to another block through the same door and assert the
   where-line's block half changed — is what stops "make the counter small" from becoming "drop the
   label". This is the one addition I would ask for in the fix's pin.
6. **`CommitBarGeometry.mounted("box", post:)` is the right settle predicate** and is already keyed by
   post (18d ladder round-1 MINOR-3), so the pin can use it as written.

**[MINOR-2] — AGREE at all three sites, and the harness-hygiene label is correct.**

*(a) `SidebarGeometry.railGroupHeight`, re-traced.* Written unkeyed by any drawn rail
(`SidebarView.swift:566–570`, inside `railGroup`), read by `NoteBoxMountTests.swift:166–180` (nil it,
wait for ANY non-nil, `#require`, then the generous-arithmetic guard at `:176–180`) and again at
`:374–388` **with no guard at all**. Reachable, not theoretical: `ShellChromeTests` mounts a `RootView`
and selects a note in both of its geometry tests, and `ShellLandingTests:297–338` mounts a second
`RootView`; either draws a rail into the same static. The guarded pin fails spuriously on a compressed
rail; the unguarded one silently takes another window's number as its reference and then compares my
keyed box against it. That the compare *usually* passes is luck (both windows are tall), which is the
worst property a pin can have. **This is my own residue** — round 1's MINOR-3 keyed the four oracles I
ADDED and left the one I only READ, and the keying is worth nothing while the reference it compares
against is shared.

*Riders on the fix:* key it by the rail's POST (`railPostID`, the value the rail already has at
`:566`) rather than by a window — both of my pins draw their rail for a post they own, so the post key
resolves both sites without a new parameter. And **keep the generous-arithmetic guard at `:176–180`**:
once the number is the pin's own, that line stops being cross-suite noise and becomes the local proof
that the rail drew at the pitch the box's frame assumes.

*(b) the pane seam's subject.* `RootView.swift:657–667` mints
`SeamGeometry.key(paneSeamFamily, subject: "\(index)")` — `paneDivider|0` for every split in every
suite and every window. `ShellChromeTests.swift:430–441` polls and `#require`s that exact key while
`ShellLandingTests.swift:338–341` opens a split in its own `RootView` (`router.openBeside(.shelf)`,
waiting for `panes.count == 2`), so the poll can exit on whichever window published first and
`abs(grip.midX - line.midX) <= 0.5` can compare two windows' rectangles. **The comment I would delete
in the same edit is the one at `RootView.swift:669–672`** — *"a window has at most one split, and the
pins mount their own window"* — which is true of windows and false of the key, and is the sentence that
would otherwise talk the next reader out of this fix.

*(c) `SeamGeometry.reset()`.* `SeamGrip` publishes through `.onGeometryChange`
(`SeamGrip.swift:87–89`, `:101–103`), which by definition fires only when the value CHANGES — so a
`reset()` from `ShellChromeTests.swift:409` or `OutlineRoomTests.swift:456` wipes a still-mounted
seam's entry in the OTHER suite and it is never republished, and that suite's `#require` times out as a
product failure. Agreed, and this is the sharpest of the three: (a) and (b) produce wrong numbers, (c)
produces a red pin with no defect behind it.

**[NIT-3] — AGREE on the total; and one PRECISION that narrows the second half of the finding.**

*Re-traced.* `identity(of:)` (`BookView.swift:745–752`) takes `total: model.entries.count`, and
`entries` is the windowed list (`BookViewModel.swift:106–107`: `truncated = new.count > 300; entries =
truncated ? Array(new.prefix(300)) : new`). So *"5 of 300"* on a 400-note book — correct, and NIT-scaled
for her library (Sherlock is 13).

*The precision (a RIDER, not a dispute).* The finding also says a note past the window *"has no
title/place at all"* because `firstIndex` returns nil. That branch is, as far as I can trace,
**unreachable through any door**: every surface that can make a note the box's subject builds its rows
from the same windowed `entries` — the navigator and Outline's rows (`model.entries`), the Index column
(`BookIndexColumn.groups(chapters: structure.grouped(entries: model.entries))` / `groups(flat:)`), and
the spread (`BookViewModel.spreadEntries`, `:255–259`, which indexes into `entries`). A note the book
has not loaded cannot be clicked, so the nil-identity path is a guard, not a symptom. The fix should
therefore be scoped to the TOTAL's honesty (`truncated` ⇒ omit it, or say `300+`), and the nil branch
left as the defensive guard it is — with that reasoning at the code, so the next reader does not
"fix" a reachable-looking hole that no door reaches.

**[NIT-4] — AGREE, and one rider on what the guard must not break.**

*Re-traced.* `NoteBoxFactsModel.load` (`:50–64`) awaits `session.database.read`, which is not
cancellation-aware mid-flight, and then assigns `subject = postID; facts = read ?? nil`
unconditionally. `.task(id: noteBoxFactsKey)` cancels the previous task on a key change, but a
superseded read that finishes last therefore claims `subject`, and `facts(for:)`'s own subject check
then answers nil for the note actually shown until the next selection change. Bounded exactly as the
finding says — a missing facts line, never a wrong one — and that subject check is deliberate
(`:36–39`) and is what keeps it honest.

*Rider on the fix.* `guard !Task.isCancelled else { return }` must sit **before both assignments**, so
a cancelled read leaves the pair entirely to the newer task — and it must NOT be conflated with the
`read == nil` case, which is a different thing and is meant to claim the subject: a note that
vanished between the ask and the read is deliberately recorded as *this* note with no facts
(`:62–63`'s comment), never left looking like a note whose facts are still coming. One line, above the
two, and the existing comment stays true.

The one addition I ask the fix to carry is MAJOR-1's rider 5 — an arm that proves the label still
updates — because a body-count pin alone is satisfied by removing the feature it is protecting.

#### ROUND-END FABLE PASS round 1 — the implementers' responses (18d batch 4)

*(the batch-4 implementer, resumed. THREE findings — MINOR-1 · NIT-1 · NIT-2. All AGREED, each
re-traced at HEAD in this session. I have touched no code and no test; the fix pass is the reviewer's.)*

**[MINOR-1] — AGREE.** Re-traced and correct in every link: `applyVoiceChrome` writes
`EditorTypography.current = chrome.typography` unconditionally (`EditorTypography.swift:231`);
`fingerprint` derives from `current` whenever `isAdopted` (`:125–130`); `isAdopted` is a process-global
latch set by whichever `ThemeStore` lands FIRST (`ThemeStore.swift:44–45`); four stores are minted, one
per window kind; both chrome hosts read `themeStore?.settings ?? Queries.ThemeSettings()`, and — the
link that makes the `??` a red herring — a real store HOLDS that same value until its own observation
returns (`ThemeStore.swift:22`). Round 2 closed the latch and left the value it guards writable by a
drawing host, which does falsify `adopt`'s own doc. My round-2 record's rule ("only the settings'
authority adopts") is true of the LATCH and false of the STAMP; that is the finding.

**Two sharpenings for the fix pass, both from greps run here — neither weakens the finding.**

1. **Of the four stores, only the NOTE WINDOW's can drive this.** `QuickNoteView` is a SwiftUI
   `TextEditor` (`QuickNoteView.swift:130`) and `AppSettingsView` mounts no text surface — neither
   reaches `applyVoiceChrome` (grepped: the only three call sites are `ReadPostView.swift:152` and
   `EditorView.swift:448, 526`). `NoteWindowView` mounts `PostDetailView` (`:90`), which is exactly
   those hosts. So the trigger is concrete and everyday: **open a note into its own window during a
   Study session**, before that window's own store's first read returns. The VICTIM is the main
   window's Outline, because `current` is a process global — the second window needs no book of its own.
2. **The finding's (i) and (ii) halves are not equally reachable, and the difference is in the settle
   closure.** (i) — `size()` refusing her Study records while that `current` stands — is reachable for
   the whole window, and is the first-frame picture round 1's MINOR-2 was raised about arriving through
   a third door. (ii) — a Study-measured height written under the Terminal stamp — is narrower than it
   looks, because `StableSurface.report`'s settle closure calls `remember(size)` **immediately before**
   `settled?()` → `persist`, so a geometry-cadence `remember` stamped Terminal earlier in the window is
   re-stamped correctly the moment the settle fires. For (ii) to bite, the settle's OWN
   remember/persist pair must fall inside the window. Real, narrow, and worth knowing when writing the
   pin: the reviewer's designed pin asserts the STAMP first, which is the reachable half and needs no
   timing at all.

**The fix shape, answering the coordinator's question directly.**

- **"Can `applyVoiceChrome` draw WITHOUT writing `current` at all — the chrome carrying its own resolved
  typography?" NO, not at this size, and the trace says why.** The body does not use `chrome.typography`
  to attribute anything: it writes `current` and then reads the document's attributes back out of it —
  `font = EditorDocument.baseFont`, `defaultParagraphStyle = EditorDocument.baseParagraphStyle`,
  `typingAttributes = EditorDocument.baseAttributes`, and the full-range `addAttributes(baseAttributes)`
  — and all three of those read `EditorTypography.current` (`EditorDocument.swift:24, 43–47, 53–56`).
  The write IS the mechanism by which a chrome reaches a document. Making the chrome carry its own
  typography means turning those three into functions of a passed-in `Resolved`, and they are the same
  three used by materialization, programmatic replaces, differential structural applies and the read
  tier (their own doc says so) — P-3 plumbing, not a MINOR's fix. **Do not attempt it in this pass.**
- **"Or must the stamp be derived from the landed settings rather than from `current`?" That is the
  better long answer, and it is one line — but it is a COMPLEMENT to the reviewer's fix, not a
  substitute.** Storing the stamp at `adopt` time (an `adoptedStamp` beside `isAdopted`, with
  `fingerprint` returning it instead of re-deriving from `current`) makes the stamp structurally immune
  to any writer of `current`, present or future — which is what "only the settings' authority adopts"
  should have meant all along, and it survives the next drawing host that forgets. **But it alone is
  insufficient:** it leaves the transient wrong-voice MATERIALIZATION untouched — a surface realized in
  the main window during the note window's read still takes `baseFont` from a Terminal `current`. The
  reviewer's own fix (`applyVoiceChrome` writes `current` only while `!isAdopted`) closes both halves,
  and I have checked its one risk: after adoption the surface draws from the ADOPTED resolution rather
  than its host's chrome, which is only ever a difference while that host is un-landed — every
  `EditorSurfaceChrome` is built from a `ThemeSettings` and there is no per-surface voice override
  (grepped), and on the voice-SWITCH path `adopt` runs before any surface re-applies, so the re-font
  still happens. **My recommendation: take the reviewer's fix as the behaviour, and add the stored
  stamp as the structural belt if it wants one line more.**
- **Rider on the pin (round 2's NIT-2, measured, not theoretical).** Whatever shape it takes, the pin
  must capture its readings and put both process globals back BEFORE it asserts, and inject stamps
  wherever the global is not itself the subject. My round-2 record has the measurement: an unbounded
  window in this same suite turned `BookOutlineLandingTests` red at `editorHeight → 24.0` (green alone,
  red beside this suite, green again once bounded). `SurfaceSizeMemoryTests` is `.serialized`, which
  does not help across suites.

**[NIT-1] — AGREE, exactly as stated.** `persist`'s guard is justified by the flow's empty-read branch
(`ReadingFlowView`'s `FlowStoryRow`: `memory.remember(...)` then `settledHere()` → `memory.persist(...)`),
and that road runs through the FLOW memory, whose stamp is `FlowHeightEstimate.fingerprint` — a
compile-time `static let String`, promoted into the closure's `String?` and therefore never nil. So the
road I cited is the one road that cannot carry an unknown-voice write. My mistake, and it is the same
class the round's own J8 copy-truth rule names. **Rider on the wording:** the genuinely same-turn road
for the `.outline` memory — the one whose stamp CAN be nil — is `StableSurface.report`'s settle closure
(`remember(size)` → `loaded = true` → `settled?()`), whose Outline consumers are `BookView`'s two
`settled: { model.persistSurfaceSize(entry.postID) }` closures; every expanded Outline row uses it. And
please keep the second sentence: the guard is belt-and-braces (with `remember` dropping, `records[key]`
holds only the record read from disk, which the `written` cache declines to re-write) — that is why it
is a NIT and not a bug, and a reader who loses that sentence will later "simplify" the guard away.

**[NIT-2] — AGREE, and I re-ran the trace rather than taking it.** `NoteVersionsPane.swift` (340 lines)
contains no `EditorView`, `PostDetailView`, `ReadPostView`, `StableSurface`, `SurfaceSizeMemory`,
`noteFocusedBlock` or `openHere` — so a version's one home mounts nothing that writes a per-note key,
and no `currentBlock.<id>` or `surfaceSize.*.<id>` can exist under a version's id. The promoted case is
the one that makes the guard non-vacuous over time, and the reviewer has it right: `promoteNoteVersion`
unarchives, so `isVersion` reads false at delete time and a promoted version IS evicted. **One rider on
the clause's wording, so it does not overclaim:** removing `!item.isVersion` would not CAUSE harm — it
would evict under an id that provably carries no keys. The guard states an INTENT (a saved moment is not
a note whose view state exists), and the honest clause says that rather than implying it prevents a
loss; otherwise the next reader treats it as load-bearing and reasons wrongly about the road around it.

**Summary: 3 agreed · 0 disputed.** Nothing here re-opens a ruling and nothing needs a QUESTIONS row.
The two things I would not want dropped from the fix pass: MINOR-1's answer that the chrome-carries-its-own-typography
shape is NOT available at this size (the trace is in `EditorDocument`, not in `applyVoiceChrome`), and
NIT-1's belt-and-braces sentence, which is the reason the guard survives its own correction.

**MINOR-3 (`WorkbenchSeam` — a FIFTH surviving copy of row 9's shape) — AGREE, and the contradicted
claim is mine.** Traced in this session, not taken: `BlocksWorkbenchView.swift:727` is
`.frame(width: 9)` inside an `.overlay` of the 1-pt line; `:738` is `NSCursor.resizeLeftRight.push()` /
`pop()` on `.onHover`; there is no `zIndex` anywhere in the file; and the host's `HStack`
(`:234–241`) is `listColumn, divider, WorkbenchInfoPanel`, so the PANEL is the divider's later sibling
